2304989.title: ICAR-IIOR to host National Consultation and Industry Interface Meet to Accelerate Commercialization of Oilseed Technologies in Hyderabad
2304989.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR-IIOR to host National Consultation and Industry Interface Meet to Accelerate Commercialization of Oilseed Technologies in Hyderabad
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:33PM by PIB Delhi

The ICAR–Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research (ICAR-IIOR), Hyderabad will organise a National Consultation and Industry Interface Meet on “Innovations in Varieties/Hybrids, Biologicals and Biopolymer-Enabled Multilayer Seed Coating Technologies for Sustainable Agriculture: Industry Partnerships for Technology Commercialization and Scaling” on 10th September 2026 at ICAR-IIOR, Hyderabad.

India is one of the world’s major vegetable oil economies, and increasing demand for edible oils, coupled with need to accelerate domestic oilseed production, necessitates accelerated technology development, commercialization and adoption to strengthen self-reliance. In this context, ICAR-IIOR has developed promising technologies, including improved oilseed varieties and hybrids, biopolymer-enabled seed enhancement technologies, and microbial biopesticide formulations.

The meet will bring together representatives from the seed industry, biopesticide and bio-input companies, technology licensees, agri-business firms, start-ups and entrepreneurs, while ICAR-IIOR will showcase its promising technologies and explore opportunities for technology transfer, licensing, public–private partnerships and large-scale deployment.

The initiative is expected to strengthen research–industry linkages and stakeholder collaboration, facilitating the validation, commercialization and adoption of innovative technologies for the benefit of farmers and the sustainable growth of India’s oilseed sector.

2304972.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) releases the 48th Report on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) for States/UTs for July, 2026
A total of 1,01,047 PG cases received for the States/UTs and 83,324 PG cases redressed in July, 2026
Under the Sevottam Scheme, in the last five Financial Years, 1,217 training courses completed, in which about 40,077 officers have been trained
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) released the Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) 48th monthly report for States/UTs for July, 2026. The said report provides a detailed analysis of types and categories of public grievances and the nature of disposal by the States/UTs.

In July, 2026, 1,01,047 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 83,324 PG cases were redressed. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in July, 2026 with 24,694 PG cases, followed by Rajasthan with 6,774 PG cases. As of 31st July, 2026, the total pendency of PG cases on the CPGRAMS portal stands at 2,33,714 across all States and UTs. Moreover, 22 States/UTs have more than 1,000 pending PG cases each.

The report provides the data for new users registered on CPGRAMS through CPGRAMS Portal during July, 2026. A total of 1,07,186 new users have registered on CPGRAMS in July, 2026, through various channels, out of which, 17,819 registrations are from Uttar Pradesh.

The said report also provides the state-wise analysis on the grievances registered through Common Service Centres in July, 2026. CPGRAMS has been integrated with the Common Service Centre (CSC) portal and is available at more than 5 lakh CSCs, associating with 2.5 lakh Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). A total of 9,475 grievances have been registered through the Common Service Centres in the month of July, 2026.

The report also provides the total number of training programmes conducted and officers trained over the last five financial years under the Sevottam Scheme. Between FY 2022–23 and FY 2026–27, a total of 1,217 training courses were conducted, training ~40,077 officers.

2304967.title: NPCI International and Uzbekistan’s NIPC Partner to Enable UPI Payments Across Uzbekistan via UZQR
2304967.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
NPCI International and Uzbekistan’s NIPC Partner to Enable UPI Payments Across Uzbekistan via UZQR
Indian tourists, business travellers and students can make instant merchant payments by scanning Uzbekistan’s national interoperable QR code, UZQR
Partnership between NIPL and Uzbekistan’s National payment system marks a significant step in expanding UPI’s international footprint
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi

NPCI International Payments Ltd. (NIPL), the international arm of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), has entered into a commercial agreement with the National Interbank Processing Centre JSC (NIPC), operator of Uzbekistan’s national payment system, HUMO, on 30th August 2026. The partnership enables Indian travellers to scan Uzbekistan’s national interoperable QR code UZQR using their familiar UPI-enabled applications to make instant merchant payments across the country.

The announcement was made during the bilateral visit of the Prime Minister of India to Uzbekistan. The execution of the agreement follows formal approvals from financial regulators, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Central Bank of Uzbekistan (CBU), which designated HUMO as NIPL’s authorised partner for cross-border merchant acceptance.

Key Highlights of the Agreement

  1. Universal Merchant Acceptance: By integrating with CBU’s mandated Unified National QR infrastructure (UZQR), UPI users gain near-universal acceptance across retail, hospitality, and service merchants in Uzbekistan.
  2. Seamless Travel Experience: Indian tourists, business travellers, and students can make direct person-to-merchant (P2M) payments from their Indian bank accounts, eliminating foreign exchange markup friction and reducing reliance on international cards or cash.
  3. Strengthened Bilateral Ties: The initiative advances digital public infrastructure cooperation and aligns with both nations' broader strategic and economic goals.

UPI is Accepted in Ten Countries

Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, and Greece, enabling Indian travellers to make seamless payments abroad through UPI.

2304963.title: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw addressed media on Semicon 2.0
2304963.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw addressed media on Semicon 2.0
Notifications for all 6 Pillars of Semicon 2.0 issued
India achieved target of developing 85,000 semiconductor engineers in four years against 10-year target: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Close to 10% of the global semiconductor industry’s market will be in India in the coming years: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Students from Tier-II and Tier-III cities have designed more than 250 semiconductor chips: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways and Information & Broadcasting, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, today addressed the media and outlined the Government’s vision for taking India’s semiconductor ecosystem to the next level. On the occasion, notifications for all six pillars of the Semicon 2.0 Scheme were issued, marking a significant step towards strengthening India’s semiconductor design and manufacturing capabilities.

The scheme builds on the momentum generated by the first Semicon India Programme and provides fiscal and infrastructure support across the semiconductor value chain from chip design, fabrication and packaging to equipment, materials, research and development, and talent development.

The scheme aims to strengthen India’s economic growth and national security by improving semiconductor supply-chain resilience and establishing technological leadership in critical sectors. It will operate through six pillars covering 10 categories.

The six pillars under Semicon 2.0 are:

• Pillar 1 -  Design

• Pillar 2 - Machines and Materials

• Pillar 3 - Setting up more Fabs

• Pillar 4 - Further strengthening the ATMP/OSAT industry

• Pillar 5 - Research and Development

• Pillar 6 - Talent Development

Pillar 1 - Design: Categories: Design of Semiconductor IPs, Chips, System-on-Chips (SoCs), and Modules for National Importance and Strategic Priorities; Design of Semiconductor IPs, Chips and SoCs for the Commercial Sector; and Deployment-Linked Incentive (DLI) for Semiconductor IPs/Chips/SoCs for deployment.

Pillar 2  - Machines and Materials: Category: Semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.

Pillar 3 - Setting up more Fabs: Categories: Silicon Semiconductor Wafer Fabs; Compound Semiconductors/Photonics/Sensors (including MEMS) Fab/Discrete Semiconductors Fab; and Display Fabs.

Pillar 4 - Further strengthening the ATMP/OSAT industry: Category: Semiconductor Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) / Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) Facility.

Pillar 5  -  Research and Development: Category: R&D for advanced semiconductor technologies.

Pillar 6  -  Talent Development: Category: Talent Development.

During the event Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said “India achieved its target of developing 85,000 semiconductor engineers over a period of 10 years in just four years, and has now set a new target of developing one lakh more engineers. In the coming years, close to 10% of the global semiconductor industry’s market is expected to be in India. Students from Tier-II and Tier-III cities have already designed more than 250 chips. In one case, commercial production commenced within just 13 months of the groundbreaking, while approvals were granted within 200 days, 150 days and even 90 days in multiple cases. The semiconductor ecosystem being developed in India is also expected to create 50,000–60,000 direct jobs.”

Projects supported under Semicon 2.0 will generally have a duration of up to six years, while the scheme will initially remain open for applications for three years.

The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) will be the nodal agency for Semicon 2.0. It will invite applications, undertake technical and financial appraisal, recommend applicants and oversee implementation. ISM may implement the design and deployment categories with the assistance of C-DAC. The mission may also announce semiconductor deep-tech awards from 2026 to promote niche innovation.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology will make budgetary provisions for fiscal support, with disbursements undertaken by the nodal agency in accordance with approved conditions. A mid-term assessment will be conducted after three years of implementation, or as required, to evaluate the scheme’s impact and consider modifications or continuation.

For the notification, you can visit  Semicon 2.0

2304767.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal reviews Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban progress in Chandigarh; Directs Fast-track Project Implementation & Strengthening of Swachhata
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, chaired a review meeting on the progress of the Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U) in Chandigarh, held at the UT Guest House.

The meeting was also attended by Home Secretary-cum-Secretary, Local Government, UT Chandigarh, Sh. Mandip Singh Brar, IAS; Commissioner, Municipal Corporation Chandigarh, Sh. Amit Kumar, IAS; Deputy Commissioner, Chandigarh, Sh. Nishant Yadav, IAS; Special Commissioner, MCC, Sh. Harpreet Singh Sudan, IAS, besides senior officers of the Chandigarh Administration and Municipal Corporation, along with senior government officials from MoHUA, Director, SBM-U, Ms. Surabhi Malik and Advisor, CPHEEO, Ankit Jain, State government officials from Urban development department.

During the review, the Hon’ble Minister underscored the need to fast‑track Aspirational Toilet construction while ensuring that all existing facilities (CT/PTs) are regularly monitored, maintained, and kept fully functional and accessible to the public at all times.

He also reviewed preparations for the upcoming 15-day Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, directing that the Swachhata Pakhwada must actively engage citizens in every initiative during the 15‑day campaign. He emphasized that citizens are the true custodians of Swachhata, and their feedback must not only be heard but acted upon with utmost seriousness.The Hon'ble Minister highlighted that all processing facilities, waste collection vehicles, and government offices must be cleaned — just as homes are readied before Diwali — so that every element associated with swachhata reflects renewed commitment.

He further advocated cross‑learning among Urban Local Bodies, pointing to best practices from Integrated Command and Control Centres where AI and digital tools are used to track vehicles, capture real‑time data and derive smart solutions.

The Union Minister directed that a structured city‑to‑city learning mechanism be institutionalized, enabling knowledge sharing of processes, facilities, and innovations. The cities showcasing these best practices should be made accessible to the others for streamlining processes in various cities.

Satisfied with Chandigarh’s progress under SBM‑U 2.0, the Hon’ble Minister reiterated that beyond achieving swachhata, the greater responsibility lies in sustaining and continuously improving it.

2304759.title: National Biodiversity Authority disburses Rs. 5.68 Crore in Access and Benefit-Sharing Funds for Biodiversity Conservation
2304759.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2304759.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Biodiversity Authority disburses Rs. 5.68 Crore in Access and Benefit-Sharing Funds for Biodiversity Conservation
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 5.68 crore under the Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism arising from the utilisation of biological resources. The funds have been channelled to State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) and a national research institution, primarily in relation to Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), Cucumber (Cucumis sativus) and Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), besides specified microbial and agricultural biological resources.

The largest ABS component relates to Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), covering 139 varieties and 28 hybrids, for which the NBA has released Rs. 3.51 crore to 32 State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils. The ABS amount was received from M/s. Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd. in connection with its access to Okra.

The other major ABS components relate to Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), covering 662 varieties and 15 hybrids and Cucumber (Cucumis sativus), covering 1009 varieties and 14 hybrids. These biological resources were accessed through markets/traders by M/s. Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd., M/s. East West Seeds India Pvt. Ltd. and M/s. Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd.

In these cases, the biological resources were accessed from markets and traders, making it not feasible to trace them to specific individual farmers, communities or a single identifiable geographic source. Accordingly, the modality recommended by the Expert Committee and approved by the Authority provides for distribution of the beneficiary share among the States and Union Territories where the concerned biological resource is cultivated.

In addition, the NBA has disbursed benefit-sharing funds to CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory (NCL) – National Culture of Industrial Microorganisms, Pune, from an ABS amount received from M/s. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd., Mumbai.

The funds disbursed to the SBBs and UTBCs are to be utilised as per Section 32 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, for activities supporting the objectives of the Act. These include documentation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers; conservation and sustainable use of biological resources; restoration of degraded ecosystems; protection of wild relatives of cultivated plants; strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites; development and maintenance of biodiversity databases; capacity building; research; and community-oriented livelihood enhancement activities.

The funds disbursed to the research institution are to support activities including maintenance of repositories of biological resources, research and bio-survey activities, capacity building in taxonomy and conservation, and in-situ and ex-situ conservation.

With this disbursement, the total ABS amount disbursed by the NBA so far has crossed Rs. 191 crore. The disbursements reaffirm the NBA's commitment to ensuring that benefits arising from the utilisation of India's biological resources are directed towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, strengthening of institutional capacities and activities benefiting communities and other stakeholders associated with the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity.

Prime Minister lays wreath at Shastri Memorial and visits Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister today paid floral tributes at the Shastri Memorial in Tashkent. This year marks the 60th anniversary of the passing away of the former Prime Minister in Tashkent in 1965. The memorial is situated on a street named after Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. The life and legacy of the former Prime Minister is fondly remembered in Tashkent. After offering respects at the Shastri Memorial, Prime Minister visited the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies. The university has an impressive record of teaching Hindi language and other Indian subjects. During his State Visit, Prime Minister announced Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language for Uzbek students. This year marks the 80th year of Hindi teaching at the university. Given the close cultural affinities between the two countries, there is admirable interest among the Uzbek students to learn Hindi. There are over 3000 words which are common between Uzbek and Hindi languages.

2304742.title: 4th Tri-Services Future Warfare Course concludes in New Delhi
2304742.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
4th Tri-Services Future Warfare Course concludes in New Delhi
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The fourth edition of Tri-Services Future Warfare Course, conducted under the aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and coordinated by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS), concluded on August 30, 2026 after four weeks of professional military education and deliberations at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi. The course brought together officers from the Army, Navy and Air Force, along with representatives from government organisations, academia, industry and strategic think tanks to examine emerging trends shaping the future character of warfare.

The curriculum covered geopolitical developments, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, cyber and cognitive warfare, information warfare, autonomous systems, future operations across land, maritime, air and space domains, grey-zone operations, multi-domain operations and technology-enabled warfare. The participants engaged with senior military officers, policymakers, scientists, industry leaders and subject matter experts through lectures, brainstorming sessions, scenario-building exercises, cognitive warfare simulations, field visits and participant-led presentations.

Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani interacted with the participants, seeking their views on the course and encouraging suggestions on emerging areas and additional subjects that could be incorporated in future editions to further strengthen the relevance of the programme. The course also dwelt on out-of-the-box ideas for enhancing the operational and functional efficiency of the services in an integrated ecosystem.

The valedictory programme included the presentation of certificates to the participants by the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) Air Marshal Tejinder Singh. Lt Gen SS Mahal (Retd), Managing Director Defence Research and Innovation Foundation, IIT Ropar presented 'PG Diploma in Future Warfare' to the attendees.

The fourth edition further reinforced the importance of joint learning, technological awareness, strategic foresight and operational preparedness in preparing military leaders for the evolving character of warfare. The fifth edition of the course is scheduled from November 16 till December 11, 2026.

2304737.title: MSDE in collaboration with Government of Uttar Pradesh organises PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow
2304737.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2304737.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MSDE in collaboration with Government of Uttar Pradesh organises PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow
From Demographic Dividend to Productive Dividend: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Calls on Defence Industry to Partner with PM-SETU for a Viksit Bharat
Industries must go beyond CSR and take ownership of ITIs; PM-SETU is designed to bridge the gap between skilling and employment: Jayant Chaudhary, MoS (I/C), MSDE
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Uttar Pradesh, today organized the PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow, bringing together senior representatives from government, industry, multilateral institutions, defence public sector enterprises, sector skill councils and skilling stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening industry participation in vocational education and transforming Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) into world-class centres of excellence.

The conclave was graced by of Minister of Defence Shri Rajnath Singh, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Deputy Chief Minister, Uttar Pradesh, Shri Brajesh Pathak and Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Kapil Dev Agarwal. Senior officials from the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Defence, Government of Uttar Pradesh and industry leaders participated in the discussions.

The event witnessed participation from senior leadership of leading defence and manufacturing organizations including Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), BrahMos Aerospace, Troop Comforts Limited (TCL), Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited (AWEIL), Gliders India Limited (GIL), Ashok Leyland, NSDC, TCIL, PTC, along with representatives from the World Bank, industry associations and other strategic stakeholders.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasized that India's journey towards becoming a global manufacturing and technology powerhouse would be driven by the availability of highly skilled manpower. He highlighted that sectors such as defence manufacturing, aerospace, electronics, drones, robotics, precision engineering and automation are witnessing rapid technological advancements and require a workforce equipped with future-ready skills. He underscored that a strong domestic defence industrial base and a strong skilling ecosystem must grow together to support India's aspirations for self-reliance and technological leadership.

The Defence Minister highlighted Uttar Pradesh's emergence as a major hub for manufacturing and defence production, driven by the rapid growth of its industrial ecosystem and the Defence Corridor. Emphasizing the importance of stronger industry-academia linkages, he noted that collaboration between industry and training institutions is crucial to equip youth with future-ready skills and expressed confidence that such partnerships would steer the state in the right direction. He further remarked that under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh is witnessing transformative development across multiple sectors.

Stressing that the availability of a skilled workforce is fundamental to nation-building, he reiterated Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of converting India's demographic dividend into a productive dividend. He underscored the need to align the skilling ecosystem with industry requirements, stating that skill certificates hold value only when they lead to meaningful employment. Calling upon industries to view PM-SETU as a collaborative mission rather than merely a government scheme, he urged them to actively participate in shaping the workforce that will ultimately serve their own growth and competitiveness.

He appealed to Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) and other defence-related organizations to actively partner in the PM-SETU initiative, while also stressing the need to transform ITIs and strengthen apprenticeship opportunities. Concluding, he stated that the success of PM-SETU should be measured not by the number of machines installed, but by the employment opportunities it creates and the lives it positively impacts.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jayant Chaudhary said that PM-SETU represents a new partnership model between government, industry and training institutions. He emphasized that the initiative is designed to bridge the gap between training and employment by enabling industries to play an active role in the development, governance and operation of ITI clusters. He highlighted that the programme aims to create a future-ready workforce through industry-aligned training, modern infrastructure, apprenticeship opportunities and pathways for entrepreneurship.

Underscoring the strategic importance of the defence sector in achieving global competitiveness, he highlighted that the industry's reliance on technology and innovation makes this scheme both timely and relevant. He called upon industries to go beyond CSR initiatives and take active ownership of ITIs to strengthen the skilling landscape.

Deputy Chief Minister Shri Brajesh Pathak assured full support to participating industries and emphasized the government's continued focus on strengthening the skilling ecosystem as a key driver towards realizing the vision of a Viksit Bharat.

Shri Kapil Dev Agrawal, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of Uttar Pradesh, said that Uttar Pradesh is committed to strengthening its skilling ecosystem to meet the needs of a rapidly expanding industrial and manufacturing base. Referring to the state's extensive network of government ITIs and the identification of eight PM-SETU clusters in Uttar Pradesh, he noted that the initiative provides a unique opportunity to align vocational training with industry requirements and emerging technologies.

Welcoming the participants, Shri Dilip Kumar, Director General -Training, highlighted the transformational potential of PM-SETU in creating a deeper and more structured engagement between industry and the skilling ecosystem. He noted that the initiative empowers Anchor Industry Partners (AIPs) to actively contribute to the growth and modernization of ITI clusters, ensuring direct alignment between institutional outcomes and industry requirements.

Dr. Hari Om, Principal Secretary, Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the significant opportunities the state offers for strengthening the skilling ecosystem and called upon industry leaders to play an active role in supporting these efforts. Smt. Manasi Sahay Thakur, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), presented an insightful overview of PM-SETU, helping the audience gain a deeper understanding of the program and its vision.

Addressing the audience, Shri Vijay Karan Anand, Chief Executive Officer, Invest UP, underscored the far-reaching benefits of the scheme and called upon officials and stakeholders to proactively participate in its rollout. He emphasized the importance of strong partnerships in realizing the scheme's vision and maximizing its impact across the state.

Representatives from defence public sector undertakings and strategic industries highlighted the growing demand for skilled technicians in areas such as aerospace systems, shipbuilding, electronics manufacturing, precision engineering, defence production, advanced welding, mechatronics and drone technologies. Industry participants reiterated their commitment to partnering with government to create sustainable talent pipelines through industry-led skilling models.

Under the PM-SETU Scheme, cluster projects comprising one Hub ITI and four Spoke ITIs can attract investments of up to ₹241 crore, supported through a funding pattern of 50% from the Government of India, 33% from State Governments and 17% from Industry Partners. Unlike traditional partnership models, the proposed Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) structure provides 51% ownership to Anchor Industry Partners, while the Centre and State Governments hold 24.5% ownership each, ensuring meaningful industry leadership in cluster development and operations. In UP so far, 32 ITIs in 8 Clusters have already been identified out of which seven are still open for collaboration.

The conclave was informed that approved Industry Partnership proposals under PM-SETU currently represent more than ₹1,500 crore of committed industry-led investment across seven clusters in five states, with several additional proposals under consideration.

During the event, NSDC and the Lucknow Cantonment Board signed an MoU to establish Shaurya Academy, a first-of-its-kind initiative aimed at preparing youth for careers in the Armed Forces, Police, and other uniformed services.

2304718.title: Joint Statement during the State Visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Uzbekistan
2304718.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Joint Statement during the State Visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Uzbekistan
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi

At the invitation of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, His Excellency Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the Prime Minister of the Republic of India, His Excellency Mr. Narendra Modi, paid a State Visit to the Republic of Uzbekistan from 29 to 30 August 2026.

President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks in a warm, friendly and constructive atmosphere. The Leaders conducted a comprehensive review of the current state and future prospects of the Uzbekistan-India bilateral relations, exchanged views on regional and international issues of mutual interest, and identified priority areas for further practical cooperation.

The Leaders expressed satisfaction with the strong level of collaboration between the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Republic of India. They noted that the relationship is firmly anchored in longstanding bonds of friendship, as well as deep historical and cultural affinities between the two nations. Reaffirming their shared resolve, the Leaders underscored their commitment to further deepening bilateral ties and elevating cooperation to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership that advances the core interests of both nations.

The Leaders welcomed the close alignment of their positions and the growing importance of Central Asia. Amid a complex geopolitical situation, they stressed the need for a free, open and rules-based international order. Building on their multilateral cooperation, Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and bilateral agreements, they reaffirmed their commitment to long-term, mutually beneficial cooperation for both peoples and future generations, agreeing to deepen political dialogue and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership across trade, economy and investment, transport connectivity, digital transformation (IT, AI, space, cybersecurity), energy transition, critical minerals, food security, healthcare, pharmaceuticals and education.

Political, Parliamentary and Security Cooperation

The Leaders underscored the importance of maintaining regular and trust-based dialogue at leadership and institutional levels and agreed to continue the exchange of visits and contacts in both the bilateral format and on the margins of international events.

The Leaders agreed to establish Foreign Ministers led mechanism to provide high level coordination and oversight of the implementation of the agreements and arrangements reached between the two countries, as well as to facilitate the timely realisation of priority bilateral initiatives and projects.

The Leaders acknowledged the growing role of parliamentary diplomacy and welcomed the intensification of contacts between the chambers of the Oliy Majlis of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Parliament of the Republic of India, including cooperation between parliamentary friendship groups and interaction within international inter-parliamentary organizations.

The Leaders underscored the importance of further strengthening the legal framework of bilateral cooperation across various fields. They emphasized the need for a comprehensive review of the existing bilateral legal instruments to ensure that they fully reflect the current priorities of bilateral engagement and agreed to work jointly on modernizing the treaty framework in line with present-day realities.

The Leaders unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, reiterated zero tolerance approach to terrorism and rejected justification of terrorism on any ground whatsoever. Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and for disrupting terrorism financing networks, safe havens and infrastructure. Leaders stressed that those responsible for terrorism should be held accountable and their perpetrators, their backers, facilitators and affiliates should be brought to justice. The Leaders stressed the importance of strengthening cooperation in law enforcement, intelligence-sharing, and combating violent extremism, and illicit drug trafficking, organized crime, and cyber threats. The Leaders reaffirmed the importance of continued cooperation under the Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism.

The Leaders appreciated the growing cooperation and close coordination between the defence and security agencies of Uzbekistan and India, including through regular exchanges, institutional mechanisms, capacity-building and joint activities, and expressed their commitment to further strengthen such cooperation in addressing shared security challenges. The Leaders expressed satisfaction with the activities of the Joint Working Group on Military Cooperation, wherein new avenues of cooperation in the defence industrial domain are being explored. They welcomed the successful conduct of Uzbekistan – India Joint Military Exercise “Dustlik”, the latest of which was held in Namangan Region, Uzbekistan, in April 2026.

The Leaders highly appreciated the progress achieved in regional cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening engagement within Central Asia – India format at the level of Heads of States and other levels. The Leaders also underscored the importance of continuing regular consultations on regional issues.

Trade, Economic and Investment Cooperation

The Leaders welcomed the strong economic partnership between Uzbekistan and India and noted the considerable untapped potential for further expanding bilateral trade and investment.

The Leaders agreed on the importance of enhancing and diversifying bilateral trade by identifying and harnessing new opportunities. They underscored that the rapidly growing number of Indian companies operating in Uzbekistan reflect the significant potential for further expanding economic cooperation.

Both sides agreed to undertake joint measures to broaden the range of goods traded between the two countries, remove non tariff barriers, and promote industrial cooperation with a view to further increasing bilateral trade turnover. They decided to create a Joint Working Group to address non tariff issues and investment barriers, with a particular focus on key sectors of bilateral trade.

Both sides expressed their interest in strengthening cooperation in the fields of e-commerce, the digitalization of trade procedures, and the introduction of digital platforms to support small and medium-sized enterprises and facilitate bilateral trade.

The Uzbek side appreciated the support of the Indian side on accession of the Republic of Uzbekistan at WTO. Both sides agreed to work together to preserve and protect the multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core, especially for the interests of the developing countries.

Both sides agreed to support efforts aimed at strengthening manufacturing and export capacities, to promote dialogue among regulators and explore mutual recognition arrangements to facilitate faster and greater market access in each others’ markets.

The Leaders highly appreciated the outcomes of the meeting of the Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation and the Uzbekistan – India Business Forums, held in June 2026 on the sidelines of the Tashkent International Investment Forum and in August 2026 in New Delhi, noting their significant contribution to the further expansion of trade, economic and investment cooperation between the two countries.

The Leaders agreed to promote collaboration between the Uzbek and the Indian companies, leverage the complementarities between the two economies and strengthen connectivity between their value-added supply chains..

Both sides acknowledged the great potential of bilateral trade in Electrical items, Engineering products, Automobiles and Pharma sectors and agreed to closer business-to-business tie up in these sectors.

The Leaders agreed to identify and promote mutually beneficial investment opportunities and establish an institutional mechanism to address investors' concerns and facilitate ease of doing business.

Both sides agreed to explore enhanced cooperation between the Investment Promotion Agency of Uzbekistan and Invest India to identify and promote mutually beneficial investment opportunities, including through joint business forums, roadshows, investment seminars and stakeholder’s interaction, with a view to facilitating greater two way investment flows and strengthening business-to-business linkages.

The two Leaders expressed satisfaction at the steady growth of bilateral trade and reaffirmed their resolve to further expand and diversify trade, with the aim of building a stronger trade relationship. Recalling the conclusion of the Joint Feasibility Study on Uzbekistan-India Preferential Trade Agreement, the Leaders directed the relevant Ministries to explore the next steps on a time bound basis.

Energy, Natural Resources and Supply Chains

The Leaders welcomed the discussions on advancing cooperation in the fields of renewable energy, modernization of energy infrastructure, and the implementation of prospective investment projects.

The Leaders agreed to explore for cooperation in the fields of geology, mining, nuclear energy, industrial cooperation, and critical & strategic minerals, including projects for the processing of mineral resources, production of value- added products and recycling initiatives. They also expressed interest in encouraging Indian companies to participate in the development of prospective mineral deposits in Uzbekistan and Uzbek enterprises for joint collaboration in India. The Leaders expressed interest in extended cooperation in peaceful uses of nuclear energy.

The Leaders agreed to expand cooperation in the field of critical minerals through the implementation of joint projects in geological exploration, mining, mineral processing, and the development of integrated value chains.

Agriculture

The Leaders agreed to cooperate in the development of agricultural value chains, strengthening export capabilities, and enhancing the technical capacity of agriculture and livestock sectors.

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in agriculture and food security, with a particular focus on innovation and resource-efficient technologies. They also agreed to continue exchanges in the field of agricultural science and to make effective use of multilateral and regional platforms to promote the development of modern and sustainable agriculture across the region. The Leaders agreed to facilitate bilateral trade in agricultural products.

The Leaders supported the expansion of cooperation between research institutions and enterprises in enhancing agricultural productivity, as well as in the conservation and sustainable utilization of plant genetic resources.

Transport, Logistics and Connectivity

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to continuing joint efforts to enhance transport and logistics connectivity between Uzbekistan and India through the development of multimodal transport routes and logistics corridors, creating favourable conditions for the seamless movement of goods.

The Leaders reaffirmed their intention to continue cooperation aimed at restoring freight transportation in order to reduce transportation costs.

The Leaders expressed their intention to expand cooperation between the relevant authorities through the exchange of expertise in road construction using advanced technologies and to explore opportunities for implementing joint projects on the reconstruction and modernization of road infrastructure.

The Leaders recognized the importance of developing environmentally friendly and energy-efficient solutions for Uzbekistan’s public transport sector and agreed to explore opportunities for implementing joint projects in this field.

Digital Technologies, Innovation and Space Cooperation

The Leaders welcomed the successful operation of the first IT Park in Tashkent, established in 2019 based on the Indian model with the active support of the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), and agreed to further expand partnerships among technology parks, companies, startups, and educational institutions of the two countries.

The Leaders welcomed the strengthening of bilateral cooperation in the fields of high technologies and digital transformation, as well as the implementation of the understandings reached in February 2026 on the margins of the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi.

The Leaders agreed to strengthen cooperation in the development and advancement of safe, secure, and trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) systems, including through the exchange of experience and best practices, with a view to harnessing AI’s potential to promote sustainable economic growth, innovation-driven development, and the effective resolution of societal challenges.

The Leaders reaffirmed their interest in further expanding practical cooperation in the exploration and peaceful uses of outer space, including in space applications, the exchange of scientific data, and capacity-building through joint workshops and training.

Education, Human Resource Development, Healthcare, Culture, Sports and Tourism

The Leaders recognised the valuable contribution of Indian students to strengthening the longstanding people-to-people ties between Uzbekistan and India.

The Leaders welcomed the continued expansion of India studies in Uzbekistan and supported the expansion of Uzbek studies in India.

The Leaders shared the view of strengthening cooperation in human resource development, which serves as an important bridge between Uzbekistan and India, including through the implementation of joint research programmes and academic cooperation initiatives.

The Leaders appreciated the longstanding and mutually beneficial partnership in capacity building and human resource development, particularly in the fields of medicine, pharmaceuticals, chemistry, nanotechnology and biotechnology. Over the years, more than 2,700 Uzbek nationals have participated in the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme, while more than 400 Uzbek students have been selected under ICCR scholarships, including scholarships under AYUSH. In this context, Uzbek side welcomed the announcement of Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi Language in Uzbekistan. The Leaders reaffirmed their readiness to further promote cooperation in human resource development under the ITEC Programme.

Uzbekistan and India share the aspiration of leaving a greener and healthier planet for future generations, as reflected in Uzbekistan’s “Yashil Makon” and India’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiatives. Building on this shared commitment, India and Uzbekistan will cooperate in the greening and ecological rehabilitation of the Aral Sea region. These rehabilitation efforts of US $1 million, including the provision of necessary technical support, will be undertaken under India’s Grant-in-Aid framework.

The Leaders agreed to expand cooperation in strengthening public health systems, including in the fields of biomedical research and medical innovation, by leveraging each other’s strengths to develop new treatments and therapies through advanced scientific research.

The Leaders highly appreciated the growing cooperation in the pharmaceutical sector and underscored the significant potential of the Tashkent Pharma Park Innovative Scientific and Industrial Pharmaceutical Cluster as an effective platform for implementing joint projects, attracting investment in modern pharmaceutical manufacturing, localizing production, facilitating technology transfer, and developing a highly skilled workforce. The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to promoting closer cooperation between the relevant institutions and pharmaceutical companies of the two countries.

The Leaders expressed their support for the establishment in Uzbekistan, in cooperation with Indian companies, of new medical centres and laboratories, as well as research institutions and joint pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprises.

Recognizing the centuries-old historical ties, shared cultural and civilizational heritage, and longstanding traditions of mutual respect between the peoples of Uzbekistan and India, the Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further expanding cultural and humanitarian cooperation through the organization of cultural days, festivals, exhibitions, tours by artistic ensembles, and by strengthening direct links between the cultural institutions of the two countries. Both Leaders welcomed the signing of the Cultural Exchange Program from 2026-2030 and the Uzbekistan-India cooperation in the Field of Archives.

The Leaders underscored the importance of cooperation in the preservation, study, restoration and promotion of World Heritage sites and expressed their interest in expanding collaboration among relevant research institutions, museums and restoration centres, including in the digitalization of cultural heritage sites, the creation of three-dimensional (3D) models of archaeological artefacts, and the application of advanced technologies for their conservation. In this regard, both Leaders appreciated the Letter of Intent signed on the conservation and restoration of ancient Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Karatepa.

The Leaders agreed to strengthen cooperation in the field of sports, including through the exchange of experience in athlete preparation and coach training in such disciplines as badminton, archery and chess.

The Leaders noted with satisfaction the role of yoga in promoting healthy lifestyles and strengthening people-to-people ties, and emphasised the significance of the International Day of Yoga on 21 June. The Leaders welcomed cooperation between the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan and India's Ministry of AYUSH on instructor training and also Uzbekistan's participation in international Yogasana competitions. The Leaders reaffirmed their readiness to continue supporting the promotion and development of yoga in Uzbekistan with the participation of leading Indian experts. The Leaders also welcomed the conclusion of the MoU for cooperation in traditional medicines.

International Cooperation

Both Leaders reaffirmed that the United Nations must play a central role in maintaining global peace and security. They agreed to strengthen their cooperation, including through mutual support, in the United Nations and other international and regional organizations.

Both Leaders called for comprehensive reform of the UN, including Security Council, to reflect contemporary global realities and to make it more representative, effective and efficient in dealing with issues of international peace and security. Uzbekistan reaffirmed its support to India’s candidature for permanent membership of the UN Security Council.

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening coordination in international fora with a view to advancing the common interests of the countries of the Global South.

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), recognizing it as an important platform for enhancing mutual trust, promoting regional peace, security and stability, and expanding cooperation in trade and economic affairs, investment, and cultural and humanitarian exchanges.

President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi on India’s Chairship of BRICS in 2026 and wished him every success in hosting the BRICS Summit.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed confidence in Uzbekistan’s successful Chairship of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) for the period 2027-2030 and reaffirmed India’s readiness to continue supporting the Movement as its founding member.

Both Leaders noted the important role of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) and the International Solar Alliance (ISA), as platforms for advancing global cooperation in their respective fields. The Indian side welcomed Uzbek side’s interest in joining these frameworks and conveyed its readiness to actively pursue the necessary consultations and processes towards their accession.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his sincere gratitude to the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev, as well as to the Government and the people of Uzbekistan, for the warm welcome and gracious hospitality extended to him during the visit.

Prime Minister of India invited the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan to pay a return visit to India. The dates will be decided through diplomatic channels.

2304717.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Conferred with “Oliy Darajali Do’stlik” Order, Uzbekistan’s highest honour for foreign leaders
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi was today conferred with the “Oliy Darajali Do’stlik” Order (Order of Highest Friendship) by the President of Uzbekistan, H.E. Shavkat Mirziyoyev for his contribution to the strengthening of friendship between the two countries. This is Uzbekistan’s highest honour for foreign leaders.

Accepting the honour, Prime Minister Modi dedicated the accolade to the 1.4 billion people of India and conveyed that it is a symbol of the enduring friendship between the two countries and civilisations. He noted that the words of appreciation spoken for him by President Mirziyoyev was a tribute to the age-old friendship between India and Uzbekistan and their shared heritage. Prime Minister further added that the honour brings added responsibility for India to work together with Uzbekistan as Global South partners for the betterment of humanity.

The conferment of the “Oliy Darajali Do’stlik” Order reflects the deep-rooted civilisational ties and the steadily deepening India-Uzbekistan Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

2304715.title: Prime Minister holds official talks on his State Visit to Uzbekistan
2304715.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister holds official talks on his State Visit to Uzbekistan
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

As part of his State Visit to Uzbekistan, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today held official talks with the President of Uzbekistan, H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev. On arrival at the Kuksaroy Presidential Palace, Prime Minister was warmly received by President Mirziyoyev and accorded a ceremonial welcome. He conveyed his warmest wishes to Uzbekistan on the occasion of their 35th anniversary of Independence.

The two leaders held wide-ranging and substantive discussions in delegation level format on the entire gamut of the bilateral strategic partnership, including trade and investment, innovation and start-up, digital public infrastructure and UPI, defence and security, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, critical minerals, agriculture, education, tourism, agriculture, space and people-to-people exchanges. Prime Minister appreciated the progress made in the long-term arrangement for supply of Uranium from Uzbekistan to India and reaffirmed the importance of strengthening cooperation in critical minerals. Reflecting the depth and salience of the relationship, they decided to elevate the bilateral Strategic Partnership to the level of Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. They also agreed to set a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion by 2030 and in this regard called for hosting a Business Summit to deepen economic and investment ties. To take forward the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in a meaningful manner, the two leaders agreed to set up a Foreign Ministers led mechanism and raise the Inter-Governmental Commission to the ministerial level.

The leaders noted that ancient civilizational linkages and contemporary people-to-people ties continue to add vitality to the partnership. In this regard, Prime Minister appreciated the popularity of Yoga in Uzbekistan. Earlier in the day, he viewed a Yoga Session organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan. To commemorate the 60th anniversary of the passing of former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, Prime Minister Modi announced the Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language for Uzbek students . Recognising the convergence between Uzbekistan’s “Yashil Makon” green initiative and India’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative, Prime Minister Modi announced India’s partnership with Uzbekistan in the ongoing environmental rehabilitation efforts in the Aral Sea region with a grant of USD 1 million for the project. The two leaders also jointly planted a tree in the Palace garden.

Following the talks, the two sides witnessed the exchange of MoUs and agreements covering a wide range of areas, including culture, higher education and research, capacity building, archives, economic collaboration, environment, tourism, mining, ayurveda and sister-state relations. A Letter of Intent for the restoration of the Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Kara Tepa in Uzbekistan was concluded. An MoU for the establishment of an ICCR Sanskrit Chair at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies was also finalised. The full list of MoUs and agreements can be accessed here.

President Mirziyoyev hosted a banquet lunch in honour of Prime Minister. Prime Minister thanked President Mirziyoyev for his gracious hospitality and invited him to visit India.

2304701.title: English Translation of Prime Minister’s Press Statement during the Joint Press Statement with the President of Uzbekistan
2304701.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
English Translation of Prime Minister’s Press Statement during the Joint Press Statement with the President of Uzbekistan
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

Your Excellency, My Friend, Mister President,
Delegates from both countries,
Friends from the media,
Namaskar !

I sincerely thank the President and the people of Uzbekistan for the warm and affectionate welcome extended to me and my delegation in Tashkent.

This is my fourth visit to Uzbekistan. It reflects the closeness of our relations, our close coordination, and our deep friendship.

For nearly a decade, I have had the privilege of working with the President. During this period, I have had the opportunity to meet him more than ten times.

His positive and forward-looking approach, along with his spirit of continuous learning, is truly inspiring. I sincerely commend him for his deep friendship towards India and his unwavering commitment to our relationship.

Friends,

Uzbekistan is at the heart of Central Asia, and at the heart of India’s engagement with the region. India and Uzbekistan share a deep convergence of perspectives and aspirations. At the heart of both “Yangi Uzbekistan” and “Viksit Bharat 2047” are our youth, innovation, inclusive growth, and modern technology. Guided by this shared vision, we are working for the well-being and prosperity of the people of both countries.

This year marks the 15th anniversary of our Strategic Partnership. On this special occasion, we have decided to elevate our relationship to the level of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

Today, we have charted an ambitious agenda to take our partnership forward in this new framework with greater momentum and concrete outcomes.

Our bilateral trade has crossed one billion dollars. We have now set a target of five billion dollars in bilateral trade by 2030. To achieve this, we will systematically address issues related to market access, connectivity, banking, and payment systems.

We will work together to enhance win-win cooperation in infrastructure development. Cooperation in Digital Public Infrastructure, Artificial Intelligence, critical minerals, clean energy, space, and nuclear energy is making our relationship future-ready.

Friends,

Our strengths in agriculture and healthcare are complementary to each other. By combining Uzbekistan’s expertise in horticulture with India’s modern agricultural practices, we will contribute to the food security of both countries.

Uzbekistan’s medicinal herbs and India’s expertise in Ayurveda are also a natural combination. The agreement reached today on Traditional Medicine will give further impetus to our joint efforts in this area.

Our endeavour is to ensure that our partnership is not confined to our two capitals. Therefore, we are working towards establishing partnerships between our cities and states. These partnerships will help foster sustained direct linkages in areas such as urban management, industry, education, tourism, and culture.

The close defence and security cooperation between our two countries reflects the deep mutual trust that underpins our relationship. Going forward, we will promote direct linkages, co-production, and co-development between the defence industries of our two countries.

We believe that terrorism, extremism, and separatism pose serious challenges to the entire region.

Our shared resolve to adopt a policy of zero tolerance towards them has been, and will continue to be, unwavering.

Friends,

The deepest roots of our relationship lie in our shared heritage. Today, we placed special emphasis on further strengthening these bonds.

We will work together for the preservation of Uzbekistan’s Buddhist heritage sites. Promoting exchanges between the youth of our two countries, particularly students and professionals, is a high priority for us. Today, we agreed on a Programme of Cooperation to promote tourism between the two countries. I am pleased that today we are going to announce scholarships to promote the Hindi language in Uzbekistan.

Sports is also emerging as an important dimension of our cooperation. Last year, the 20-year-old Uzbek Grandmaster Sindarov won the FIDE World Cup in Goa. He is now set to face India’s 20-year-old chess champion, Gukesh, in November. When these two young stars meet across the chessboard, the entire world will be watching this exciting contest. I also extend my very best wishes for the Chess Olympiad to be held in Samarkand next month. In the times ahead, traditional sports such as Kurash and Kabaddi will also bring renewed energy to our sporting partnership.

Today’s discussions have charted a clear course for the future of our relations. A stronger India-Uzbekistan partnership will be a powerful force for peace, progress and prosperity in Central Asia.

Excellency,

Once again, I thank you very much for your friendship and for the fruitful discussions we had today.

In two days, Uzbekistan will celebrate the 35th anniversary of its Independence. On behalf of the 1.4 billion people of India, I extend my warmest congratulations and best wishes to you and all the citizens of Uzbekistan on this occasion.

Thank you very much.

 

***

2304691.title: Vice President inaugurates Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali, celebrates Keralam’s rich cultural heritage
2304691.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President inaugurates Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali, celebrates Keralam’s rich cultural heritage
Aranmula Vallamkali reflects Keralam’s timeless traditions, devotion and spirit of togetherness: Vice President
Tradition and modernity can go hand in hand: Vice President at Aranmula Vallamkali; recalls Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi’
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali on the River Pamba, describing the festival as a glorious symbol of Keralam’s rich cultural heritage, devotion and timeless traditions.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali on the River Pamba, describing the festival as a glorious symbol of Keralam’s rich cultural heritage, devotion and timeless traditions.

The Vice President said the Aranmula Vallamkali,… pic.twitter.com/n2iuofS92w

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 30, 2026

 

Congratulating the people of Keralam on the State’s recent renaming, the Vice President recalled that, as Chairman of Rajya Sabha, he had the privilege of presiding over the passage of the State Renaming Bill during the recently concluded Session. He also conveyed his greetings on the occasion of Onam.


Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the Aranmula Vallamkali, associated with Onam and the sacred tradition of Vallasadya, showcases teamwork, discipline and sportsmanship, with beautifully decorated Palliyodams and more than a hundred oarsmen rowing in perfect rhythm.

Highlighting the spiritual significance of the River Pamba, he said it forms an integral part of the Sabarimala pilgrimage and represents faith, purification and spiritual surrender. Recalling his seven pilgrimages to Sabarimala, he shared that he considers his first visit to the shrine, shortly before his nomination as a Member of Parliament, particularly significant. He said he believes Lord Ayyappa’s blessings were instrumental in his subsequent electoral victory.

Referring to Aranmula’s heritage, the Vice President highlighted the ancient Sree Parthasarathy Temple and the renowned GI-tagged Aranmula Kannadi. Recalling the celebrations at the Vice-President’s Residence last year, he said he had gifted Aranmula Kannadi to the guests, who greatly appreciated its exquisite craftsmanship. He stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional arts, crafts and knowledge systems for future generations.

Observing that people working abroad also return to participate in such cherished traditions, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Aranmula demonstrates how cultural traditions continue to connect people with their roots.

Emphasising that tradition and modernity can go hand in hand, he recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”. He said India’s diverse festivals reflect the country’s cultural unity and observed, “Our diversity is not a source of division; it is a source of our strength.”

The programme was attended by Governor of Keralam Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar;

Minister for Home Affairs Shri Ramesh Chennithala; Minister for Higher Education Shri Roji M. John; Minister for Water Resources Shri Mons Joseph; MP Shri Anto Antony; MLA, Aranmula, Shri Abhin Varkey, and other dignitaries.

2304690.title: Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS) Enters a New Phase of Data-Driven Fertilizer Management
2304690.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers
2304690.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS) Enters a New Phase of Data-Driven Fertilizer Management
iFMS Integration with Meri Fasal Mera Byora (MFMB) Strengthens Data-Driven Fertilizer Management
iFMS Connects More Than 14 Crore Aadhaar-Linked Buyers, Over 2.5 Lakh Retailers and Around 7 Crore Metric Tonnes of Annual Fertilizer Sales Transactions
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS), the digital backbone of fertilizer management in India, has entered a new phase with the introduction of a series of digital initiatives aimed at strengthening transparency, improving fertilizer availability and enabling more effective, data-driven monitoring of the fertilizer supply chain.

Developed and technically supported by the National Informatics Centre (NIC) for the Department of Fertilizers, iFMS connects key stages of the fertilizer ecosystem, including production, imports, movement, stock availability, retail sale and subsidy processing. Operating at a national scale, the system covers more than 14 crore Aadhaar-linked fertilizer buyers, over 2.5 lakh retailers and around 7 crore Metric tonne fertilizer sale transactions annually, while supporting the administration of fertilizer subsidy of nearly ₹2 lakh crore annually.

iFMS Expands Beyond Transaction Monitoring

In recent years, the Department has expanded the role of iFMS beyond recording fertilizer transactions, with a focus on developing it into an integrated monitoring and decision-support platform.

New dashboards and analytical tools have been developed to provide officials with a consolidated view of fertilizer production, imports, dispatches, movement, stocks and retail sales. These tools enable monitoring at the national, State, district and retailer levels, helping identify unusual trends and emerging supply situations at an early stage.

The increasing use of analytics has also enabled examination of fertilizer purchases across buyer categories, landholdings, crops, districts and fertilizer types. The large volume of transactional information available through iFMS can therefore be used not only to record sales but also to identify consumption patterns and support more targeted monitoring and informed decision-making.

Integrating Farmer, Land and Crop Information

An important step towards data-driven fertilizer management has been the integration of iFMS with farmer, land and crop databases maintained by States and other Government platforms.

Integration with Meri Fasal Mera Byora (MFMB) in Haryana and subsequent work towards integration with AgriStack established mechanisms for linking fertilizer transactions with farmer and agricultural information.

These initiatives provided valuable experience in matching fertilizer buyers with farmer and land records and highlighted practical issues relating to the availability, completeness and quality of land and crop information. They also demonstrated the potential of combining fertilizer transaction data with agricultural data to develop a better understanding of fertilizer requirements and consumption.

The experience gained through these integrations has laid the foundation for a more structured approach towards linking fertilizer purchases with farmer requirements.

Framework for Fertilizer Sale Introduces an Additional Digital Layer

Building upon this experience, the Framework for Fertilizer Sale (FFS) has emerged as an important initiative aimed at integrating a Mobile App-based fertilizer booking system with the existing iFMS Point of Sale (PoS) ecosystem.

Under the framework, a farmer can book the required fertilizer based on his ID created in AgriStack, following verification of land and ownership details. A QR-based booking is subsequently generated, and the booking information is accessed at the PoS device, enabling verification between the fertilizer required and the quantity ultimately purchased.

The framework is being implemented in a phased manner, allowing the Department and participating States to study booking behaviour, land and crop information, fertilizer consumption and operational issues before wider implementation. The pilot has also created an important new verification and analytical layer between AgriStack and iFMS.

The framework enables analysis of parameters such as fertilizer consumption per hectare, consumption across different landholding categories, product-wise and crop-wise fertilizer use, and the relationship between fertilizer requirement indicated at the time of booking and actual purchase.

More importantly, the framework enables genuine farmers to access and purchase fertilizer in accordance with their assessed requirements, while bringing greater transparency and data-driven oversight to the fertilizer sale process. Such analysis represents a significant progression from monitoring individual transactions towards understanding fertilizer consumption in its agricultural context.

Digital Monitoring of Fertilizer Movement Strengthened

Digital monitoring of fertilizer movement has also been strengthened during this period through the Vehicle Location Tracking System (VLTS) initiative.

VLTS is intended to provide greater visibility into fertilizer movement across the supply chain. By linking dispatch information with vehicle-location data, the system enables monitoring of fertilizer consignments while they are in transit and can assist in identifying delays and unusual movement patterns.

When combined with Goods-in-Transit, dispatch and stock information already available in iFMS, vehicle tracking provides administrators with a more complete digital view of fertilizer movement from the point of dispatch to its destination.

This strengthens the ability of the Department to monitor not only the quantity of fertilizer dispatched but also its movement through the supply chain and its eventual availability at the intended destination.

Electronic Subsidy Processing Enhances Transparency and Auditability

iFMS continues to play a central role in fertilizer subsidy administration, with subsidy payments linked to actual fertilizer sales recorded through the PoS network.

On 1 January 2026, further work was undertaken towards electronic processing of subsidy bills and integration with financial systems, including PFMS/e-Bill processes. Digitization of the workflow reduces manual intervention, improves traceability and enables different stages of subsidy claims and payments to be monitored electronically.

Random verification mechanisms and additional analytical checks are also being introduced to strengthen scrutiny of DBT-related bills and transactions. Together, these initiatives are intended to make subsidy processing more efficient while providing stronger digital controls and auditability.

iFMS Evolves into an Integrated Digital Platform for Fertilizer Management

The developments undertaken represent an important evolution of iFMS. What began primarily as a system for managing fertilizer movement, sales and subsidy-related transactions is increasingly becoming an integrated digital platform connecting multiple stakeholders and datasets across India's fertilizer ecosystem.

The growing integration of production, imports, logistics, stocks, farmer and land information, fertilizer booking, retail transactions and subsidy processing, together with improved dashboards and analytical capabilities, is providing decision-makers with a more comprehensive and timely view of the fertilizer situation.

 

Inaugurated the e-Bill System at Kartavya Bhawan in New Delhi today, strengthening digital governance and financial reforms.

The system will facilitate smoother, more integrated processing of fertilizer subsidy payments, while eliminating any physical movement of bills.

The… pic.twitter.com/NCyS5F05sG

— Jagat Prakash Nadda (@JPNadda) January 1, 2026

 

The progression from farmer and land-data integration through MFMB and AgriStack to the Framework for Fertilizer Sale, along with vehicle tracking, enhanced analytics and electronic subsidy processing, reflects a broader shift in the role of iFMS.

Technology is increasingly being used not only to record transactions, but also to understand where fertilizer is available, how it is moving, who is purchasing it, how much is being consumed and how these patterns relate to agricultural requirements.

This evolution is strengthening the use of reliable digital information for ensuring timely fertilizer availability, improving transparency and enabling more informed management of one of India's most important agricultural inputs.

2304675.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2304675.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Dr. Jitendra Singh holds Interaction with the delegation of Armed Forces HQ Association; Discussions Focus on Promotions and Pending Service-Related Issues
Union Minister Assures Delegation that Representations made by them Will be dealt in Consultation with Stakeholder Departments
Dr. Jitendra Singh Assures of Thorough Examination of Employee Concerns
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today held an interaction with a delegation of the Armed Forces HQ Association, during which various demands and service-related concerns of employees were discussed.

The delegation submitted a memorandum to the Minister and held detailed discussions on issues concerning career progression, promotions and pending service-related matters. The interaction provided an opportunity for the representatives to place their concerns before the Minister and discuss the issues in a constructive and positive atmosphere.

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated the delegation for coming forward to discuss the concerns of employees in a structured manner. He said that continuous and constructive dialogue with employee representatives is important for addressing genuine service-related concerns and for ensuring greater administrative efficiency.

The Minister assured the delegation that the demands and representations submitted by them would be thoroughly examined in consultation with the relevant stakeholder departments. He further assured that he would make his best efforts in the interest of employees, while ensuring that the concerns raised are considered through the appropriate administrative process.

Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised that a structured and continuous engagement with employee representatives enables the administration to better understand service-related concerns and work towards their appropriate resolution. He reiterated the importance of an open and responsive approach in dealing with employee representations and assured that the concerns raised by the Association would receive due consideration.

The representatives of the Armed Forces HQ Association appreciated Dr. Jitendra Singh and the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) for their continued engagement with employee representatives and for giving due consideration to issues concerning government employees. They particularly acknowledged the work undertaken by DoPT in recent years in addressing long-standing employee-related issues and in taking steps aimed at reducing stagnation and improving employee morale.

The delegation also expressed appreciation for the Minister's approach of providing an opportunity to employee representatives to directly discuss their concerns. The interaction reflected the importance of maintaining a continuous dialogue between the administration and employee associations so that service-related issues can be appropriately examined and addressed.

The meeting concluded on a positive note, with both sides engaging in a constructive discussion on employee-related matters. The Minister reiterated that the representations submitted by the Association would be examined with the concerned stakeholders for appropriate consideration and action.
