2303955.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses the 72nd convocation ceremony of Gujarat Vidyapith in Ahmedabad
2303955.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses the 72nd convocation ceremony of Gujarat Vidyapith in Ahmedabad
Indian way of life, values and traditions form the foundation of Mahatma Gandhi’s message; therefore, his message will never become outdated
Established on October 18, 1920, Gujarat Vidyapith became a centre of research for developing the Indian education system through continuous experimentation
“My mother made me take a lifelong pledge to wear khadi,” said Union Home Minister Amit Shah
The turnover of Khadi and Village Industries was ₹31,000 crore in 2013–14, which increased to ₹1.87 lakh crore in 2025–26
True education is that which gives skill to the hands, sensitivity to the heart, and knowledge along with conscience to the mind
Mahatma Gandhi described religious conversion as a sin and inspired every individual to live according to their ‘Swadharma’
Gandhi Ji spoke not of ‘Navnirman’, but of ‘Punar-nirman’, guided by this spirit, the Modi Government is taking the country forward by making culture, prosperity, security, self-reliance, and ethics in leadership the foundation of its progress
Gandhi Ji believed that freedom would remain incomplete without our indigenous language, culture and labour, Swaraj cannot be achieved without one's own language
Appeal to the youth: Set goals not merely for yourself, but for the nation, society and the poor, no matter how many difficulties arise, you will never become disheartened
There is no mindset more sinful than the one that says, ‘If I speak in my own language, I will become inferior.’” Language connects us with the values of our country, its history and our roots
Mahatma Gandhi emphasised Gram Swaraj, Gram Samriddhi and cooperation, the Modi Government is undertaking numerous initiatives afresh in all three of these directions
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 8:59PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of CooperationShri Amit Shah today addressed the 72nd convocation of Gujarat Vidyapith in Ahmedabad as the chief guest. Gujarat Governor Acharya Devvrat and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

Addressing the convocation, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that today 900 students of Gujarat Vidyapith are receiving their degrees and entering social life, and that this is a precious moment inthe lives of these students.

Shri Amit Shah said that he has been an admirer of Mahatma Gandhi since childhood. His mother too has been a devoted follower of Mahatma Gandhi. Shri Shah said that in the early years of his life he wove khadi and also spun yarn. He said that his mother took a vow from him to wear khadi throughout his life.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Gujarat Vidyapith is the very place where strategy used to be formulated to win the country its freedom in the independence struggle, and where great men such as Acharya J. B. Kripalani and Kaka Saheb Kalelkar worked to awaken the people for Indianness and the mother tongue. He said that when Mahatma Gandhi laid the foundation of Gujarat Vidyapith, he had decided that after India became free, Gujarat Vidyapith itself would create the model for the Indian education system.

Shri Amit Shah appealed to the students receiving their degrees from Gujarat Vidyapith today to be sure to set the goal of their lives before leaving the campus. While setting that goal, there should be no burden in the mind about whether the goal will be achieved or not. He said one should never think whether the work can be done or not, but whether the work is worth doing.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah told the students that one should never set goals for oneself, but rather set them for the nation, society, the people, and especially the poor. If a goal is set for society and the nation, the burden of victory or defeat will not remain on you. No matter how many difficulties one faces in life, there will never be any room for disappointment. If goals are set for oneself and one’s family, difficulties can lead to disappointment, and one may even lose one’s way. Citing his own example, Shri Shah said that he had faced many difficulties in life, but he never became disappointed. He said the reason was that the goals he had set were neither for himself nor for his family. That is why his enthusiasm to work always remained intact. He said that despite all efforts to discourage him, he was never disheartened.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that he has read about, understood and imbibed the thoughts of many great personalities in his life. However, the message of Mahatma Gandhi was relevant then, is relevant today, and will remain relevant for the next 100 years. He said that Gandhi Ji’s message shows the path of welfare to the entire world. Indian ways of life, Indian values and traditions are the fundamental basis of Gandhi Ji’s message, and therefore, it will never become irrelevant.

Shri Amit Shah said that today, 900 students are graduating from Gujarat Vidyapith with degrees and 11 gold medals. Going forward, they will have to face many family and social challenges, but these can be overcome through daily practice and self-study. He said that Gujarat Vidyapith is based on Mahatma Gandhi’s concept of Basic Education, which emphasises village-centric development and the transition from “self” to “others”—that is, an education that teaches us to think of everyone rather than just ourselves. He said that after returning to India, Mahatma Gandhi, following the advice of Gopal Krishna Gokhale, travelled across the country. Despite the immense diversity of languages, dialects, attire, food habits and religions, when he returned, he told Dr. Rajendra Prasad in Champaran that he had witnessed a remarkable sense of unity in the country. He worked to translate this unity into reality through numerous experiments, and Gujarat Vidyapith became a laboratory for these efforts. Shri Shah said that, in accordance with Gandhi Ji’s thoughts and guidance, Gujarat Vidyapith was established on October 18, 1920.

Shri Amit Shah said that Mahatma Gandhi believed that independence remains incomplete until our language, culture, labour and objectives are aligned with the national interest. He believed that Swaraj can never be achieved without one’s own language. He said that if we are not connected with our religion and culture, freedom has no meaning. If our labour and our objectives are not connected with our nation, then even after attaining independence, we will not be able to protect it.

The Home Minister said that the objective of education should be to rebuild the nation through the harmonious integration of the hands, the heart and the mind. Education should impart skills to the hands, awaken sensitivity in the heart, and equip the mind with knowledge along with wisdom and discernment. He said that a mind filled with knowledge alone can give rise to arrogance, whereas a mind enriched with knowledge and wisdom fosters humility and scholarship.

Shri Amit Shah said that the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 rests on five pillars—mother tongue, skills, multidisciplinary learning, the Indian knowledge tradition, and holistic personality development. In a way, this is the same education system that India had imparted to the world for centuries, and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji has now brought that very education system back for the youth of India. He said that without changing its core essence, modern advancements from across the world have been incorporated into the National Education Policy.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Mahatma Gandhi identified seven social sins. If these seven social sins are avoided, 90% of the evils in society can be eliminated. These include politics without principles, business without morality, wealth without labour, pleasure without conscience, knowledge without character, science without humanity, and worship without sacrifice. He said that all young people should always remember these seven social sins. He added that none of us is a great personality who can claim that we would never commit any of these sins. However, if we remain conscious of them, we will hesitate and stop ourselves when faced with the temptation to commit them; and if we ever do commit one, we will also be willing to repent and atone for it.

Shri Amit Shah said that Mahatma Gandhi had prescribed 11 vows, including non-violence, non-stealing, celibacy, non-possession, physical labour, control of the palate, fearlessness, equal respect for all religions, Swadeshi, and the removal of un-touchability. These 11 vows remain relevant even today, and we should move forward by following them. He said that Gandhi Ji had described religious conversion as a sin. The students have also taken a pledge today to live according to their own ‘Swadharma’.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Khadi is not merely a fabric or an economic activity; it is an idea that one should uphold the spirit of Swadeshi in every aspect of one’s life. He said that the turnover of Khadi and Village Industries was ₹31,000 crore in 2013–14, which increased to ₹1.87 lakh crore in 2025–26. He said that Mahatma Gandhi placed great emphasis on cleanliness, and today there is not a single household in the country without a toilet. He added that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has worked to instil the values of cleanliness in the new generation by integrating them with education.

Shri Amit Shah said that there is no objection to learning any language in the world when it comes to knowledge of languages. However, there can be no greater mistake than thinking that speaking in one’s own language will make one inferior. Language is what connects us with the values, history and roots of our country. That is why Gandhi Ji also emphasised the importance of one’s own language. He said that Gandhi Ji also placed emphasis on Gram Swaraj, Gram Samriddhi and cooperation. The Modi Government is working afresh in all three of these areas.

The Home Minister said that even during the period of colonial rule, despite facing repeated setbacks, Gandhi Ji always used the term ‘Punar – Nirman’ of the nation, rather than ‘Navnirman’. Gandhi Ji believed that the principles that had been followed for thousands of years would remain unchanged; however, we would modernise and undertake reconstruction. Shri Shah said that over the past 12 years, the country has embarked on the path of reconstruction. The Modi Government has made a concerted effort from 2014 to 2026 to move forward with the nation’s strength, prosperity, security, self-reliance, and ethics in leadership as its core principles. He said that when the country completed 75 years of Independence, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi placed a resolve before the youth of the country that by 2047, the centenary year of India’s Independence, India should be number one in the world in every field. He said that if we become number one, we will not think only about ourselves but about the welfare of the entire universe. We will be powerful, but our power will be used with wisdom and discretion. We will be prosperous, but that prosperity will be for every citizen of the country and for every suffering person across the world. It is with this vision that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has presented the vision of India in 2047 before today’s youth.

2303936.title: "Students of Today Are the Torchbearers of Democracy Tomorrow": CEC Gyanesh Kumar
2303936.body_html:
Election Commission
"Students of Today Are the Torchbearers of Democracy Tomorrow": CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi
  1. The Election Commission of India (ECI) organised its third regional conference on "Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC 2.0) and ECINET" in Chennai today, focusing on strengthening electoral literacy and democratic awareness among young citizens. Addressing the gathering, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar said that the students of today are the torchbearers of democracy tomorrow. He added that Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELCs) across India will help strengthen the backbone of the world's oldest and largest democracy.
  2. Addressing the participants comprising students and teachers from schools, colleges and universities across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar described students as the future of the nation and emphasised that engaging young citizens and securing their trust and informed participation in the electoral process is an investment in the future of democracy.
  3. CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar stated how elections in India are held strictly as per the Constitution of India, law and instructions issued by ECI and are conducted transparently under the concurrent audit of political parties, candidates or their representatives at all stages. He underlined the need for students and young electors to familiarise themselves with India’s electoral system, democratic values, electoral registration, polling and counting processes, and the role and functioning of the Election Commission of India.
  4. ELC 2.0, with the tagline "Learn Democracy. Lead Democracy.", reimagines Electoral Literacy Clubs as structured, visible and digitally enabled platforms across schools, colleges and universities, encouraging young and first-time voters to understand and meaningfully participate in democracy. Leveraging the extensive ECINet digital platform, which provides all election-related services from roll to poll, the initiative will drive continuous, year-round electoral literacy activities through a dedicated ELC portal, building a streamlined pan-India network of ELCs.
  5. The initiative assumes significance in view of India’s extensive educational ecosystem, comprising approximately 15 lakh schools with nearly 25 crore students and over one crore teachers. The higher education sector comprises nearly 1,500 universities and around 70,000 educational institutions, with an estimated enrolment of 4.33 crore students.
  6. Through this extensive institutional network, ELC 2.0 seeks to promote factual and experiential electoral education, enhance awareness of India’s electoral system, and encourage young citizens to become ambassadors of informed democratic participation. The ELCs will also disseminate information on electoral registration, polling, counting, ECINet App and other key ECI initiatives.
  7. Earlier in the day, in an interactive session with over 500 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) of Tamil Nadu, CEC Gyanesh Kumar congratulated the BLOs for their service which resulted in smooth execution of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the Electoral Rolls in the State. He also congratulated them for the highest-ever poll-participation in the recently concluded Legislative Assembly elections in the State with 4.93 crore votes polled and 86.03% voter turnout which was the highest ever in the history of the State.
  8. The students and the BLOs had a Question-and-Answer session with the CEC as part of the meeting. BLOs had an opportunity to clarify their doubts directly through the interaction.

2303931.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF RAKSHA BANDHAN
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu in her message on the eve of Raksha Bandhan says: -

“On the occasion of Raksha Bandhan, I extend my heartiest greetings to all Indians living in India and abroad.

The festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of our culture and tradition since ancient times. The rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, has been regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as ‘Raksha Bandhan’. In many shlokas and mantras, we find the words “Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala”. These words express the imploration, “May this bond of protection continue forever”.

Raksha Bandhan has become popular as a social festival in which sisters tie a Rakhi on the wrists of brothers and their siblings. This symbolises the feelings of warmth, respect and mutual responsibility not only between brothers and sisters but also among siblings, families, friends and the society. This festival reminds us that every relationship rests on the pillars of trust, sensitivity and mutual cooperation.

On this auspicious occasion, let us pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst our families and our communities. Let us march forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat”.

2303923.title: Student’s Suggestion Prompts Sarbananda Sonowal to Announce Swimming Pool at Dibrugarh University
2303923.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2303923.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Student’s Suggestion Prompts Sarbananda Sonowal to Announce Swimming Pool at Dibrugarh University
Top-performing university athletes to be sent for National Sports Excursion
We Must Take India’s Sporting Culture Deeper Into Educational Institutions: Sarbananda Sonowal
Sonowal interacted with Dibrugarh University Students at PM Narendra Modi ‘Khelo India Samvaad
PM Modi Addresses Nearly 8 Lakh Youth, Calls for Sports to Drive a Healthy, Strong & Self-Reliant India
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

A student’s suggestion during an interaction with Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal at Dibrugarh University in Dibrugarh, Assam, at the ‘Khelo India Dialogue’ has led to the announcement of a swimming pool on the university campus. Sonowal also announced a national sports excursion for the university’s top-performing athletes.

During the interaction, a student raised the need for swimming facilities at the university and asked whether students could be taught swimming, particularly because Dibrugarh and surrounding areas are prone to flooding. Taking note of the suggestion, Sonowal announced that immediate initiative will be taken to develop a swimming pool within the university campus.

The student’s intervention brought a practical dimension to the dialogue, highlighting how sports infrastructure can also address local needs. Besides promoting swimming as a competitive sport, the proposed facility would provide students an opportunity to acquire important water-safety and life skills in a flood-prone region.

“The suggestion raised by the student today reflects the kind of practical thinking and awareness we want to encourage among our young people. In a flood-prone region like Dibrugarh and other adjoining areas, learning to swim is not only about pursuing a sport but also about developing an essential life skill. The proposed swimming pool will create an opportunity for students to learn, train and pursue swimming in a structured environment,” Sonowal said.

Sonowal also joined the students in listening to an address by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the country’s youth. He interacted with the students on the role of sports and fitness in building a healthy and resilient society.

Indian football legend and former national team captain Baichung Bhutia was also present at the programme and addressed the students. His remarks and interaction with the students added to the sporting focus of the event.

Speaking on the occasion, Sonowal said the enthusiasm displayed by students toward sports was encouraging. He said sports are an important means of building healthy individuals and a healthy society and should become an integral part of the lives of young people.

“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has given unprecedented importance to sports, fitness and the development of young sporting talent through initiatives such as Khelo India and Fit India. Our focus is to take this sporting culture deeper into educational institutions, provide young athletes with better infrastructure and exposure, and create opportunities for the youth of Assam and the Northeast to compete and excel at the national and international levels,” Sarbananda Sonowal said.

Sarbananda Sonowal highlighted Prime Minister Modi’s ‘Fit India’ vision and his call to make sports an integral part of everyday life. He said the focus on sports was not limited to developing international-level athletes but also aimed at encouraging young people to lead healthier lives and contribute to building a stronger and self-reliant India.

Sonowal further announced that Dibrugarh University’s top-performing athletes will undertake a national sports excursion. The exposure visit will give promising athletes an opportunity to experience a premier national sports training ecosystem and gain insights into high-performance training and sporting practices.

The programme saw enthusiastic participation from students, who interacted with the speakers and shared their views and suggestions on sports and fitness. Sonowal said the combination of student-led suggestions, better sporting infrastructure and exposure to national-level training facilities can help strengthen the sporting ecosystem and create greater opportunities for young athletes from Assam and the Northeast.

Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Calibrated market intervention to ensure onion availability.

Kanda Express Boosts Movement and buffer Stocks Support Price Stability
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has taken up measures to ensure adequate availability of onions at affordable prices. As part of the intervention, buffer onions are being made available at ₹35 per kg through retail outlets and mobile distribution points across Delhi-NCR. The intervention is being undertaken in response to prevailing market conditions and is aimed at improving consumer access, moderating price pressures and ensuring that adequate quantities of onions remain available in the market.

   

The Kanda Express initiative has strengthened the Government’s logistics response by facilitating the movement of buffer onions from producing regions to major consumption centres. During 2024-25, nearly 12,000 MT of buffer onions were transported through 14 railway rakes to five cities. The initiative witnessed a major expansion in 2025-26, with 86 railway rakes transporting around 88,000 MT of onions to 16 cities across the country.

For the ongoing intervention, onions are being moved through both rail and road networks. The Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) has also been brought into the mechanism to support scientific storage and efficient distribution of buffer onions.

Ms. Nidhi Khare, Secretary, Department of Consumer Affairs (DoCA), flagged off mobile vans of NCCF and NAFED from Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi, marking the start of retail sale of onions through government buffer stocks at ₹35/kg.

2303920.title: From Daily-Wage Work to Scientist-C: How NFSC Support Enabled Tamil Nadu Scholar Karnan A to Build a Distinguished Research Career
2303920.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Daily-Wage Work to Scientist-C: How NFSC Support Enabled Tamil Nadu Scholar Karnan A to Build a Distinguished Research Career
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi

Financial assistance at the right stage can enable talented scholars from disadvantaged backgrounds to continue higher education, pursue meaningful research and build careers that contribute to national development.

Karnan A, a 30-year-old scholar from Sivagangai district in Tamil Nadu, experienced this transformation through support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme. He is now a full-time employee serving as Scientist-C at the CSIR Fourth Paradigm Institute, Bengaluru.

Karnan belongs to a Scheduled Caste community and is the first researcher in his family and among the very few researchers from his community. His parents are seasonal farmers with limited and irregular income, while his two brothers also depended on the same family income for their education.

From school through postgraduate studies, Karnan undertook daily-wage work on weekends to pay his fees and meet basic needs. During the final year of his postgraduate course, he began taking tuition classes, but the income remained insufficient. In 2017, he cleared the National Eligibility Test for Lectureship on his first attempt but narrowly missed the Junior Research Fellowship cut-off.

Without a fellowship, Karnan had to meet his PhD fees and research expenses entirely through income from tuition classes. He also lacked academic guidance, mentorship and professional networks as the first researcher from his village and one of the very few in his taluk. These economic, educational and social barriers made it extremely difficult for him to continue his doctoral studies without burdening his family.

A turning point came in 2019 when Karnan was selected for the NFSC fellowship based on his December 2018 CSIR-UGC NET Lectureship score. His assistance commenced in September 2019, and he received approximately Rs 16 lakh in the form of fellowship support, House Rent Allowance and contingency assistance.

The fellowship gave Karnan financial freedom for the first time in his academic life. He no longer had to depend on daily-wage work or tuition income to meet his fees and research expenses. The resulting confidence and peace of mind enabled him to focus fully on his research. Motivated by the support, he appeared for the NET examination again and successfully qualified for the Junior Research Fellowship.

Karnan completed his PhD, and his thesis received a 'Highly Commended' distinction. He published six research articles in SCI/SCIE-indexed international journals. After completing his doctorate, he was selected as an Institution of Eminence Postdoctoral Fellow at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, with a fellowship of Rs 67,000 per month along with HRA.

Karnan subsequently joined the CSIR Fourth Paradigm Institute, Bengaluru, as Scientist-C. He is currently placed at Level 11 under the Seventh Pay Commission, with a basic pay of Rs 69,700 per month. The support also enabled him to assist his family and contribute towards his brother’s education. Today, he supports his parents and contributes to the education of children in his community.

Talking about the impact of the support, Karnan said, “This fellowship did not just fund my research; it gave me freedom, confidence and a future. Whatever I have achieved in my life after completing my PhD has been possible because of this fellowship.”

Karnan’s journey demonstrates how timely fellowship assistance can help a determined scholar overcome economic and social barriers, achieve academic excellence and build a career in scientific research. He expressed sincere gratitude to the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment for providing the fellowship and to the University Grants Commission for its effective implementation.

2303919.title: DELIVERY OF SAMARTHAK – THE FIRST INDIGENOUS MULTI-PURPOSE VESSEL OF INDIAN NAVY
2303919.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
DELIVERY OF SAMARTHAK – THE FIRST INDIGENOUS MULTI-PURPOSE VESSEL OF INDIAN NAVY
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi

Samarthak, the first Multi-Purpose Vessel (MPV), built by Larsen & Toubro Ltd. (L&T), Kattupalli, was delivered to the Indian Navy on 27 Aug 2026.

The ship comprises over 75 percent indigenous content and has been conceived as a versatile trial and evaluation platform. Further, the ship is engineered to perform maritime surveillance and reconnaissance, Offshore patrolling and support Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief operations, when required.

The ship has been aptly named ‘Samarthak’, meaning ‘The Proponent’. The name signifies the ship’s intended role as a dependable enabler of multiple missions. True to its designation, Samarthak is not limited to one specific task but is engineered to support a wide spectrum of activities, thereby embodying the concept of a multi-purpose vessel. 

The delivery of Samarthak is yet another milestone in the Indian Navy’s indigenous shipbuilding journey and a reaffirmation of the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. The ship stands as a testament in India’s pursuit towards self-sustaining domestic defence industrial ecosystem.

2303917.title: From Sanitation Worker to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneur: NAMASTE-SUY Enables Himanshu to Build a Safer and Dignified Livelihood
2303917.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Sanitation Worker to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneur: NAMASTE-SUY Enables Himanshu to Build a Safer and Dignified Livelihood
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

Timely financial assistance and access to mechanised equipment can enable sanitation workers to move away from unsafe work, become self-employed and build secure livelihoods with dignity.

Himanshu, a 25-year-old graduate from the OBC Lohar community, experienced this transformation through assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) component of the NAMASTE Scheme. A resident of Village Nandgram, Mariyam Nagar, Ghaziabad, he now independently operates a tractor-cum-suction machine and provides mechanised sanitation services in nearby areas.

Himanshu grew up in a family where financial hardship was part of everyday life. His father worked as a daily-wage labourer, and the family often struggled to meet basic needs. As the eldest son, Himanshu assumed responsibility for supporting his parents and younger siblings at an early age. Difficult financial circumstances compelled him to begin working while pursuing his aspirations for a more secure future.

He entered sanitation-related work under local contractors, undertaking sewer and septic tank cleaning in harsh and risky conditions. The work involved physical exhaustion, irregular wages and dependence on contractors. Social stigma associated with the occupation further affected his confidence and dignity, while the absence of financial assets prevented him from starting independent work.

Despite these challenges, Himanshu remained determined to become self-employed and operate modern sanitation equipment instead of continuing unsafe manual labour. He wanted financial stability and social respect for himself, as well as a secure future for his family. He believed that sanitation workers, when provided appropriate support and opportunities, could become independent entrepreneurs.

 

A major turning point came when Himanshu received financial assistance under NAMASTE-SUY for procuring a tractor-cum-suction machine. The assistance, released in August 2025, supported a total project cost of Rs 10,70,400, comprising a loan of Rs 6,74,200 and an upfront capital subsidy of Rs 3,96,200.

The tractor-cum-suction machine enabled Himanshu to begin mechanised sanitation service work independently. Mechanisation reduced his dependence on unsafe manual practices and contractors while improving the safety, efficiency and reliability of his operations. Gradually, his work expanded and he came to be recognised not merely as a labourer, but as a young entrepreneur providing dignified sanitation services.

Before receiving support, Himanshu worked as a sanitation labourer and earned an irregular income that was insufficient to meet his family's needs. After establishing his mechanised sanitation service, his financial condition improved significantly. Even after meeting operational expenses and paying a monthly EMI of Rs 15,059, he now earns and saves approximately Rs 25,000-Rs 35,000 per month. His earnings increase further during the rainy and winter seasons because of higher demand for sanitation services.

The improved income has enabled the family to manage household expenses more comfortably and plan for the future with greater confidence. For Himanshu, the most meaningful change is the happiness and relief visible on his parents' faces. Ownership of the sanitation vehicle has also strengthened his confidence, self-respect and sense of independence.

At present, Himanshu successfully operates his tractor-cum-suction machine in nearby areas and continues to expand his sanitation service work. The initiative has provided him with a stable and sustainable income, safer working conditions through mechanisation, improved social dignity and long-term self-employment opportunities.

Standing beside his tractor-cum-suction machine, Himanshu represents the impact of the NAMASTE-SUY Initiative in empowering sanitation workers through mechanisation, financial support and dignified livelihood opportunities. His journey demonstrates how timely assistance, combined with courage and perseverance, can transform years of struggle into self-reliance and inspire others in the community.

2303894.title: Convergence for Rural Development: DDWS urges States/UTs to integrate works of JJM 2.0 and SBM-G 2.0 under VB-G RAM G Act
2303894.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Convergence for Rural Development: DDWS urges States/UTs to integrate works of JJM 2.0 and SBM-G 2.0 under VB-G RAM G Act
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant initiative, the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, in collaboration with the Ministry of Rural Development, has called for the convergence of works of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) SBM-(G) 2.0 under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025. This convergence is an initiative towards strengthening rural development, integrated planning for rural water security and resilience.

The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 identifies water security as one of its four thematic focus areas, recognising its importance for sustainable livelihoods, agricultural productivity, climate resilience and long-term rural development. The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0, approved on 10 March 2026, places drinking water source sustainability, groundwater recharge and greywater management at the core of its strategy to ensure reliable and resilient rural drinking water services. Similarly, SBM(G) 2.0 focuses on scientific management of solid and liquid waste to improve environmental sanitation and public health. The complementary objectives of these programmes provide an opportunity for integrated planning and implementation through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs).

Under the convergence plan, the States and UTs have been requested to

  • Ensure proper integrated planning
  • Prioritise water security under the VGPPs
  • Include the official in charge of Rural Water Supply/ Public Health Engineering Department in the State-level Steering Committee constituted under the Act
  • Nominate dedicated nodal officers from State Water and Sanitation Mission and Rural Development Department, with corresponding nodal officers to facilitate planning, implementation and monitoring of convergent activities.
  • Technically align VGPPs with Village Action Plans under JJM 2.0 and SBM-G 2.0
  • Register and geo-tag all works under JJM 2.0 and SBM- G 2.0 and other convergent assets on the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack
  • States to utilise geospatial planning tools such as Yuktdhara, along with water budgeting and hydrogeological assessments
  • Institutionalise convergence to ensure that investments under VB-G RAM G, JJM 2.0, SBM-G 2.0 collectively contribute to sustainable drinking water security and improved rural livelihoods.

This close coordination among the Departments of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Rural Development, Panchayati Raj and other concerned departments at the State, district and Gram Panchayat levels is critical for successful implementation. Also, such convergence strengthens the sustainability of rural drinking water services while promoting ecological sustainability, climate resilience and quality of life in rural communities, contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

2303882.title: High-Level African Delegation and UNDP Engage with Department of Land Resources on India’s Digital Public Infrastructure in Land Governance
2303882.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
High-Level African Delegation and UNDP Engage with Department of Land Resources on India’s Digital Public Infrastructure in Land Governance
Secretary, DoLR highlights the vision of ‘Bharat Land Stack’ and ‘Bhu-Aadhaar’ as transformative DPI tools to unlock economic potential and empower citizens
Technical deep dive showcases DILRMP milestones: Over 40.58 Crore land parcels assigned Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) and near-universal computerisation of land records
Delegates from the African Union, Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, and Zambia explore technology adoption, drone-based surveying, and urban land mapping under NAKSHA
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level delegation representing the African Union Commission, senior government officials from six African nations (Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, and Zambia), and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) visited the Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Government of India, at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi, for an intensive technical engagement on Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) in land governance.

The exposure visit aimed to study India’s pioneering digital transformation in land administration, specifically focusing on the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP), the Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN / Bhu-Aadhaar), the National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS), and the NAKSHA initiative for urban habitations.

Land Records as Foundational DPI: Unlocking Economic Value

Welcoming the international delegation, the Secretary, Shri Narendra Bhooshan Department of Land Resources, outlined India’s evolutionary trajectory from colonial and legacy land administration systems to a modern, technology-driven, and citizen-centric digital ecosystem. Emphasizing that digital identity served as India’s foundational layer of DPI through Aadhaar, he noted that geospatial land identity—through the 14-digit Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN)—is serving as the next transformative leap.

Addressing the delegates, the Secretary highlighted:

"Land is the largest and most foundational asset class in any developing economy. In traditional systems, without clear spatial titles and interoperability, vast amounts of land remain 'dead capital' that citizens cannot leverage. Our vision under DILRMP and the Bharat Land Stack is to build an unshakeable digital trust architecture. By linking georeferenced land records, circle rates, registration, and encumbrances into a single interoperable layer, we are creating an ecosystem where even the most vulnerable citizen or rural landowner can unlock formal credit and mortgages seamlessly. This experience and architecture are open to be shared with our partner nations across Africa to accelerate DPI-led inclusive growth across the Global South."

Technical Deep Dive: DILRMP and the Multi-Layered Bharat Land Stack

During the technical sessions, Shri Amit Kumar Singh, Director (LR), DoLR, presented a comprehensive overview of the macro reforms and technological framework powering DILRMP.

Key milestones shared with the international delegates included:

  • 99.90% of textual Records of Rights (RoRs) computerised across the country.
  • 97.43% of cadastral maps digitized, with 76.16% of land parcels fully georeferenced.
  • 85.24% spatial-textual integration achieved between cadastral maps and Records of Rights.
  • Over 40.58 Crore land parcels assigned the 14-digit alphanumeric Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN).
  • 98.96% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs) computerised, with 17 States/UTs adopting the centralized NGDRS platform and 17 States operating state-specific digital registration software.
  • 94.11% of Revenue Courts computerised under the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS), enabling real-time litigation marking on property records.

The delegation was given a walkthrough of the Bharat Land Stack—an integrated, GIS-based federated architecture that layers satellite/drone imagery, georeferenced cadastral boundaries, RoRs, property registration data, master planning/zoning regulations, building approvals, restrictions/litigations, circle rates, and tenancy details to provide a single, authoritative digital source of truth.

Next-Generation Urban Mapping: The NAKSHA Programme

Presenting the urban land records initiative, Shri Shyam Kumar, Director (LR) DoLR, briefed the delegation on the NAKSHA (National Geospatial Knowledge-based Land Survey of Urban Habitations) pilot programme.

The presentation detailed the end-to-end workflow utilizing high-precision surveying technologies:

  • Deployment of 2D Nadir cameras, 5-camera Oblique systems, and LiDAR sensors mounted on aerial drones to achieve centimetre-level positional accuracy.
  • Generation of Ortho-Rectified Imagery (ORI), Digital Elevation Models (DEM), and 3D Reality Models for complex urban landscapes.
  • Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) GNSS rover-based ground truthing, participatory ground validation, and transparent claims/objections redressal.
  • Milestone progress in the pilot phase, with aerial flying completed across 145 out of 150 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), leading to the issuance of legally authentic Urban Property (UrPro) Cards.

Fostering South-South Cooperation

The delegation commended India’s scale, technical rigor, and open-architecture approach to digital governance.

During the discussions, representatives from the UNDP emphasized that India’s DPI model offers invaluable blueprints for African economies seeking structural transformation, tenure security, and efficient digital public service delivery.

Officials representing the African Union Commission highlighted the relevance of India's geospatial integration for Africa’s broader digital transformation strategies and data governance frameworks.

Furthermore, senior delegates from the participating partner nations—including Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, and Zambia—engaged in interactive technical discussions on institutional adaptation, legal harmonization, data privacy, and the deployment of drone-based surveys for land mapping.

The visiting UN and UNDP teams appreciated the Department of Land Resources' collaborative approach to sharing knowledge with the global community.

The meeting concluded with a mutual commitment to deepen technical knowledge exchanges, capacity-building partnerships, and South-South collaboration to advance inclusive, transparent, and resilient land governance frameworks globally.

2303881.title: VADM DAMIAN FERNANDO, COMMANDER OF SRI LANKA NAVY, ON AN OFFICIAL VISIT TO INDIA
2303881.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
VADM DAMIAN FERNANDO, COMMANDER OF SRI LANKA NAVY, ON AN OFFICIAL VISIT TO INDIA
Maiden Visit after taking over as the Commander of the Sri Lanka Navy
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

VAdm Damian Fernando, Commander of the Sri Lanka Navy, is on an official visit to India from 26 to 29 Aug 2026. The visit is aimed at further strengthening bilateral maritime cooperation and enhancing Navy-to-Navy engagements between India and Sri Lanka.

VAdm Damian Fernando was accorded a ceremonial Guard of Honour at South Block, New Delhi, and paid homage to the fallen soldiers by laying a wreath at the National War Memorial on 27 August 2026. He also held discussions with Adm Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, on furthering bilateral maritime cooperation, including joint operations, capacity building, training and measures related to maritime security.

During the visit, VAdm Fernando is scheduled to meet senior defence officials, and also interact with representatives of the Indian defence industry to explore avenues for cooperation and collaboration.

As part of the visit, VAdm Fernando will travel to Kochi to visit Indian Naval training establishments and Headquarters Southern Naval Command, with a focus on enhancing training linkages and professional exchanges between the two navies.

The Sri Lanka Navy is an important and longstanding maritime partner of the Indian Navy. The visit of VAdm Damian Fernando is expected to further consolidate the longstanding and multifaceted Navy-to-Navy relationship between India and Sri Lanka, contributing to enhanced maritime cooperation and greater stability in the Indian Ocean Region.

2303873.title: Vice President releases Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari’s book ‘Sankalp Se Siddhi Ka Modi Yug’
2303873.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President releases Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari’s book ‘Sankalp Se Siddhi Ka Modi Yug’
Prime Minister Modi is ‘Setu Purush’ between dreams and reality: Vice President
‘Sankalp Se Siddhi Ka Modi Yug’ reflects India’s journey from resolve to achievement: Vice President
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today released the book ‘Sankalp Se Siddhi Ka Modi Yug’, authored by Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ghanshyam Tiwari, at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan released Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ghanshyam Tiwari’s book ‘Sankalp Se Siddhi Ka Modi Yug’ at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi today.

Describing the book as an inspiring account of Bharat’s journey from resolve to achievement, the Vice President… pic.twitter.com/7PN3JY9ICl

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 27, 2026

Describing the title ‘Sankalp Se Siddhi Ka Modi Yug’ as carrying a powerful and inspiring message, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that resolve is not merely a wish but a firm determination backed by dedication, hard work and discipline. He said the book traces Bharat’s journey over the past twelve years, covering administrative achievements as well as an ideological renaissance, and presents this journey in the context of the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

 

The Vice President highlighted the book’s effort to connect contemporary governance with the ideas and ideals of great national thinkers including Swami Vivekananda, Rabindranath Tagore, Keshav Baliram Hedgewar, Veer Savarkar and Atal Bihari Vajpayee. He noted that the author aptly describes Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as ‘Setu Purush’ - a bridge between dreams and reality, capturing the link between the sankalp of these thinkers and its realisation in contemporary India.

Recalling the major developments under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the book brings together the spirit of Rashtra Pratham (Nation First), Integral Humanism and Antyodaya. Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan also highlighted national integrity, social and economic justice, women-led development, self-reliant Bharat and transparent governance. He said the work presents various governance initiatives as an effort to translate enduring national ideas into action and encourages readers to reflect on India’s journey and look towards the future with confidence and optimism.

Union Minister of State for Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Rajya Sabha MP and author Shri Ghanshyam Tiwari, Rajya Sabha MP Shri Lahar Singh Siroya, and Shri Pawan Kumar of Prabhat Prakashan were present on the occasion.

2303839.title: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Flags Off Special Metro Train Showcasing India’s Freedom Struggle
2303839.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Flags Off Special Metro Train Showcasing India’s Freedom Struggle
Special Metro train highlights the sacrifices and contributions of freedom fighters and revolutionaries
Initiative will inspire the younger generation to learn about the country’s freedom struggle: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today flagged off a Metro train themed around India’s freedom struggle at Central Secretariat Metro Station in New Delhi. The train showcases the lives, thoughts and contributions of freedom fighters, revolutionaries and other prominent personalities associated with India’s independence movement.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Chouhan said that the initiative would provide Metro commuters an opportunity to learn about the country’s freedom movement and the sacrifices made by its national heroes. He said that the initiative would also help acquaint the younger generation with this important chapter of India’s history and inspire them with the courage and patriotism of those who fought for the nation.

On the occasion, Shri Chouhan also wrote the patriotic words, “Fairs will be held every year at the pyres of the martyrs,” on the Metro train as a tribute to those who made the supreme sacrifice for the country.

Shri Chouhan said that the sacrifices and contributions of India’s martyrs and revolutionaries should continue to inspire generations to come. He appreciated the initiative and thanked Prabhat Prakashan, the Managing Director of Delhi Metro and the entire Metro team for their efforts in bringing the inspiring stories of India’s freedom movement closer to the people.

During the event, Shri Chouhan was also presented with books published by Prabhat Prakashan, including Apnaapan. Books highlighting the journey and story of the Delhi Metro were also showcased on the occasion.

The initiative seeks to make the everyday Metro journey an opportunity for citizens to connect with the nation’s history and draw inspiration from the ideals and contributions of India’s freedom fighters.

2303836.title: Union New and Renewable Energy Minister Pralhad Joshi Brings Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026 Roadshow to Mumbai, urges stakeholders for Clean Energy Investment Push
2303836.ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
2303836.body_html:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Union New and Renewable Energy Minister Pralhad Joshi Brings Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026 Roadshow to Mumbai, urges stakeholders for Clean Energy Investment Push
Green-energy sector presents significant opportunities for investment and collaboration: Shri Pralhad Joshi
Government of Maharashtra to participate as a partner state in the Summit, states Government of Maharashtra Minister Shri Atul Moreshwar Save
Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 to be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi from 2nd to 5th November, 2026
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 5:46PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai, 27 August 2026

 

Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education, Consumer Affairs and Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi, addressed a high-level gathering of investors, developers, financial institutions and industry leaders and stakeholders today at the Mumbai Roadshow for the upcoming Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026.

Delivering the keynote address on the occasion, Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Shri Pralhad Joshi urged stakeholders across the energy sector to participate in the upcoming BRESE 2026, noting that the Summit is generating considerable interest internationally. BRESE 2026 will bring together three major global platforms under one roof — the BRE Summit & Expo, the 9th General Assembly of the International Solar Alliance, and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen. The four-day event is expected to bring together Heads of Government and Energy Ministers from more than 75 countries, global institutional investors, technology providers and over 25,000 participants from across the renewable-energy value chain, Shri Joshi said.

Shri Joshi said that the Summit will provide industry stakeholders an opportunity to build partnerships, explore new markets and engage with global investors and technology providers. For States, the Summit will offer a platform to showcase their project pipelines to global developers and international financial institutions, while for banks and investors, it will facilitate greater convergence between projects and financing opportunities, he added.

Highlighting the growth of the renewable-energy sector in the country, Shri Pralhad Joshi said that India has crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil-fuel capacity, reaching around 302–303 GW, while the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has reached approximately 53.5 lakh beneficiary households. Shri Joshi also said that India’s non-fossil-fuel capacity has increased from 80.3 GW to 300.5 GW over the last 12 years, registering a 275 per cent increase. During the same period, solar capacity increased from 2.8 GW to 165 GW, representing nearly 58-fold growth, while wind capacity rose from around 21 GW to 58 GW, registering a 176 per cent increase. The Union Minister said that India added more than 17 GW of renewable-energy capacity during the first four months of FY 2026–27, including 14.33 GW of solar capacity and over 2 GW of wind capacity.

Shri Joshi said that India, as the fastest-growing major economy in the world, is attracting significant domestic and foreign investment. With rapid infrastructure development taking place across the country, he said that the green-energy sector presents significant opportunities for investment and collaboration. Shri Joshi said that achieving the target of 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel capacity by 2030 will require more than ₹30 lakh crore in investment over the next five years. A significant share of this capital will need to be mobilised through Indian financial institutions, capital markets, insurance funds, infrastructure investors and private capital, he said, adding that this makes Mumbai an important centre for India’s clean-energy investment ecosystem.

Urging Maharashtra to leverage BRESE 2026, Shri Joshi called upon the State to showcase its renewable-energy projects and successful models, particularly its experience under PM-KUSUM, and explore international partnerships to replicate successful solarisation models in agriculture.

Shri Atul Moreshwar Save, Government of Maharashtra Minister for Renewable Energy stated that Maharashtra will be a partner state in the BRESE 2026.  He stated that the state also ranks among the top states nationally for active vendor networks under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, with a robust rooftop solar delivery infrastructure already in place. Maharashtra has fulfilled the target of installing the highest number of solar pumps in the state. . Maharashtra has a target of achieving 65 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030, backed by one of the country's largest industrial energy demand bases and a rapidly expanding renewable energy delivery ecosystem. Shri Save said that the Government of Maharashtra is positive about achieving this target.

The Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Shri Santosh Kumar Sarangi stated that BRESE 2026 will be a one-stop platform for deliberations of the challenges and opportunities of the RE Sector. Joint Secretary, MNRE, Shri JVN Subramanyam, presented the opportunities that the BRESE 2026 will provide to the RE sector stakeholders.  

Hosted by the Ministry of New and Renewable Eneregy and ISA and supported by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), the roadshow was the second in a nationwide series of regional events building momentum ahead of BRE Summit 2026 to be held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi from 2nd to 5th November, 2026. The event brought together senior representatives from the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), the Government of Maharashtra and leading voices from across India's renewable energy, banking and infrastructure sectors.

The Mumbai roadshow also highlighted the accelerating reach of India's clean energy programmes at the grassroots level. Over 50 lakh households across the country are now generating their own solar power under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, with central financial assistance of over Rs 28,000 crore released since the scheme's launch in February 2024. The scheme's budget has been raised from Rs 17,000 crore in 2025-26 to Rs 22,000 crore in 2026-27, reflecting its scale and momentum. Under PM-KUSUM, lakhs of farmers have replaced diesel-dependent irrigation with solar pumps, transforming them from energy

The Mumbai event follows the successful inaugural roadshow held in Jaipur on 24th August 2026. Upcoming roadshows are scheduled across Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Bengaluru and Kolkata in the coming weeks. The MNRE and organising partners are inviting all state governments, utilities and industry stakeholders to actively participate in these regional sessions.

 

About Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRE Summit) 2026:

The Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRE SUMMIT) 2026, one of the world's largest renewable energy expos, is the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy's flagship global platform for advancing clean energy collaboration and investment.

For more information and updates, please visit: www.bresummit.in.

2303703.title: Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft meets with accident near Ganga Barrage in Kanpur
2303703.body_html:
Ministry of Civil Aviation
Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft meets with accident near Ganga Barrage in Kanpur
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 2:08PM by PIB Delhi

As per preliminary information received, a Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft, bearing registration VT-NBV and operated by M/s Garg Aviation Ltd., Kanpur, met with an accident on the afternoon of 27 August 2026, approximately 5 NM from Kanpur Civil Airport, near Ganga Barrage.

The aircraft was on a training flight in the Local Flying Area of Kanpur Civil Airport. There were two persons on board, a trainee pilot and an instructor. Both sustained fatal injuries in the accident.

A team of three officials from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is proceeding to the site for necessary regulatory oversight and coordination.

The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been informed and will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules. The circumstances and cause of the accident will be determined through the investigation.

2303680.title: Text of PM's address at the Khelo India Dialogue via video conferencing
2303680.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM's address at the Khelo India Dialogue via video conferencing
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi

नमस्कार।

आप सभी ने इतने शानदार तरीके से खेलो इंडिया संवाद का ये कार्यक्रम आयोजित किया है। मैं आप सभी को बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं। मैं टेक्नोलॉजी के माध्यम से इस कार्यक्रम से जुड़े केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल के मेरे साथी, सभी मुख्यमंत्री, राज्य सरकार के अनेक मंत्री, संसद में मेरे सहयोगी, My Bharat के लाखों-लाख वॉलिंटियर्स का भी बहुत हृदय से अभिनंदन करता हूं। आज इस कार्यक्रम में देशभर के एथलीट्स और स्पोर्ट्स जगत के महानुभाव भी हम सबके साथ  शामिल हुए हैं।

आप सबको पता है साथियों,

दो दिन बाद, 29 अगस्त को नेशनल स्पोर्ट्स डे भी है। मैं आप सभी को, देशभर के युवाओं को और खेल जगत से जुड़े सभी साथियों को खेल दिवस की अग्रिम शुभकामनाएं देता हूं। ये दिन माँ भारती की एक महान संतान, मेजर ध्यानचंद जी को, उनको याद करने का भी अवसर होता है। 100 वर्ष पहले भारतीय सेना की हॉकी टीम न्यूजीलैंड के दौरे पर टूर पर गई थी और उस टीम में ध्यानचंद जी भी थे। वो टूर भारत और न्यूजीलैंड के, स्पोर्ट्स रिलेशंस के 100 वर्ष पूरे होने का आधार है। कुछ दिन पहले मैं न्यूजीलैंड की यात्रा पर गया था। तब भी मैंने न्यूजीलैंड  में उन्हें याद किया था। मेजर ध्यानचंद जी ने जिन रिश्तों की नींव रखी थी, आज भारत उन रिश्तों की समृद्धि के लिए निरंतर काम कर रहा है।

साथियों,

मैंने इस 15 अगस्त को लाल किले से भारत का स्पोर्ट्स विजन देश के सामने रखा है। जब मैं स्पोर्ट्स की बात करता हूं, तो ये केवल मेडल जीतने तक सीमित नहीं है, ये विकसित भारत के निर्माण में भारत की खेलशक्ति और भारत की युवाशक्ति को एक साथ जोड़ने का अभियान है। मैं हमेशा कहता आया हूं - जो खेले, वो खिले। और खेल में खिलना सिर्फ मैदान पर जीतना नहीं है, खेल में खिलना मतलब व्यक्तित्व का खिलना, परिवार का खिलना और देश का गौरव बढ़ाना।

साथियों,

जब कोई खिलाड़ी सफल होता है, तो वो सफलता केवल उसकी नहीं होती, उसकी सफलता से उसके परिवार की पहचान बनती है, प्रतिष्ठा बढ़ती है। जिस स्कूल और कॉलेज में वो पढ़ा, उसकी प्रतिष्ठा बढ़ती है। उसके जिले और राज्य की पहचान और मजबूत होती है। यानि दुनिया उस खिलाड़ी के नाम से उस शहर या राज्य को पहचानने लगती है। और जब ऐसी अनेक सफलताओं को लेकर कोई क्षेत्र Global Sports Map पर चमकता है, तो दुनिया का उस शहर को देखने का नजरिया भी बदल जाता है। आज के इस कार्यक्रम में देश के जिन सैकड़ों जिलों के खिलाड़ी जुड़े हुए हैं, हर जिले में दुनिया के Sports Map पर चमकने की ताकत है। इस ताकत को समझते हुए ही हमें इस संवाद कार्यक्रम को आगे बढ़ाना है।

साथियों,

इस बार लाल किले से मैंने खेलों से जुड़ी एक बहुत बड़ी चुनौती की तरफ भी देश का ध्यान दिलाया है। ये चुनौती ओलंपिक्स से जुड़ी है। एक कड़वी सच्चाई ये है कि ओलंपिक्स में जितने अलग-अलग स्पोर्ट्स होते हैं, भारत की टीमें उसमें से आधे स्पोर्ट्स में हिस्सा ही नहीं लेती हैं। यानि मेडल टैली के एक बहुत बड़े हिस्से के लिए तो हम कंपीट ही नहीं करते और दशकों से ऐसा ही चला आ रहा है। 2012 के ओलंपिक्स में, उस समय भारत ने सिर्फ, 2012 में सिर्फ 13 खेलों में हिस्सा लिया था। 20 से ज्यादा खेलों में तो भारत की भागीदारी ही नहीं थी। और इन 20 से ज्यादा खेलों में कई सारे खेल ऐसे हैं, जिनका नाम तक देश में लोगों ने शायद ही सुना हो। दुनिया के दूसरे देश उन खेलों में मेडल जीतते हैं और हम उनमें हिस्सा ही नहीं लेते। हमें मेडल टैली बढ़ाने के लिए इन खेलों में भी महारथ हासिल करनी ही होगी। अब जैसे, सर्फिंग और स्पोर्ट्स क्लाइंबिंग, हमारे पास इतनी बड़ी कोस्टलाइन है, इतना बड़ा पहाड़ी क्षेत्र है, जहां इस प्रकार के स्पोर्ट्स के लिए एक स्वाभाविक रूचि हो सकती है। हमारे पास वॉटर स्पोर्ट्स से लेकर विंटर स्पोर्ट्स तक के लिए डेमोग्राफी भी है और जियोग्राफी भी है। लेकिन फिर भी हम ऐसे खेलों में दुनिया में कहीं दिखते ही नहीं हैं। इसलिए, हमें अलग-अलग जिलों में ऐसी संभावनाओं को तलाशना होगा जहां किसी एक खास स्पोर्ट्स का इकोसिस्टम विकसित हो सके,  और इसमें आज के इस कार्यक्रम की बहुत बड़ी भूमिका है।

साथियों,

जब हम 2036 ओलंपिक्स की तैयारी की बात करते हैं, तो हमारा फोकस ये होना चाहिए कि हमें आज से ही वो खिलाड़ी तैयार करने हैं जो 2036 में अलग-अलग स्पोर्ट्स के लिए क्वालीफाई और कंपीट करेंगे। और इसलिए, लाल किले से मैंने 5 साल की उम्र से 15 साल की  उम्र के खिलाड़ियों की पहचान करने के लिए एक बड़े टैलेंट हंट अभियान का ऐलान किया है। और इसमें भी हमें केवल ये नहीं देखना है कि किस बच्चे की किस खेल में रुचि है, बल्कि ये भी देखना है कि कौन सा बच्चा किस खेल के लिए फिट है। हमें उस हिसाब से ही उस बच्चे को ट्रेनिंग देनी होगी। और मैं आप सभी को भरोसा देता हूं, इसके लिए सरकार की तरफ से जो भी सपोर्ट चाहिए, सरकार उसमें आपके साथ कंधे से कंधा मिलाकर चलेगी।

साथियों,

हमारी सरकार भारत में 21वीं सदी का आधुनिक स्पोर्ट्स इकोसिस्टम बनाने के लिए पूरी तरह प्रतिबद्ध है। आज स्पोर्ट्स और स्पोर्ट्स यूनिवर्सिटीज से लेकर आधुनिक ट्रेनिंग सेंटर्स तक देश में एक ऐसी व्यवस्था बनाई जा रही है, जिसमें प्रतिभा को पहचानने से लेकर उसे दुनिया के मंच तक पहुंचाने तक हर स्तर पर सहयोग मिले। हम दुनिया के दूसरे देशों के साथ भी Sports Science, Training, Coaching और अनुभव साझा करने के लिए सहयोग बढ़ा रहे हैं।

साथियों,

Sports को लेकर सरकार कितनी गंभीर है, ये आयोजन भी इसका उदाहरण है। खेलो इंडिया संवाद सिर्फ खेल की बात करने का कार्यक्रम नहीं है। ये एक ऐसे संवाद का मंच है जिसका एक-एक विचार देश के स्पोर्ट्स विजन को एक नई दिशा दे सकता है। और इसके साथ जो युवा संवाद हो रहा है, वो कार्यक्रम आपके Ideas और Aspirations को देश के सपनों से जोड़ने का बहुत बड़ा माध्यम है। इस कार्यक्रम में स्पोर्ट्स इकोसिस्टम, टैलेंट डेवलपमेंट, गवर्नेंस और विकसित भारत को लेकर युवा क्या सोचते हैं, उनके सुझाव क्या हैं, इन बातों को सुना जाएगा और policy process में शामिल किया जाएगा। इसलिए, आप सबसे कहूंगा कि जितना ज्यादा से ज्यादा हो सके, इस मंच का सार्थक उपयोग कीजिए, नए Ideas आने दीजिए, युवा शक्ति के ये नए Ideas ही विकसित भारत की सिद्धि की ताकत बनेंगे।

साथियों,

हम अक्सर सुनते हैं, एक स्वस्थ समाज के लिए, एक अच्छी पारिवारिक व्यवस्था के लिए, एक बेहतर कार्यसंस्कृति के लिए स्पोर्ट्स-पर्सन स्पिरिट बहुत जरूरी होती है और ये स्पोर्ट्स-पर्सन स्पिरिट खेल के मैदान में गए बिना सीखनी बहुत मुश्किल होती है। खेल हमें केवल चैंपियन बनना ही नहीं सिखाता, बल्कि खेल हमें एक बेहतर कंपीटिटर बनना भी सिखाता है। उठना, गिरना, गिरकर फिर से उठना, स्पोर्ट्स ये ज़ज्बा हमारे भीतर लाता है।

साथियों,

खेलों से जीवन कैसे बदलता है, इसका एक बड़ा उदाहरण हमारे पैरा एथलीट्स हैं। पैरा एथलीट्स को जब कोई मैदान में देखता है, तो जीवन के बारे में सोचने का नज़रिया बदल ही जाता है। और जब वो कुछ अचीव करता है, तो उस एथलीट के साथ ही उसके पूरे परिवार को नई ज़िंदगी मिल जाती है। वो मां-बाप, भाई-बहन, जो अपने उस बच्चे को शुरुआती दिनों में संघर्ष करते देखते हैं, उनके लिए उस दिव्यांग खिलाड़ी की सफलता, उनके सपनों को, उनके हौसलों को भी एक नई ऊंचाई दे देती है।

साथियों,

मैं खुद ऐसे प्लेयर्स से हमेशा इंस्पायर होता रहा हूं, अब जैसे आपने सबने नाम जो सुने हैं,  आर्चरी में हमारी एक बेटी, एक कमाल की खिलाड़ी हैं, नाम जानते हो आप?, शीतल। जब पैरालंपिक में उन्होंने मेडल जीता, तो पूरा जम्मू-कश्मीर, पूरा हिन्दुस्तान गर्व से भर उठा। ऐसे ही हमारी एक और बेटी अवनि लेखरा हैं, जिन्होंने दो-दो बार पैरालंपिक के मेडल जीते। मैं जब भी बेटी अवनि से मिलता हूं, बहुत गर्व महसूस करता हूं। सुमित अंतिल हो, नितेश कुमार हो  और अभी-अभी तो आपने नाम सुना होगा, हमारे झंडू कुमार। ऐसे हमारे पैरा-एथलीट्स हैं, ऐसे हर साथी, हमें भी प्रेरित करते हैं।

साथियों,

स्पोर्ट्स, एक बेहतर जीवन की गारंटी है। स्पोर्ट्स हमें बेहतर जीवन जीने के लिए फिट बनाता है, हमारी क्वालिटी ऑफ लाइफ को बेहतर करता है। हम सभी फौजा सिंह जी के बारे में जानते हैं। पिछले वर्ष 100 वर्ष से ज्यादा की आयु में फौजा सिंह जी का निधन हुआ है। खेल के प्रति प्यार हो, फिटनेस हो, ये कैसे जीवन पर्यंत चलता है, फौजा सिंह जी इसकी मिसाल थे। उनका जीवन इस बात की बहुत बड़ी प्रेरणा है कि कैसे स्पोर्ट्स और क्वालिटी ऑफ लाइफ आपस में जुड़े हुए हैं।

साथियों,

स्पोर्ट्स का एक और बहुत बड़ा फायदा होता है, जो असली खिलाड़ी होते हैं, उनमें ड्रग्स, नशे से दूर रहने की इच्छाशक्ति भी पैदा हो जाती है। आज जब नशे की इतनी बड़ी चुनौती युवाओं के सामने है, तो स्पोर्ट्स इसमें भी बहुत सार्थक भूमिका निभाता है।

साथियों,

मुझे खुशी है कि आज भारत में स्पोर्ट्स एक बेहतरीन प्रोफेशन के तौर पर उभरा है। समाज में Sports को लेकर नज़रिया बदला है। आज आप देखिए, हमारे देश में लोग ट्रायाथलोन में हिस्सा ले रहे हैं, 5K और 10K Races दौड़ रहे हैं। यार-दोस्त मिलकर हाय-रॉक्स जैसे चैलेंजेस को पूरा कर रहे हैं। कोई पहली बार शीर्षासन करने की खुशी मना रहा है, तो कोई दोस्तों और फैमिली के साथ मिलकर पिकलबॉल और बैडमिंटन खेल रहा है। ये छोटी-छोटी चीजें हैं, लेकिन अगर इसको एक बड़े नजरिए से देखें, तो इसमें बहुत बड़ा चेंज नज़र आएगा। चेंज ये कि स्पोर्ट्स अब हमारी जिंदगी का हिस्सा बन रहा है। अगर पढ़ाई और करियर का टाइमटेबल बन रहा है, तो दिन भर के रूटीन में स्पोर्ट्स को भी जगह मिल रही है। और यही चेंज है, यही परिवर्तन है, जिसके कारण भारत के स्पोर्ट्स फ्यूचर पर भरोसा भी बढ़ रहा है।

साथियों,

देश में स्पोर्ट्स कल्चर तभी बनता है, जब सामान्य मानवी इससे जुड़े। जब स्कूल्स, स्पोर्ट्स के पीरियड को, को-करिकुलर नहीं, जीवन का हिस्सा मानें। जब ऐसा होता है, तो इससे टैलेंट पूल भी बढ़ता है और स्पोर्ट्स को करियर मानने वाले बच्चों को, उनकी फैमिली का सपोर्ट भी मिलता है। और इसलिए ही मैं कहता हूं, स्क्रीन से ज्यादा, स्पोर्ट्स सेंटर्स की अहमियत है। प्ले-स्टेशन से ज्यादा, प्लेग्राउंड की अहमियत है। और ये तभी होगा, जब आप सब युवा साथी इस अप्रोच को आगे बढ़ाएंगे।

साथियों,

मुझे भारत की युवाशक्ति के सामर्थ्य औऱ उसकी सफलता पर बहुत भरोसा है। मैं देश के हर युवा से कहना चाहता हूं, खेल के मैदान में हो या समाज के बीच, आपकी भागीदारी ही भारत की शक्ति है। आपको खेल से प्यार है, तो इससे जुड़ने के अनेक माध्यम बन रहे हैं। अब नए- नए स्पोर्ट्स इक्विपमेंट्स आ गए हैं, नई टेक्नोलॉजी आ गई है। ट्रेनिंग और कोचिंग के तरीके बदल गए हैं। खेलों के आयोजन की, उसकी प्रतिस्पर्धा की, उसकी विधाओं की जरूरतें बदल गई हैं। इक्विपमेंट डिजाइन है, स्पोर्ट्स टेक्नोलॉजी है, Sports Medicine है, Nutrition है, Psychology, Analytics, ऐसे अनेक क्षेत्रों में युवाओं के लिए नए अवसर बन रहे हैं। आपको ये अवसर छोड़ना नहीं है। इसलिए, इस संवाद में खुलकर अपने ideas सामने रखिए। युवा शक्ति की ये भागीदारी विकसित भारत की सबसे बड़ी ताकत है। एक बार फिर आप सभी युवा साथियों को बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं।

धन्यवाद।

वंदे मातरम्।  

*****

2303663.title: Rajbhasha Utkrishtta Sammaan to Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances in the category of Ministries/Departments with less than 300 personnel for the year 2025-26, by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs
2303663.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2303663.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Rajbhasha Utkrishtta Sammaan to Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances in the category of Ministries/Departments with less than 300 personnel for the year 2025-26, by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 1:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, New Delhi, has been selected for "Rajbhasha Utkrishtta Sammaan" for the year 2025–26 by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, for its outstanding work and continuous excellent performance in the implementation of the Official Language.

 It is noteworthy that the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances was honored with the Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar (First) by the Department of Official Language for two consecutive years—2023–24 and 2024–25.

This year as well, the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, New Delhi, secured the first position for its excellent performance in the implementation of the Official Language.

 According to the rules, if a Ministry/Department receives the first prize for two consecutive years, it is not awarded the Puruskar in the subsequent year.

However, the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances has been consistently performing outstanding work in the field of the Official Language for several years. Therefore, to recognize its continuous excellence in the implementation of the official language, the Department has been selected for this special "Rajbhasha Utkrishtta Sammaan."

This "Rajbhasha Utkrishtta Sammaan" will be presented to the Department during the Hindi Diwas Sammelan scheduled to be held in Navi Mumbai on September 14, 2026, on the occasion of Hindi Diwas.

2303656.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of three newborns and injuries to four others due to a fire incident at the Sick Newborn Care Unit of the District Women's Hospital at Amravati, Maharashtra
2303656.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of three newborns and injuries to four others due to a fire incident at the Sick Newborn Care Unit of the District Women's Hospital at Amravati, Maharashtra
Issues a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report expected to include the status of health of the injured babies and disbursement of compensation announced by the government
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 12:55PM by PIB Delhi

 

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that three newborns died and four others were injured in a fire incident at the Sick Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) of the District Women's Hospital at Amravati, Maharashtra on 24th August 2026. Reportedly, the incident occurred due to a blast in the ventilator machine.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of health of the injured babies and disbursement of compensation announced by the government.

According to the media report, carried on 25th August 2026, there were nine babies in the SNCU when the incident happened. The condition of one of the four injured babies has been reported to be critical.

2303654.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of a woman raped during a diagnostic test at Civil Hospital of Panipat, Haryana
2303654.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of a woman raped during a diagnostic test at Civil Hospital of Panipat, Haryana
​​​​​​​
The Commission issues notices to the Haryana Chief Secretary and Panipat Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 12:52PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report about the death of a 57-year-old woman, who was subjected to rape during a diagnostic test at Civil Hospital of Panipat in Haryana on 16th August 2026. She died during treatment at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Science in Rohtak on 18th August 2026.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Haryana Chief Secretary and Panipat Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

According to the media report, carried on 19th August 2026, the terminally ill patient was taken to the Civil Hospital for medical treatment, where the doctors had prescribed X-ray and CT scan tests. Reportedly, the machine operator had raped the victim inside the CT scan room and threatened not to disclose the incident to anyone.

2303652.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of reported burn injuries to a woman after people allegedly poured boiling water on her, branding her a witch in Bhojpur village, Garhwa district, Jharkhand
2303652.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of reported burn injuries to a woman after people allegedly poured boiling water on her, branding her a witch in Bhojpur village, Garhwa district, Jharkhand
​​​​​​​
Issues notices to the Garhwa District Magistrate and SP, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report to include the status of the victim’s health and compensation, if any, paid to her
Posted On: 27 AUG 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a woman suffered 40% burn injuries after being attacked by a group of people, branding her a witch in Bhojpur village, Garhwa district, Jharkhand. Reportedly, the perpetrators, who are residing in the same village, poured boiling water on the victim during the attack.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Garhwa District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the status of the victim’s health and compensation, if any, paid to her.

According to the media report, carried on 24th August 2026, the victim was admitted to the hospital for medical treatment and an investigation is underway.
