2303121.title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Emphasises deeper Integration of Traditional Knowledge with Modern Science and Medicine
2303121.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Emphasises deeper Integration of Traditional Knowledge with Modern Science and Medicine
Traditional Knowledge Should Move Beyond Conventional Boundaries and Connect with Modern Science, Medicine and Emerging Technologies: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh Visits CSIR-TKDL as Traditional Knowledge Repository Expands Beyond Medicinal Formulations
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 4:36PM by PIB Delhi

Traditional knowledge should not remain confined to conventional systems of medicine but should seek deeper integration with Medicine, modern science and emerging technologies to widen its reach and societal impact, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh, said during his visit to the CSIR-"Traditional Knowledge Digital Library" (CSIR-TKDL) here today.

Dr Jitendra Singh emphasised the need for greater outreach and a wider scope of work in the field of traditional knowledge. He said that traditional knowledge should not be viewed only through the prism of Ayurveda and other indigenous systems, but should increasingly be connected with institutions and disciplines across science and medicine as India moves towards a more integrated approach to research and innovation.

The Minister called for stronger collaboration between CSIR-TKDL and academic and medical institutions. He suggested greater scholarly engagement, including opportunities for co-guidance of postgraduate medical students, to expand traditional knowledge research among students and the wider research community. He noted that such collaborations would also help connect the work of TKDL with the younger generation.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also underlined the importance of bringing together cutting-edge technology and India's rich repository of traditional knowledge. He observed that India's advanced scientific and technological capabilities, together with its extensive traditional knowledge base, provide an opportunity to develop a more integrated approach to research and innovation.

During the interaction, the Minister was briefed on the evolution of TKDL from an initiative focused on digitising traditional knowledge into a structured knowledge resource that makes such knowledge accessible and understandable in modern scientific and intellectual property terminology. The initiative was institutionalised in 2001, initially focusing on Ayurveda formulations, and was subsequently expanded to cover other systems of traditional knowledge.

The discussions also highlighted the data architecture and standardised terminology developed for TKDL, enabling effective searches and presentation of traditional knowledge in formats that can be understood by patent examiners. The knowledge resources have been made available to patent offices in multiple languages, including English, French, German, Japanese and Spanish.

The Minister was informed that TKDL has played an important role in preventing the grant of patents based on already documented traditional knowledge. The database has also continued to expand beyond traditional medicinal formulations to cover areas including diagnostic methods, devices and surgical practices.

Dr. Jitendra Singh called for further strengthening the academic and educational outreach of TKDL. He highlighted the need to familiarise younger students and researchers with traditional knowledge, intellectual property and the processes involved in documenting and protecting such knowledge. The interaction also covered ongoing online learning and capacity-building initiatives aimed at widening access to education related to traditional knowledge.

The Minister further emphasised the potential of collaboration between traditional knowledge institutions and organisations working in modern medicine and scientific research. Referring to emerging research and studies involving traditional practices, he stressed the importance of expanding institutional engagement and encouraging evidence-based work that connects traditional knowledge with contemporary scientific approaches.

During the visit, Dr. Jitendra Singh also visited the book stall and digital library, reviewing resources and knowledge collections associated with TKDL. He interacted with officials and experts on the work being undertaken to document, organise and disseminate India's traditional knowledge in a structured digital format.

The Minister also participated in a plantation activity during the visit, reinforcing the broader emphasis on connecting knowledge, science and societal engagement.

The programme was attended by Dr. M. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR; Dr. Viswajanni Sattigari, Head, CSIR-TKDL; and Shri Mahendra Kumar Gupta, Joint Secretary, CSIR, among other officials and experts.

Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed confidence that CSIR-TKDL, by widening its outreach, strengthening interdisciplinary collaborations and connecting traditional knowledge with contemporary science and technology, can further enhance the relevance and impact of India's rich traditional knowledge repository.

2303108.title: From Outsourced Sewer Work to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneurship: How NAMASTE–SUY Transformed Sushil Kumar Sharma’s Livelihood
2303108.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Outsourced Sewer Work to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneurship: How NAMASTE–SUY Transformed Sushil Kumar Sharma’s Livelihood
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi

Mechanisation and access to affordable finance can transform sanitation work into safer, dignified and sustainable self-employment. Timely assistance enables experienced workers to acquire modern equipment, improve service delivery and secure a more stable livelihood.

Sushil Kumar Sharma, a 32-year-old resident of Ward No. 23 near Loyalka School, Rajura, Pilani, in Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan, has experienced this transformation through the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) under the NAMASTE initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

A graduate with a Bachelor of Arts degree, Sushil belongs to a modest family and lives with his elderly parents. He is the principal earning member of the household. He has also fulfilled his responsibilities towards his three sisters, who are now married. His father’s poor health and the family’s difficult financial circumstances compelled Sushil to discontinue his studies and begin working to support the household. He later joined Nagar Palika Vidya Vihar, Pilani, as an outsourced sewer-cleaning worker and earned approximately ₹15,000 per month.

The work was physically demanding and offered limited financial security. Sushil faced unstable employment, occupational hardship, restricted access to capital and the social stigma associated with sanitation work. Despite these challenges, he remained committed to supporting his family and aspired to establish dignified self-employment in sanitation services.

Sushil received assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana within the NAMASTE framework. The support enabled him to procure a tractor with a suction tanker for mechanised sewer and septic-tank cleaning services. The project, supported on 15 January 2026, had a total cost of ₹10.70 lakh. It was financed through a loan of ₹5.35 lakh and a capital subsidy of ₹5.35 lakh. Access to the vehicle and equipment enabled Sushil to move beyond outsourced work and establish himself as a self-employed sanitation entrepreneur.

Mechanisation made sanitation operations more efficient and reduced dependence on physically strenuous cleaning practices. It also gave Sushil greater control over his work and created a more stable and dignified source of livelihood.

Expressing his contentment over help and support through NAMASTE–SUY, Sushil Kumar Sharma said, “My monthly income increased from approximately ₹15,000 to ₹30,000–₹35,000. The improved earnings have strengthened my financial position and enabled me to support elderly parents and meet the family’s needs with greater confidence”.

Today, Sushil is the owner and operator of a mechanised sanitation enterprise. His transition from an outsourced sewer-cleaning worker to an entrepreneur has brought greater income, stability, self-reliance and social respect.

Sushil Kumar Sharma’s journey demonstrates how financial assistance, capital subsidy and access to modern sanitation equipment can convert occupational experience into sustainable entrepreneurship. His success reflects the role of the NAMASTE–SUY initiative in promoting safety, dignity and economic empowerment among sanitation workers.

Through determination and timely support under NAMASTE–SUY, Sushil has progressed from uncertain outsourced employment to dignified mechanised self-employment. His story is an inspiring example of how targeted assistance can improve livelihoods while advancing safer and more professional sanitation services.

2303115.title: Flash Report on Central Sector Infrastructure Projects worth ₹150 crore and above
2303115.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Flash Report on Central Sector Infrastructure Projects worth ₹150 crore and above
PAIMANA Portal tracks 1,775 Infrastructure Projects worth ₹37.11 lakh crore as of July 2026
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) continues to strengthen monitoring of Central Sector infrastructure projects through its PAIMANA platform, enabling improved tracking, timely reviews, and data-driven decision-making across Ministries. The portal tracks 1,775 Infrastructure Projects worth of ₹37.11 lakh crore as of July 2026.

Key Highlights

  • As of July 2026, 1,775 ongoing infrastructure projects, with a total revised cost of ₹37.11 lakh crore, are being monitored across 17 Central Ministries/Departments. The cumulative expenditure incurred on these projects stands at ₹19.26 lakh crore, accounting for approximately 51.91 per cent of the revised project cost, indicating steady progress in project implementation.
  • A significant proportion of projects are at advanced stages, with 675 projects (~38%) achieving over 80% physical progress, while 305 (~17%) have crossed 80% financial completion. The data also reflects a balanced pipeline, with projects distributed across early and advanced stages of implementation.
  • The Transport & Logistics sector (as per the DEA’s Harmonized Master List) accounts for the highest number of ongoing projects (1246 projects), with revised estimates of ₹19.81 lakh crore underscoring priority to connectivity-driven infrastructure growth.
  • 1,775 ongoing infrastructure projects include 735 Mega projects (project cost of ₹1,000 crore & above) with an original cost of ₹28.77 lakh crore, and 1,040 Major projects (project cost below ₹1,000 crore and up to ₹150 crore) amounting to ₹4.93 lakh crore.
  • Physical and financial progress broadly move in tandem, with a large number of projects clustered at the initial (0–20%) and advanced (81–100%) stages, indicating a pipeline of newly-started projects alongside many nearing completions. While physical progress exceeds financial progress in the 81–100% range, financial progress is relatively higher in the early stages, reflecting upfront expenditure patterns in project implementation.

2.   Ministry/ Departments-wise progress of Infrastructure Projects

  • Ministry of Road Transport & Highways accounts for the highest number of projects, with 993 projects (56%), and a share of total revised project cost of ₹9.62 lakh crore (26%), highlighting its central role in national infrastructure development.
  • Ministry of Railways is implementing 190 projects (11%), with a total revised project cost of ₹6.38 lakh crore (17%).
  • Ministry of Coal accounts for implementing 121 projects (7%), with a total revised project cost of ₹2.22 lakh crore (6%).
  • The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Ministry of Power, Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, and the Department of Water Resources, River Development & GR are implementing 103, 98, 50, and 38 projects, with associated revised costs of ₹4.23 lakh crore, ₹6.08 lakh crore, ₹3.78 lakh crore, and ₹2.01 lakh crore, respectively.
  • The remaining 182 projects (10%), with a total revised cost of ₹2.78 lakh crore (8%), are distributed across various Ministries/Departments including Higher Education, Civil Aviation, Steel, Telecommunications, Labour & Employment, Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Health & Family Welfare, Mines, DPIIT, and Sports. (Refer Annexure I)

3.   Sector-wise (as per DEA’s Harmonized Master List of Infrastructure) Progress of Infrastructure Projects

  • Transport & Logistics remains the dominant sector, accounting for 53% of total revised project cost (₹19.81 lakh crore) across 1,246 projects (70% of the total Projects), underscoring the central role of Roads & Highways, Railways, Aviation, Urban Public Transport, Shipping, and Inland Waterways in economic integration and logistics efficiency.
  • The Energy sector follows with 29% of aggregated revised cost (₹10.66 lakh crore) across 205 projects, reflecting sustained emphasis on Oil & Gas infrastructure, electricity generation, transmission and distribution networks, and energy storage systems.
  • Communication infrastructure, with a project cost of ₹1.34 lakh crore (4%) across 31 projects, represents targeted interventions aimed at strengthening digital connectivity.
  • Water & Sanitation projects account for ₹2.05 lakh crore (5%) across 53 projects, highlighting continued focus on essential urban services.
  • Social & Commercial infrastructure, comprising 91 projects with a revised project cost of ₹0.99 lakh crore (3%), reflects selective investments in education, healthcare, real estate, and tourism, hospitality and wellness.
  • Projects classified under ‘Others’, amounting to ₹2.26 lakh crore (6%) across 149 projects, indicate diversification across sectors such as coal, steel, metals, and mining.

(Refer Annexure II)

 

4.   Completed Projects and New Additions

  • During July 2026, notable commissioned projects include-
    • Project – “Srikakulam Angul Gas Pipeline Project” (₹2,810 crore) of Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas.
    • Project – “Aligarh-Kanpur Pkg I [Aligarh-Bhadwas]” (₹2,069.6) and “Dwarka Expressway Pkg-III Delhi/HR Border to Start of RoB Gurugram (₹2298.37)” of Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.
    • Project – “Transmission System for Evacuation of power from Potential RE Zone in Khavda Area of Gujarat under phase IV 7GW-Part E4” (₹ 224.41 crore) of Ministry of Power.
  • During July 2026, 36 additional projects were brought under the monitoring of PAIMANA. Of these 16 are from Department of Telecommunications, 9 are from Ministry of Steel, 6 are from the Ministry of Road Transport & Highway, 3 are from Department for Promotion of Industry & Internal Trade, 1 from Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs and 1 from Ministry of Power. These include:
  • “Meja Thermal Power Project, Stage-II, (3x800 MW)” (₹ 38,358 crore)
  • “Jaipur Metro Rail Project Phase 2 (Prahladpura to Todi Mod)” (₹ 13,037.66 crore).
  •  “6 Lane Greenfield Varanasi- Ranchi- Kolkata Highway from Chatra to junction with NH- 100 in Deoria village from km 222.000 to km 253.000 Pkg -9” (₹ 1,418.16 crore).

5.   Next date of Press Release: Flash Report for the month of August 2026 would be released on 25th September 2026.

Note

  1. The press release summarizes highlights from the MoSPI’s Flash Report (July 2026) on Central Sector Infrastructure Projects (₹150 crore and above), available at https://paimana-proj.mospi.gov.in/ or via the QR code(below).
  2. The project monitoring interface of PAIMANA is renamed as PAIMANA-PROJ (earlier called as PAIMANA). Further, the PAIMANA-CRIP (Central Repository of Infrastructure Projects), launched by MoSPI in July 2026, serves as the underlying data repository/input layer. Nearly 80% of data are updated via API’s on PAIMANA-CRIP portal that serves as a national central repository of infrastructure projects contributing towards standardized infrastructure monitoring and support informed decision-making for nation-building.

2303091.title: INDIAN NAVY SET TO COMMISSION SECOND INDIGENOUS DIVING SUPPORT VESSEL 'NIPUN'
2303091.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY SET TO COMMISSION SECOND INDIGENOUS DIVING SUPPORT VESSEL 'NIPUN'
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy is set to commission Nipun, the second Diving Support Vessel (DSV) of the Nistar-class, on 31 Aug 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The induction of the specialised vessel will mark an important addition to the Navy’s deep-sea diving and underwater support capabilities and herald the beginning of a new chapter in the ship’s journey from construction to operational service.

 Indigenously designed and constructed by Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), Visakhapatnam, Nipun represents a significant milestone in India’s pursuit of self-reliance in defence shipbuilding. The vessel was delivered to the Indian Navy on 30 Jul 2026, following completion of an extensive programme of outfitting and trials. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2292073

Nipun is a purpose-built platform designed to support a wide spectrum of diving and underwater operations. The ship is equipped with modern diving systems and underwater intervention capabilities, enabling sustained support to divers operating in demanding conditions at sea. It will also augment the Indian Navy’s capability to support submarine rescue operations.

The ship incorporates modern systems for navigation, platform management and precise station keeping, complemented by specialised facilities for diving, underwater intervention and medical support. These capabilities enable Nipun to function as an integrated platform for complex operations beneath the surface.

The forthcoming commissioning of Nipun will further strengthen the Indian Navy’s ability to undertake specialised diving and underwater missions across India’s maritime areas of interest. The induction of this indigenously built platform also reflects the growing capability of the country’s shipbuilding ecosystem to deliver technologically advanced and specialised vessels in support of the Navy’s operational requirements.

2303065.title: CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories Unveils Indigenous Micro and Small Gas Turbine Engines, Boosting India’s Unmanned Defence Capabilities
2303065.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories Unveils Indigenous Micro and Small Gas Turbine Engines, Boosting India’s Unmanned Defence Capabilities
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 2:51PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards self-reliance in advanced aerospace propulsion, CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories (CSIR-NAL) today unveiled three indigenous Micro and Small Gas Turbine Engines — NJ-05 with 5 kg thrust, NJ-50 with 50 kg thrust and NJ-100 with 100 kg thrust — at the SSB Auditorium, CSIR Headquarters, New Delhi. Developed to address critical requirements in indigenous defence technologies, these compact propulsion systems are envisaged for applications including tactical unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), drone interceptors and compact missile systems.

The event brought together senior leadership from India’s defence and scientific communities. Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, PVSM, AVSM, VM, Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC), graced the occasion as the Chief Guest.

From Left to Right:  Dr (Smt) N Kalaiselvi, Director General (CSIR) & Secretary (DSIR), Air Marshal Tejinder Singh PVSM, VSM, VM (Chief Guest & CISC) and Dr Abhay A Pashilkar, Director (CSIR-NAL) at the unveiling of the indigenous Micro and Small Gas Turbine Engines at the SSB Auditorium, New Delhi

Welcoming the gathering, Dr Abhay A. Pashilkar, Director, CSIR-NAL, highlighted the laboratory’s evolving role as a multi-stage integrator for the country’s growing drone ecosystem. He emphasised that Indian industry, including the rapidly expanding aerospace start-up ecosystem, has the potential to manufacture these advanced engines at scale to meet the requirements of the Indian defence sector.

The CSIR-NAL scientific team, led by Shri R. Prathapanayaka, made a detailed technical presentation on the development of the gas turbine engines. The presentation highlighted the advances in high-RPM turbomachinery and high-temperature combustion technologies that have enabled the development of these indigenous propulsion systems.

Addressing the gathering, Dr N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, commended the collaborative efforts of the project team. She underscored that indigenous development of such highly specialised and critical subsystems marks an important milestone in advancing Atmanirbhar Bharat in aerospace engineering.

Unveiling the propulsion systems, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh emphasised the strategic importance of developing advanced gas turbine engine technologies within the country. He observed that indigenous capabilities in such critical technologies would strengthen national security and enhance the technological self-reliance of the Armed Forces.

The successful development of the NJ-05, NJ-50 and NJ-100 represents an important step towards building an indigenous ecosystem for the design, development and manufacture of miniaturised gas turbine propulsion systems. Together with emerging domestic manufacturing capabilities, these technologies are expected to contribute significantly to India’s growing UAV, drone and defence aerospace ecosystem.

2303038.title: Publications Division Wins 7 Honors at FIP Excellence in Book Production Awards 2026
2303038.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Publications Division Wins 7 Honors at FIP Excellence in Book Production Awards 2026
‘Bharat 2026’ Wins Second Prize, ‘Dharti Ki Sehat’ Secures Third Prize at FIP Awards 2026
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Publications Division, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production 2026 for excellence in publishing. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.

Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia, felicitated the editors of the award-winning books and journals and congratulated all the officers and personnel associated with this achievement.

On the occasion, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said, “The seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel. This recognition further motivates us to publish high-quality, credible and useful content. The Publications Division remains committed to reaching readers with outstanding books and journals in Hindi, English and Urdu, carrying important ideas and perspectives related to knowledge, literature, culture and national development.”

He further said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, knowledge and science, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers.

The seven awards comprise four Second Prizes and three Third Prizes. The achievement reflects the Publications Division’s continued commitment to excellence in publishing, editorial quality and diversity of content.

Publications Securing Second Prizes

  • Bharat 2026 (Hindi) received the Second Prize in the Reference Books – Hindi category.
  • Wings to Our Hopes – Volume 2 received the Second Prize in the General and Trade Books – English category.
  • Yojana – July 2026 (Hindi), themed ‘Viksit Bharat@2047’, received the Second Prize in the Journals & House Magazines – Hindi category.
  • Kurukshetra – A Rural Development Monthly Since 1952 received the Second Prize in the Journals & House Magazines – English category.

Publications Securing Third Prizes

  • Dharti Ki Sehat received the Third Prize in the Children’s Books (General Interest) (0–10 Years) – Hindi category.
  • Rangoli Roop Sur Lay Ki received the Third Prize in the Art and Coffee Table Books – Hindi category.
  • Ajkal Urdu – July 2026 received the Third Prize in the Journals & House Magazines, Indian Languages (Urdu) category.

These awards further strengthen the Publications Division’s role in publishing and disseminating credible, informative and culturally enriching content. The recognition will encourage the Division to continue bringing high-quality books, journals and reference publications to readers with authentic and public-oriented content.

Bharat 2026 (Hindi) received the Second Prize in the Reference Books – Hindi category.

Wings to Our Hopes – Volume 2 received the Second Prize in the General and Trade Books – English category.

Yojana Hindi – July 2026, themed ‘Viksit Bharat@2047’, received the Second Prize in the Journals & House Magazines – Hindi category.

Kurukshetra – A Rural Development Monthly Since 1952 received the Second Prize in the Journals & House Magazines – English category.

Dharti Ki Sehat received the Third Prize in the Children’s Books (General Interest) (0–10 Years) – Hindi category.

Rangoli Roop Sur Lay Ki received the Third Prize in the Art and Coffee Table Books – Hindi category.

Ajkal Urdu – July 2026 received the Third Prize in the Journals & House Magazines, Indian Languages (Urdu) category.”

About Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP)

The Federation of Indian Publishers is the representative body of publishers in English, Hindi and other regional Languages with its membership from all over India, representing more than 80 percent of the publishing industry. All the leading publishers of the country are its direct members other publishers being represented through various local associations.

2303019.title: Prize Distribution Ceremony of Swachhata Pakhwada Awards 2026
2303019.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Prize Distribution Ceremony of Swachhata Pakhwada Awards 2026
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 1:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI) successfully observed Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 1st to 15th July, 2026 with active participation from all its Divisions, Attached/Subordinate/Autonomous Organizations including Field Offices located across the country. The fortnight long Pakhwada focused on sanitation, strengthening cleanliness, workplace hygiene, record management, environmental sustainability, waste management and efficient office practices in line with the objectives of Swachh Bharat Mission.

During the fortnight, all the offices and field formations of the Ministry undertook a wide range of activities such as plantation drives, awareness campaigns, seminars, workshops, competitions, rallies, shramdaan and extensive community outreach programmes in Mohallas, schools and public places, Nukkad Nataks, Sea Beach cleaning drives, large scale public participation campaigns, waste-to-wealth initiatives and environmental conservation activities. Initiatives relating to reduction of single-use plastic, waste segregation, recycling and sustainable waste management were undertaken.

The Pakhwada concluded with the Prize Distribution Ceremony of Swachhata Pakhwada Awards–2026 under the chairmanship of the Secretary, MoSPI, wherein Secretary, MoSPI presented Mementos to the three top performing offices. The First, Second and Third Prize was awarded to the Field Operations Division (FOD), National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) and Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) respectively, for their outstanding, exemplary and active participation in the Swachhata Pakhwada.

The Secretary, MoSPI appreciated the active participation and dedicated efforts of all officers and officials across the Ministry. He emphasised that cleanliness may not remain confined only to the Pakhwada but should become an integral part of the working culture and everyday life.

The Ministry reiterates its commitment towards institutionalizing cleanliness, promoting environmental responsibility and fostering a culture of public participation with the vision of a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable India.

 

*****

Samrat/

Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards achieving the vision of Aatmanirbharta in defence, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has approved the transfer of DRDO-developed technologies of all conventional missile systems to the Indian defence industry for production within the country. This Transfer of Technology marks an important milestone in promoting greater participation of the domestic industries in the defence ecosystem by enabling them to undertake indigenous production, as per applicable qualifications, certifications and regulatory requirements.

The provision will enable successful transition of missile system development to industrial production, reflecting the continued efforts of DRDO to leverage the capabilities of the Indian industry for the development and manufacture of advanced defence systems. The objective is to enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, strengthen the defence industrial base and create opportunities for the participation of Indian MSMEs and other technology partners in the supply chain.

The initiative aims to enhance operational capability, reduce import dependence and increase domestic value addition, while supporting the growth of India's defence manufacturing sector. DRDO remains committed to working closely with Indian industry to facilitate the transfer and absorption of advanced defence technologies and to further strengthen the country's indigenous defence capabilities.

2303012.title: India calls for a shift from Drought Response to Drought Resilience at UNCCD CoP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
2303012.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2303012.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India calls for a shift from Drought Response to Drought Resilience at UNCCD CoP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
Treat Drought as a Predictable and Preventable Risk, Not a Recurring Disaster: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Preparedness over Response, Prevention over Crisis Management, Resilience over Recovery should be the Goal: Union Environment Minister
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 12:59PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today called for a fundamental shift in the global approach to drought - from reactive relief to proactive, technology-enabled resilience. Addressing the Ministerial Dialogue on ‘Accelerating Drought Resilience’, at the 17th Conference of Parties (CoP17) of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), in Ulaanbaatar (Mongolia), the Minister said drought is “no longer an occasional event, but a defining development challenge”, affecting water security, food systems, biodiversity and economic stability.

Shri Yadav highlighted India’s coordinated, multi-institutional approach integrating early warning, mitigation, relief and community resilience. Rainfall monitoring and satellite-based drought assessments trigger preparedness at the inter-ministerial and State levels, ensuring that a dry spell does not escalate into a crisis. Emphasising the critical link between land and water, he stated, “restore the forest, before the flow”, underscoring India’s focus on catchment and riverscape forestry to reduce erosion, improve water retention and recharge groundwater. River rejuvenation and revival of traditional water bodies further strengthen water security and rural drought resilience.

The Minister highlighted that community-led restoration of springs and recharge zones in India's hills, while in the plains, a pan-India watershed programme addresses degraded rainfed lands through a ridge-to-valley approach, supported by community institutions and convergence with rural employment programmes. At the household level, drinking water programmes seek to ensure reliable supplies during periods of stress, with assured service levels, local quality testing and prioritisation of vulnerable areas. He also highlighted crop insurance that protects farmers against drought and other non-preventable losses across the crop cycle, combining subsidised premiums with technology-driven assessment for faster and transparent claim settlement. The Minister stressed that community ownership, capacity building and livelihood diversification are central to the transition from reactive relief to proactive, technology-enabled resilience.

Shri Yadav said India’s core belief is that “drought must be managed as a predictable, preventable risk, and not a recurring disaster demanding emergency response”. He highlighted prevention measures including watershed development, water harvesting, afforestation, groundwater recharge and climate-resilient crops, complemented by disaster-related funds, employment guarantees, fodder support and emergency water supplies when required. Calling for stronger global action, Shri Yadav advocated greater investment in ecosystem restoration, stronger early warning systems and coordinated action. “Preparedness over response, prevention over crisis management, resilience over recovery should be the goal”, he said. He concluded by emphasizing that building drought resilience is not optional for the world’s most vulnerable, but a matter of survival, and affirmed India’s readiness to share its knowledge and capacities, including on early warning, for a drought-resilient future for all.

2302979.title: India-Japan Investment Partnership Gains Momentum; Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Invites Greater Japanese Institutional Capital
2302979.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India-Japan Investment Partnership Gains Momentum; Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Invites Greater Japanese Institutional Capital
Shri Goyal highlights India’s strong growth fundamentals and opportunities in semiconductors, AI, clean energy and digital infrastructure
Japanese financial institutions underline long-term confidence in India; seek greater ease of capital flows and profit repatriation
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 10:44AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, today held discussions in Tokyo with senior leaders of leading Japanese financial and investment institutions on strengthening long-term capital flows, deepening investment partnerships and expanding Japanese participation in India’s growth story.

The meeting brought together senior representatives of MUFG, Development Bank of Japan (DBJ), Mizuho, Morgan Stanley, Nomura and Nippon Life. The discussions focused on India’s economic outlook, emerging investment opportunities and measures to further facilitate Japanese institutional investment in India.

Shri Goyal highlighted the strength and resilience of the Indian economy, noting that India recorded 7.7 per cent growth last year despite global uncertainties and is working towards becoming a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047. He underlined the strength of India’s banking sector, robust capital adequacy, low levels of non-performing assets, expanding middle class and rising disposable incomes as key drivers of sustained economic growth.

The Minister highlighted significant opportunities for Japanese investors in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, data centres, renewable energy, green hydrogen, advanced manufacturing and digital infrastructure. He noted that India’s expanding renewable energy capacity and national power grid provide a strong foundation for the growth of energy-intensive digital industries, while the India Semiconductor Mission is creating new opportunities across manufacturing and technology.

Highlighting the strategic and comprehensive nature of India-Japan relations, Shri Goyal said India regards Japan as a trusted partner in its journey towards becoming a global manufacturing, technology and investment hub. He emphasised India’s commitment to intellectual property protection, availability of high-quality talent, policy reforms and creating an increasingly conducive business environment.

The Japanese financial institutions shared their growing engagement with India and expressed strong confidence in the country’s long-term growth prospects. MUFG highlighted its investment of around USD 4 billion in Shriram Finance and its expanding interests in areas including renewable energy and hydrogen. DBJ outlined its dedicated India strategy and growing interest in property development, venture capital and other long-term investment opportunities.

Mizuho highlighted the improving profitability of Japanese companies operating in India and the expansion of its India operations, including its Global Capability Centre in Pune. Morgan Stanley described India as one of its most important global locations, with more than 19,000 employees, and highlighted the evolution of its India operations towards higher-value capital markets and financial services activities.

Nomura highlighted its long-standing presence in India and its role in connecting Japanese companies and global industries with Indian opportunities, including through technology capabilities in areas such as artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. Nippon Life emphasised the importance of long-term “patient capital” and noted the strong returns generated by its Indian operations.

The discussions also covered measures to further facilitate the flow of Japanese institutional capital into India. Participants highlighted the importance of simplifying processes for profit repatriation, improving access to Indian capital markets and ensuring greater regulatory predictability for long-term investors.

The Japanese institutions reiterated that their long-term strategic outlook on India remains strongly positive, while noting that currency movements and certain regulatory and policy considerations can influence short-term investment decisions. Shri Goyal welcomed the feedback and reiterated the Government’s commitment to continuously improving the ease of doing business and creating a more seamless investment environment.

The meeting also explored the potential of GIFT City as a gateway for international capital into India and as a platform for facilitating greater cross-border investment flows between Japan and India.

Shri Goyal emphasised that India is seeking not merely capital but long-term partnerships that bring technology, innovation, manufacturing capabilities, employment and integration with global value chains. He highlighted opportunities in both new and emerging sectors and established businesses requiring modernisation and technological upgrading.

The discussions assume significance in the context of the India-Japan objective of mobilising 10 trillion yen of Japanese private investment into India over the next decade. The interaction reaffirmed the strong confidence of leading Japanese financial institutions in India’s long-term growth prospects and highlighted the considerable potential for expanding bilateral investment, technology and business linkages.

The meeting marked another important step towards deepening the India-Japan economic partnership and unlocking greater flows of long-term Japanese institutional capital into India’s next phase of growth.

 

***

2302977.title: Parishrama Adalat in Hyderabad resolves 65 delayed-payment cases worth ₹8.29 crore, helping MSEs restore cash flow and business continuity
2302977.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Parishrama Adalat in Hyderabad resolves 65 delayed-payment cases worth ₹8.29 crore, helping MSEs restore cash flow and business continuity
Conciliation and ODR mechanisms help turn delayed payments into renewed business confidence
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 10:31AM by PIB Delhi

The ‘Parishrama Adalat’, a Conciliation Conclave for Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE) delayed-payment disputes, organised by the Commissionerate of Industries and Commerce, Government of Telangana, in association with the Ministry of MSME, successfully resolved 65 delayed-payment cases involving ₹8.29 crore. Held at FTCCI, Hyderabad, the conclave brought together MSEs, buyers, public sector enterprises, MSE Facilitation Councils, ADR institutions and officials from the Ministry of MSME and the Government of Telangana.

For a Micro or Small Enterprise, a delayed payment is not merely an unpaid invoice. It can affect salaries, purchase of raw materials, repayment of loans and the ability to take up new business opportunities. The Parishrama Adalat highlighted how timely and effective dispute resolution can support business continuity, restore confidence and strengthen commercial relationships.

The strongest evidence at the conclave came from entrepreneurs who shared how delayed-payment resolution affected their businesses and what they were able to do next. These experiences demonstrated that the real impact of dispute resolution is measured not only in cases closed, but in businesses moving forward.

Success Stories: From Delayed Payments to Business Continuity

Recovery of dues restores confidence: Mrs. Shalini of Neemus Software Solutions Pvt. Ltd. described prolonged delayed payments and contract-related disputes that had drained the enterprise’s savings and confidence. Through the delayed-payment mechanism, the enterprise resolved nine out of eleven cases. Her experience highlighted the wider meaning of payment recovery—the restoration of confidence to continue operating and growing.

Conciliation preserves business relationships: Sri Mukund Maheshwari of Nagarjuna Agro Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. shared how intervention by the Council helped clear an outstanding amount from a buyer who had earlier avoided his calls. Beyond recovery of the payment, the commercial relationship survived. He stated at the event, “Cash flow is the oxygen of industry.”

From two years of waiting to resolution in months: Sri Atmakuri Nammalwar of Sree Solutions described waiting for more than two years for dues. Through the dispute-resolution mechanism, the enterprise reported recovery of close to ₹30 lakh, with four cases closed within approximately two to three months.

Inclusive dispute resolution supports every entrepreneur: A case from Karimnagar highlighted the importance of accessible dispute-resolution mechanisms. A person with disability running a home-pipes business was able to pursue resolution of approximately ₹11 lakh in delayed payments. The case underscored the importance of ensuring that the circumstances of an entrepreneur do not become barriers to seeking a remedy.

ODR turns stuck payments into business momentum: Hyderabad Ammonia & Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. faced delayed payments of nearly ₹79 lakh from nine buyers, putting pressure on its cash flow. Through the ODR Platform, three conciliation meetings helped bring the parties together. One major buyer settled ₹20 lakh, while other buyers also began clearing their dues. The company reported recovering ₹54 lakh in total.

Behind every case number is a person: Sri Gopi Krishna of Shabari Industries shared how delayed payments had begun affecting the enterprise’s credit profile. The mechanism helped the enterprise realise approximately ₹40 lakh in two payments. Sri Ranjith Reddy of A.P. Engineering shared that three cases were resolved through ODR, while Sri Srinivasulu of Panduranga Enterprises spoke of a long-delayed matter involving approximately ₹16 lakh that moved towards settlement.

ODR: Bringing Technology, Institutions and Human Intervention Together

The ODR platform, launched in 2025, brings technology into the dispute-resolution process and provides a digital pathway through which delayed-payment matters can be taken forward, while the institutional role of MSE Facilitation Councils remains central to resolution.

Ms. Ankita Pandey, Director, RAMP, Ministry of MSME, traced the evolution of the delayed-payment framework from the Samadhan Portal to the MSME ODR platform. Figures shared during the programme indicated that more than 800 cases had been filed in Telangana through the ODR ecosystem, with around 85 resolved.

Shri J. Nikhil Chakravarthi, Commissioner of Industries, Government of Telangana, placed the initiative within the State’s wider MSME agenda and underlined technology and institutional strengthening as instruments for improving ease of doing business.

The Parishrama Adalat reinforced that the measure of a dispute-resolution system is not simply how many files it processes, but how many businesses it helps move forward. By bringing together conciliation, institutional mechanisms and digital tools, the initiative seeks to reduce the distance between an entrepreneur, a legitimate claim and a possible resolution.

2303075.body_html:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Minister of State Smt. Savitri Thakur Celebrates 10 Years of UPI, Says Phone Has Become the Wallet of Every Indian
Posted On: 25 AUG 2026 10:00AM by PIB Delhi

Minister of State for Women and Child Development, Smt. Savitri Thakur celebrated the completion of 10 years of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI).

In a post on 'X' the Union Minister of State said that there was a time when carrying cash was a must, while today, phone has become the wallet. 2302944.title: CSIR-CRRI Organises One-Day National Workshop on Road Asset Management Systems and Predictive Analysis
2302944.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-CRRI Organises One-Day National Workshop on Road Asset Management Systems and Predictive Analysis
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 9:49PM by PIB Delhi

The CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI), New Delhi, in collaboration with the Ministry of Education under the Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration (SPARC), organised a one-day workshop on “Road Asset Management Systems & Predictive Analysis” on 24 August 2026 at the CSIR-CRRI Auditorium. The workshop brought together researchers, practitioners and industry experts to deliberate on modern Road Asset Management Systems (RAMS) and the application of predictive analytics for pavement performance, maintenance prioritisation and life-cycle cost optimisation.

The inaugural session was graced by Shri Rajesh Verma, IAS, Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) in NCR and Adjoining Areas, as the Chief Guest. The session commenced with the welcome of the Chief Guest and dignitaries, followed by the National Song and National Anthem and ceremonial lighting of the lamp. Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI, delivered the Welcome Address, while Dr. Sampath Kumar Pasupunuri, Scientist ‘E’ and Workshop Coordinator, CSIR-CRRI, provided an overview of the workshop.

Prof. Manoranjan Parida, Professor, IIT Roorkee, and Prof. Rabibrata Mukherjee, National Coordinator, SPARC, also addressed the gathering. The inaugural address was delivered by Chief Guest Shri Rajesh Verma, IAS, Chairperson, CAQM. The session concluded with the felicitation of the Chief Guest and dignitaries and a vote of thanks by Dr. Pradeep Kumar, Scientist ‘G’ and Head, Pavement Evaluation Division, CSIR-CRRI.

The workshop highlighted that road networks constitute critical public assets and their systematic management is essential for ensuring safe, efficient and cost-effective mobility. The deliberations focused on strengthening scientific and data-driven approaches to road asset management, particularly for improving pavement maintenance decisions and optimising whole-life costs.

The technical programme featured keynote lectures by Prof. Manoranjan Parida and Dr. N. C. Pal, followed by sessions covering road asset management in practice, case studies and implementation challenges; industry perspectives and technologies for road asset management; data acquisition and whole-life costing for road networks, with contributions from Sh. Anukul Saxena, Dr. Bhavesh Jain, Sh.Rohit Mane, Mrs. Prerna Kalra, Dr. Anand Sreeram, Sh. Neeraj Chadha, and Prof. Indrajit Ghosh.

A key highlight of the workshop was the demonstration of the Life-Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA) Tool for Indian Roads, presented by Prof. Kranthi Kumar Kuna and Sh. Soumyarup Biswas. The demonstration provided an opportunity for participants to understand the application of life-cycle cost considerations in road infrastructure decision-making.

The programme concluded with a panel discussion on “From Pilot to Practice: What Will It Take to Make RAMS a Routine Part of Road Agency Decision-Making?”, bringing together experts from academia, government and industry to discuss pathways for wider adoption and institutionalisation of Road Asset Management Systems; featuring Sh. L. P. Padhy, Prof. S. S. Mohapatra, Prof. Amit Goel, Prof. Nikhil Sabu, Sh. Sunil Jain, and Prof. A. K. Singh.

The workshop provided a valuable platform for knowledge exchange and collaboration among stakeholders and underscored the importance of integrating asset management, predictive analytics, data acquisition and whole-life costing into road infrastructure planning and management. The event concluded with a closing ceremony at CSIR-CRRI.

2302939.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates the 9th two-day National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference-2026 in New Delhi
2302939.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates the 9th two-day National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference-2026 in New Delhi
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 9:40PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Co-operation Shri Amit Shah inaugurated the 9th two-day National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference-2026 in New Delhi today.

Prior to the inauguration, Union Home Minister paid homage at the Martyrs’ column by laying a wreath in remembrance of the brave personnel of Intelligence Bureau who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty to safeguardnational security and integrity.

The Conference held in hybrid format was attended by over 850 participants from across the country. Ministers of State for Home Affairs, Union Home Secretary, Deputy NSAs, Heads of CAPFs/CPOs attended the conference in Delhi. DGsP of States and UTs, young police officers working at the cutting-edge level and domain experts from specialised fields joined the conference through virtual mode.

On the first day of the Conference, discussions focused on critical aspects of national security,including response to counter-terrorism challenges, fusion, analysis and operationalisation of intelligence through the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), vision document on narcotics control, detection & deportation of illegal migrants, a policy framework to combat cyber-crime and proxy warfare by Pakistan.

For effective tackling of terrorism & radicalisation, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah emphasised on training for implementation of MHA’s PRAHAAR scheme, expediting trial by bringing back fugitives & using trial in absentia provisions and undertaking comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating UAPA cases. The Home Minister directed that an AI-based analysis of information available on MAC platforms should be done to create SOPs to counter various national security challenges. Union Home Minister directed all the agencies to take strict measures against infiltration.

The second day of the Conference will focus on the threat landscape from sub-aerial systems and formulating countermeasures, securing the blue economy, information warfare and its implications on national security and the need for a bio-security framework.

In pursuance to the directions of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, NSSC is being held every year in hybrid format since 2021, with the objective of finding solutions to major National Security Challenges using the extensive experience of cutting-edge level officers working at the grass roots level in collaboration with domain experts.

2302936.title: Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) and PHARMEXCIL Sign Memorandum of Understanding to Boost Legitimate Pharmaceutical Exports and Strengthen Regulatory Cooperation
2302936.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) and PHARMEXCIL Sign Memorandum of Understanding to Boost Legitimate Pharmaceutical Exports and Strengthen Regulatory Cooperation
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 9:36PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards facilitating legitimate international trade and preventing the diversion of pharma products, the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India and the Pharmaceuticals Export Promotion Council of India (PHARMEXCIL), set up by Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Govt of India signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) today at the CBN Headquarters in Gwalior.

Recognizing India’s position as a leading global supplier of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), bulk drugs, formulations, biologics, and medical devices, the MoU aims to balance the promotion of India’s pharmaceutical exports with effective regulatory oversight.

Role of CBN under the NDPS Act, 1985 Functioning under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) is the agency administering the facilitation, regulations and enforcement provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. Under the NDPS Act, the CBN holds the critical mandate of supervising the licit cultivation of opium poppy, issuing authorizations for the import and export of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, and ensuring that essential chemical inputs are not diverted for illicit use.

This collaborative framework with PHARMEXCIL is a strategic extension of the Government of India’s National Roadmap of Ease of Doing Business. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) executed today broadens this comprehensive approach by integrating, voluntary compliance mechanisms directly into the pharmaceutical export ecosystem to secure international supply chains.

Signing Ceremony and Dignitaries The formal signing ceremony saw the exchange of MoU documents between Dr. Dinesh Bisen, Narcotics Commissioner, representing the CBN, and Shri Raja Bhanu, Director General of PHARMEXCIL.

Key Highlights of the MoU:

• Voluntary Code of Conduct (VCC): The Government, in close consultation with PHARMEXCIL, will develop a Voluntary Code of Conduct setting out recommended practices for the industry. This code will remain voluntary and non-binding, ensuring it does not interfere with normal business operations or create additional statutory or financial burdens on exporters beyond applicable laws.

• Trade Facilitation & Ease of Doing Business: The partnership will focus on identifying operational bottlenecks and recommending measures to streamline legitimate export procedures for compliant pharmaceutical exporters.

• Capacity Building: Both parties will organize joint workshops, seminars, and awareness campaigns for exporters, in coordination with relevant government institutions like CDSCO and Customs wherever required.

• Information Sharing: The MoU establishes a framework for the exchange of necessary information to achieve regulatory objectives, subject to applicable laws and confidentiality obligations. Furthermore, the pharma industry will endeavor to nominate ‘Contact Persons’ from member companies to coordinate matters associated with the VCC.

Following the signing, the dignitaries engaged in detailed deliberations on the way forward, focusing on a six-month action plan. This plan will prioritize pan-India outreach, stakeholder sensitization in collaboration with PHARMEXCIL, and establishing core areas of institutional and regulatory cooperation.

This MoU reaffirms the Government of India's commitment to ensuring the compliant and sustainable growth of the pharmaceutical sector, nurturing growth and boost of export sector, by reduction of dwell time for export authorizationswhile safeguarding against the misuse of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, and controlled precursors.

2302927.title: National Conclave on Tribal Languages & Museums begins in Mysuru, Karnataka
2302927.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
National Conclave on Tribal Languages & Museums begins in Mysuru, Karnataka
Launch of Adi Vaani Platform along with iOS application, addition of five new languages
MoTA AI bot “Jago” Launched
Ministry of Tribal Affairs signs MoU with Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL)
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 9:14PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs today began the three-day National Conclave on Tribal Languages & Museums in Mysuru, Karnataka. The Conclave brings together policymakers, linguists, researchers, technologists, and tribal community representatives to deliberate on the documentation and revitalisation of tribal languages and on strengthening tribal and Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums (TFFM) across the country.

The inaugural session was attended by Shri Durga Das Uikey, Hon'ble Union Minister of State, Ministry of Tribal Affairs; Sri Raghumurthy, Hon'ble Minister, Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka; Shri Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Hon'ble Member of Parliament, Mysuru Constituency; Shri Anant Prakash Pandey, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs; Smt. Kanagavalli, IAS, Secretary, Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka; Prof. Basavaraja Kodagunti, Director, Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL), along with senior officials of the Central and State Governments. The proceedings began with the National Song, the National Anthem and the Naadageethe, followed by the lighting of the ceremonial lamp.

India is witnessing a transformative era in tribal development under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Government remains committed to preserving tribal languages, oral traditions and cultural heritage as a vital part of India’s civilisational identity. Many tribal languages and dialects survive primarily through oral tradition, making systematic documentation, technology-enabled revitalisation and the creation of dedicated spaces such as tribal and Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums an urgent national priority. It is one of the many steps in the journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

The Conclave is being organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in collaboration with the Karnataka State Tribal Research Institute (KSTRI), Government of Karnataka, and the Central Institute of Indian Languages. Nearly 150+ participants across State took part in the National Conclave.

Karnataka Primers Released

In a special release ceremony, the Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, together with KSTRI, released Karnataka Primers in tribal languages — the Primer of Jenukuruba for Class 1 (Kannada, Maths, EVS), along with Sannivesha, Pragiti Nota, Thattegalu flashcards.

MoU signed between MoTA & CIIL

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs and CIIL signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on language documentation and corpus development, under which CIIL will support and share data with the Ministry on tribal languages.

Full-fledged Adi Vaani Platform, AI Bot Released

The session also saw the launch of “Jago”, the official AI conversational assistant of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, along with its mascot. Jago is designed to make information on tribal welfare schemes, programmes, initiatives and repositories easier to find, understand and access, bringing together trusted information from the Ministry through one intelligent interface.

The major highlight of the Conclave was the launch of the upgraded Adi Vaani platform, with new features including its new iOS application, the addition of five new languages, and the launch of the Adi Vaani logo.

 

In her welcome address, Smt. Kanagavalli, IAS, Secretary, Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, highlighted the urgent need for collective dialogue on tribal languages, stressing that the loss of a language also results in the loss of the culture and traditions associated with it.

Delivering the CIIL institutional address, Prof. Basavaraja Kodagunti, Director, Central Institute of Indian Languages, said that languages are living evidence of history and carry the knowledge and experiences of communities across generations. He highlighted the rich and ancient cultural heritage of tribal communities and stressed the need for field-level documentation, use of modern technology, and greater involvement of tribal youth in preserving tribal languages.

In his opening remarks, Shri Anant Prakash Pandey, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, said the preservation of tribal languages and heritage is an important component of the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, and that development should be rooted in dignity, knowledge and community-led interventions.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Member of Parliament, Mysuru Constituency, highlighted the contribution of tribal communities in preserving core Indic traditions through their languages and oral traditions. He further called for expanding the reach of the PM-JANMAN initiative to a larger number of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, and stressed the importance of mainstreaming tribal products through stronger market linkages.

Addressing the inaugural session, Shri Durga Das Uikey, Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs, said the biggest objective is to bring tribal communities into the mainstream on an equal footing, and that various initiatives are being continuously undertaken towards this goal. He also highlighted the presence and contribution of tribal communities in historical narratives, including references to tribal communities.

The session also highlighted the importance of celebrating and documenting the historical legacy of tribal communities, including the legacy of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.

Technical Sessions

Following a presentation by Shri Ganesh Nagarajan , Deputy Secretary, MoTA setting the tone for the day’s deliberations, the afternoon featured three panel discussions.

The first panel, on Documentation, Endangerment & Community-Led Revitalisation, examined the current state of tribal language documentation and community-driven revival models. Panellists included Dr R. Karthick Narayanan, Executive Director, CoDin; Amalesh Gope, Assistant Professor, Tezpur University; Chaithra Puttaswamy, Associate Professor, Department of Humanities and Social Sciences, IIT Kanpur; and Dr Sujoy Sarkar, Lecturer-cum-Junior Research Officer, CIIL.

The second panel, on Technology Meets Tribal Languages, mapped available technical tools — including automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, machine translation, corpus building, and keyboards and fonts — for tribal-language documentation, and discussed data protection, risk of misuse and safeguards for tribal linguistic knowledge, including questions around commercialisation of tribal-language data and content. The session included a live translation demonstration using audio recorded at the morning registration booth. Panellists included Dr Narayan Kumar Choudhary, CIIL Mysore; Prof. A.R.D. Prasad, Former Head, DRTC, ISI Bengaluru; Prof. Dileep A.D., IIT Dharwad; Dr Ritesh Kumar, CEO, UnRealTece; and Ranjani Prasad, Program Coordinator, Keystone Foundation.

The third panel, on Multilingual Education for Tribal Students: Pedagogy, Content & Outcomes, discussed tribal-language pedagogy and curriculum for tribal Schools, content-development gaps measured, availability of primers, dictionaries and teacher handbooks, and the link between tribal-language proficiency and livelihood outcomes. Panellists included Prof. Basavaraja Kodagunti, Director, CIIL; Prof. Minati Panda, JNU; Dr Ramanujam Meganathan, NCERT; and Arunabh Konwar, LLF.

Four Tribal Research Institutes — from Kerala, Odisha, Sikkim and Jharkhand — made presentations on their best practices in language preservation and ongoing projects.

The Conclave will continue on 25 August 2026 with a panel discussion on what tribal communities want, the adoption and signing of the Mysuru Declaration, and a series of sessions on Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums (TFFM).

******

2302922.title: Chirag Paswan inaugurates PMFME Bazaar showcasing India’s Diverse Micro Food Enterprises
2302922.body_html:
Ministry of Food Processing Industries
Chirag Paswan inaugurates PMFME Bazaar showcasing India’s Diverse Micro Food Enterprises
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 9:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) is organising the PMFME Conclave 2026 on 24–25 August 2026 at India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, bringing together over 500 stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening the micro food processing ecosystem and enhancing access to finance, technology and markets.

The Conclave was inaugurated by the Hon’ble Minister of Food Processing Industries, Shri Chirag Paswan, who also inaugurated the PMFME Bazaar, a major attraction of the two-day event. The Bazaar features exhibitors from 25 States and Union Territories, showcasing a wide range of unique, ethnic and traditional food products representing India’s rich culinary and cultural diversity.

During his visit to the Bazaar, the Hon’ble Minister interacted with PMFME beneficiaries and exhibitors, explored their products and appreciated their entrepreneurial journeys. The exhibition provides a platform for micro food processing enterprises, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), cooperatives and individual entrepreneurs to showcase their products, connect with buyers and explore new market opportunities.

The PMFME Bazaar brings together an impressive range of region-specific and traditional food products, including processed foods, millet-based products, spices, pickles, snacks, beverages and other value-added products. The exhibition highlights how local raw materials, traditional knowledge and grassroots entrepreneurship are being transformed into market-ready food products through support under the PMFME Scheme.

The Bazaar also serves as a platform for beneficiaries to gain visibility beyond their local markets and explore opportunities in institutional procurement, modern retail, digital commerce and export markets. It reflects the Ministry’s emphasis on moving micro enterprises from production at the local level towards stronger branding, packaging, quality, market access and commercial sustainability.

The two-day Conclave brings together representatives from all States and Union Territories, District Nodal Officers, District Resource Persons, banks and financial institutions, Ministries and Government organisations, technical institutions, industry bodies, incubation centres and PMFME beneficiaries. The programme provides a platform for knowledge sharing, convergence and exchange of successful experiences.

The inaugural session featured a welcome address by Shri Devesh Deval, Joint Secretary, MoFPI, followed by an address by Shri Avinash Joshi, Secretary, MoFPI. The programme also included felicitation of dignitaries, lamp lighting and screening of a short film on PMFME.

In his brief address, the Hon’ble Minister highlighted the importance of strengthening the micro food processing ecosystem and ensuring that entrepreneurs receive support not only through financial assistance but also in areas such as technology, capacity building, quality, branding and market access. He emphasised the need for a stronger and more comprehensive PMFME 2.0 to respond to the evolving needs of micro food processing enterprises.

A key highlight of the inaugural programme was the launch of a Coffee Table Book featuring 30 success stories of PMFME beneficiaries, showcasing entrepreneurial journeys from different parts of the country. The event also witnessed the launch of ‘FoodNova’, the Ministry’s quarterly magazine featuring developments, innovations, success stories and emerging trends in the food processing sector.

Three MoUs were also signed with APEDA, ONDC and NABKISAN to strengthen market and institutional linkages for PMFME beneficiaries. The partnerships aim to facilitate wider market access, promote digital commerce and create opportunities for micro food processing enterprises in domestic and export markets.

The first day of the Conclave features four thematic technical sessions covering access to finance and sustainability; incubation and entrepreneurship; domestic and global market linkages; and strengthening SHG-led food enterprises through clusters and institutional support.

The PMFME Bazaar remains a central feature of the Conclave, providing a national showcase for the creativity, diversity and commercial potential of India’s micro food processing enterprises. It reflects the Ministry’s commitment to creating stronger market linkages and enabling grassroots entrepreneurs to transform local products into competitive brands with wider domestic and global reach.

The PMFME Conclave 2026 thus brings together policy, finance, technology, entrepreneurship and markets on a common platform, while celebrating the achievements of micro food entrepreneurs and creating a collaborative roadmap for building a stronger, market-oriented and globally competitive micro food processing sector.

2302920.title: Regional Manthan Conference on Road Safety
2302920.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
Regional Manthan Conference on Road Safety
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) today organised a Regional Manthan Conference to deliberate on strengthening road safety through e-Enforcement, integrated data systems, safer vehicles, improved emergency response and stronger district-level capacity for western states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and Union Territory of Dadra Nagar Haveli and Daman Diu (DNH & DD) at Mumbai under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Justice A M Sapre [Retd.], Chairman Supreme Court  Committee on Road Safety. Shri Sanjay Bandyopadhyay Member SCCORS and Shri Mahmood Ahmed AS(T), MoRTH along with other senior officials also attended the conference. The following were deliberated in detail during conference: -

 

  1. Zero Fatality District Initiative: Targeting Where It Matters Most

 

            Good intentions and good schemes must be directed with precision. The Zero Fatality District (ZFD) initiative is our strategic response to the question: where do we act first, and how do we act comprehensively? The ZFD model has been expanded nationally, with 100 critical districts identified across 15 states for focused, 360-degree intervention combining engineering, enforcement, emergency care, and education. These 100 districts together recorded with an average of 400+ fatalities per district annually. The ZFD framework, tailored to each district's specific crash profile, offers a proven strategy to achieve substantial fatality reduction.

 

B.        PM Rahat: No Victim Should Be Lost for Want of Care

 

            Research tells us that 50% of fatalities can be averted if the victim is admitted to hospital within the first one hour i.e., the Golden Hour. And yet, across our country, victims lie unattended, families scramble for cash, and hospitals hesitate to act without assurance of payment. The PM Rahat Scheme, is our definitive response to this tragedy.

 

            PM Rahat provides cashless treatment of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for up to 7 days from the date of accident, covering all road accident victims irrespective of insurance status. What makes this scheme genuinely transformative is its technology backbone including the seamless integration of eDAR (MoRTH) with TMS 2.0 (NHA), the linkage with the 112 emergency helpline. For the first time, Transport, Health, and Police are working from the same data, in real time, toward the same outcome i.e., no victim is lost due to a delay in care.

 

C.        Rah-Veer: Honoring the Courage of the Good Samaritan

 

Even the best emergency care system cannot function if no one acts in those first critical moments at the scene of an accident. This is where the Rah-Veer scheme enters. Rah-Veer is the Government of India's formal recognition and reward for Good Samaritans i.e., individuals who, in the face of uncertainty and risk, choose to stop and save a life by rushing the accident victim to hospital within the Golden Hour.

 

            Every Rah-Veer who saves a life in a serious accident including one involving major surgery, brain or spinal cord injury, at least three days of hospitalization, or death during treatment, is entitled to a cash award of Rs. 25,000 per incident, accompanied by a Certificate of Appreciation. Critically, these Good Samaritans are also protected by law i.e., no Rah-Veer can be subjected to legal proceedings without their consent. Together, PM Rahat and Rah-Veer create a complete emergency care chain i.e., from the moment of accident to the moment of full recovery.

 

D.        Sadak Suraksha Mitra: Building a Community of Road Safety Champions

 

            Road accident statistics reveal that individuals in the age group of 18–45 years account for 66.1% of all fatalities, underscoring the urgent need to involve youth in road safety initiatives. With this objective, the Sadak Suraksha Mitra (SSM) Programme was launched as a youth-led road safety initiative jointly conceptualised by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports.

 

            The programme seeks to strengthen district-level road safety interventions by engaging trained youth volunteers through the MYBharat platform, with a special focus on the top 100 high-fatality districts across the country, where District Road Safety Committees (DRSCs) serve as the primary governance mechanism. These volunteers are not passive bystanders; they are structured road safety professionals, assuming defined roles as Crash Scene Coordinators, data collection for Road Safety Auditors, and Awareness & Engagement Leads. Each role contributes to a specific dimension of district-level road safety action, thereby creating a cadre of youth leaders dedicated to reducing fatalities and promoting safer roads.

 

E.        Data-Driven Hyperlocal Interventions: The Science Behind the Solution

 

            Knowing where accidents happen is only the first step. Acting on that knowledge systematically, at scale, and with the right tools is the harder challenge. The Data-Driven Hyperlocal Intervention (DDHI) framework, is built precisely for this purpose. DDHI empowers District Road Safety Committees (DRSCs) to move from intuition-based planning to evidence-based action.

 

            The DDHI roadmap follows a structured five-stage cycle: Alignment Meeting, Capacity Building, Interventions Planning, Implementation, and Impact Assessment. Each district begins with an alignment on programme objectives, moves through capacity building that deskills processes and upskills people, and proceeds to the identification and implementation of hyperlocal interventions suited to that district's unique crash profile.

            These five programmes are not just isolated efforts. They are interlocking pieces of a single, coherent road safety architecture. Community engagement through SSM feeds into district planning, data intelligence directs enforcement and engineering, Good Samaritans bridge the gap to emergency care and cashless treatment ensures that no Golden Hour is wasted. Hence, every State and district official were urged to take the insights of this workshop back to the field, and integrate these programmes into your road safety plans.

The Conference reaffirmed that reducing road fatalities requires coordinated action across technology, enforcement, vehicle safety, emergency care, crash investigation and institutional capacity.

States and districts were urged to translate these discussions into time-bound action on the ground, strengthening enforcement and road safety systems towards the goal of safer roads and Zero Fatality Districts.

At the end of the conference, it was agreed that States will due root cause analysis of road fatalities, prepare action plan to reduce road accidents and fatalities, prepare District Road Safety Plan to achieve India’s goal of reducing road fatalities by 50% by 2030.
