2302901.title: India Post Accelerates Digital and Infrastructure Transformation with Upgraded Dak MITRA and Dak Sewa Apps
2302901.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
India Post Accelerates Digital and Infrastructure Transformation with Upgraded Dak MITRA and Dak Sewa Apps
“Postal Services at the Click of a Button: India Post Enters a New Era of Technology-Enabled Jan Seva” -  Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia
Aligned with the Vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 under the Leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India Post is Emerging as a Modern, Trusted and Technology-Enabled Institution
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts has taken significant steps towards modernising postal service delivery with the rollout of upgraded Dak MITRA and Dak Sewa mobile applications and the inauguration of 14 renovated Post Office buildings across the country. Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, and Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, launched the upgraded applications and inaugurated the renovated Post Office buildings, in line with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for a digitally empowered, citizen-centric and inclusive India. The initiatives are aimed at strengthening last-mile service delivery, enhancing citizen experience and accelerating the digital transformation of India Post.

Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Minister of State for Communications, Shri Subrat Das, Secretary (Posts), Shri Jitendra Gupta, Director General, Department of Posts, and Smt. Pratima Nath, Member (Estates), during the launch of the upgraded Dak MITRA and Dak Sewa applications and 14 Renovated Post Office Buildings

 .

Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and DoNER, said that the Department of Posts is undergoing a comprehensive transformation driven by technology, policy reforms, organisational change and modern infrastructure. Highlighting the launch of Dak Sewa and Dak MITRA, he said the initiatives reflect the Department’s commitment to making postal services easier to access, easier to use and relevant to every generation of Indians. He congratulated the teams involved in developing these platforms and modernising the postal network, emphasising that the transformation is taking place across India Post in the way it thinks, works and serves citizens.

Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, said that the launch of Dak Sewa and Dak MITRA, along with the modernisation of Post Office infrastructure, marks a significant step towards making India Post more citizen-centric and technology-enabled. He highlighted how Dak MITRA empowers the postal workforce with digital tools for doorstep service delivery, while Dak Sewa brings multiple postal services together through a single, accessible platform available in 23 Indian languages. He said the initiatives reflect the Department’s vision of combining India Post’s traditional trust and service ethos with modern technology, greater speed and ease of access.

Developed indigenously by the Centre for Excellence in Postal Technology (CEPT) under the Advanced Postal Technology (APT) platform as part of DoP IT 2.0 Modernization, the upgraded Dak MITRA (Mobile Interface for Transactions & Rural Assistance) application serves as a unified operational platform for more than 1.4 lakh Branch Post Offices. Deployed on Android-based handheld devices, it enables Branch Postmasters to undertake paperless and real-time postal and financial transactions, including mail booking, OTP-based doorstep delivery, Core Banking Services, insurance services, Aadhaar-based biometric e-KYC, cash deposits and withdrawals, and PLI/RPLI premium collection at the doorstep.

The Dak Sewa App provides citizens with 24x7 access to postal services, including tracking, booking, complaints, Post Office and PIN code locators, and financial calculators, with support for 23 Indian languages through BHASHINI. Simultaneously, the Department of Posts, in collaboration with the School of Planning and Architecture (SPA), New Delhi, is modernising Post Office facilities through a Design Manual focused on functionality, accessibility, operational efficiency and enhanced customer experience, while allowing flexibility for local requirements.

The Design Manual is guided by four core principles identity as a public service, citizen-centric service delivery, future readiness through technology and innovation, and standardisation with flexibility for local adaptation. It also adopts a five-zone spatial framework comprising the Urban Interface Zone, Open Access Forecourt, Open Access Services, Service and Transaction Zone, and Staff Zones, designed to improve accessibility, movement, operational efficiency and overall customer experience.

As part of the Proof of Concept, 40 Post Offices across 17 States were identified for transformation in accordance with the SPA Design Manual. 27 Post Offices have already been completed, with four already inaugurated and 14 additional renovated Post Offices inaugurated on August 24, 2026. The remaining Post Offices under the initial 40-Post Office phase are targeted for completion by August 31, 2026. Based on the experience and learnings from this initiative, the Department proposes to extend the programme to an additional 60 Post Offices during the current financial year. The 14 Post Offices inaugurated today are located at Patliputra (Bihar), Vasant Kunj (Delhi), Sector-56 Gurugram (Haryana), Kakurgachi (Kolkata), Vidisha and Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh), Shillong (Meghalaya), Kandivali West (Mumbai), Shankar Nagar and Ayodhya Nagar (Nagpur), Nirala Nagar, Gomti Nagar and Indira Nagar (Lucknow), and Prayagraj.

             

A glimpse of the modernised interior of one of the newly inaugurated Post Offices, featuring citizen-centric service counters, improved seating and a contemporary India Post design.

 

The renovated Post Offices feature a distinctive India Post identity, improved signage, citizen-centric layouts, dedicated service areas and technology-enabled facilities, with provisions such as 24x7 Sewa facilities, ATMs, after-hours booking and smart parcel services, wherever feasible. Together with Dak MITRA and Dak Sewa, the modernised infrastructure strengthens last-mile delivery, improves accessibility and efficiency, and advances the Department’s vision of a more citizen-centric India Post, combining its trusted legacy with new technology in support of Digital India, Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

2302879.title: RBI's USD-INR Swap Facility Sparks Unprecedented Forex Inflows into India, Banks Raise USD 73 Billion in eleven weeks
2302879.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
RBI's USD-INR Swap Facility Sparks Unprecedented Forex Inflows into India, Banks Raise USD 73 Billion in eleven weeks
Scheme’s Success Reflects Indian Diaspora’s confidence in India’s Banking sector and Economy
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Reserve Bank of India's special USD-INR forex swap facility for FCNR(B) deposits, Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCB) and External Commercial Borrowings (ECB), launched on June 8, 2026, has driven an unprecedented surge in foreign exchange inflows into the country by mobilizing total foreign exchange inflows of US $73 billion as on August 21, 2026. FCNR(B) deposits alone accounted for US $65.40 billion, underlining the overwhelming response of Non-Resident Indians to the scheme.

The scheme's success underscores the strength of the Indian diaspora, who have reposed faith in the Indian banking system and have once again demonstrated their enduring economic and emotional stake in India's growth story, channeling savings into FCNR(B) deposits at a pace that has consistently exceeded expectations.

Having reached US$ 73 billion in under eleven weeks, with still another week to go, this stands out as the largest and fastest foreign-currency mobilisation exercises undertaken by India, comfortably surpassing the scale and pace of the RBI's 2013 FCNR(B) swap scheme, which had raised about US$ 26 billion over roughly three months. The response has been strong enough for the RBI to advance the closure of the FCNR(B) window itself, from September 30 to August 31, 2026, having already achieved its objective ahead of schedule.

By securing large-scale, long-term non-resident deposits and commercial institutional funding entirely on tap, the Government of India has fortified its external buffers with maximum cost-efficiency. This spectacular response is a testament to the fact the Indian economy, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is moving from strength to strength despite unprecedented challenges in the global financial landscape.

2302876.title: Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers chairs CEO Roundtable to discuss priorities to transform India into a Global Chemical Manufacturing and Innovation hub
2302876.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
2302876.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers chairs CEO Roundtable to discuss priorities to transform India into a Global Chemical Manufacturing and Innovation hub
Government and Industry representatives Deliberate on roadmap for India’s USD 1 Trillion Chemicals Economy by 2040
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, in partnership with Invest India, convened a high-level CEO Roundtable today to deliberate on India’s ambition of building a USD 1 trillion Chemicals sector by 2040.

Chaired by Honourable Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri J.P. Nadda in the presence of Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel,   the roundtable: “India’s Chemicals Sector: Charting the Path to USD 1 Trillion by 2040,” deliberated on the strategic priorities required to transform India into a globally competitive chemicals manufacturing and innovation hub. The roundtable was attended by more than 100 delegates from chemical industry from across the globe representing both foreign and domestic industry such as BASF, Tronox, Exxonmobil, Fujifilm, Lubrizol, Dow Chemicals, UPL, Reliance, DCM Shriram, HMEL, SABIC, Haldia Petrochemicals amongst others.

Representatives from more than 30 leading global and Indian chemical companies across speciality chemicals, petrochemicals and bulk chemicals participated in the discussions. 

During the interaction, industry leaders highlighted several issues critical to the long-term competitiveness and growth of the sector, including:

  • Facilitation of large-scale investments through appropriate financing and investment-support mechanisms, particularly for capital-intensive upstream projects.
  • Upgradation of existing PCPIRs from industrial zones into major chemical manufacturing hubs which means upgrading infrastructure facilities and utilities for the industry.
  • Adopting Trade remedial measures to provide level playing field to ensure protection against unfair trade practices.
  • Greater support for R&D, innovation and technology development, through following measures :
    • To attract global talents from abroad, special tax breaks may be offered as done in countries like China, Japan and UK.
    • A Sovereign Fund may be formed to facilitate technology acquisition on the lines of S. Korea and USA.
  • Time-bound single-window clearances for chemical and petrochemical projects, particularly given that the multiple Central and State-level approvals involved in setting up such projects.
  • Development of a comprehensive National Feedstock Policy to reduce vulnerability to geopolitical and global supply-chain disruptions.

Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers Sh. Nadda emphasised that the sector has to touch USD 1 trillion vision by 2040 in the country.  He said the Government is committed to establishing a continuous and institutionalised dialogue mechanism with industry, with the objective of identifying impediments and translating suggestions into time-bound action. It would require sustained investment, technology development, stronger domestic manufacturing capabilities. He further stated that under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government continues to focus on creating an enabling ecosystem for investment, innovation, sustainability and long-term growth. The roundtable provided an important platform for engaging with industry leaders, understanding their priorities and discussing measures to further strengthen India’s position as a globally competitive chemicals manufacturing and innovation hub. He also assured that issues raised by the industry are duly noted and shall be suitably taken up relevant stakeholder Ministries.

In her address, Smt. Anupriya Patel, Union Minister of State of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers, mentioned that recent reforms and schemes launched by the Government to promote manufacturing across the sectors including Chemical and Petrochemical sector such as Bhavya Rasayan, Coal Gasification, Rare Earth Corridors, Critical Mineral Mission, reforms including Tax reforms, Labour reforms. She assured that industry that the Government is committed to transition from a regulatory facilitator to an active growth partner, reducing administrative burden and ensuring the long-term viability of investments.

Stressing the importance of government and industry partnership, Shri Tejveer Singh, Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, stated that the Chemicals sector offers major opportunities across given the expanding domestic demand across key downstream sectors. He emphasized the Department's commitment to collaborating closely with industry leaders to shape future policy interventions. On behalf of the Ministry, he also responded to the questions from the industry leaders.

Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Nivruti Rai, MD & CEO, Invest India mentioned that India is well positioned to emerge as a preferred global destination for chemicals manufacturing, supported by its large domestic market, skilled talent, improving infrastructure and ongoing reforms.

The roundtable also featured a presentation on global investment trends, foreign direct investment flows, state-level competitiveness and sector-specific opportunities.  Invest India also presented  the outcome of a survey conducted with the industry leaders which showed keen interest on part of the industry to come up with investments in the sector.

Apart from the above, representatives from State Governments of Odisha, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh also made interventions in the form of policy packages offered by respective State Governments to attract investment in the State.

The recommendations emerging from the consultation will inform future policy design, institutional reforms and investment facilitation framework that can be acted upon as a  ‘Whole of Government approach’ supporting India’s advancement towards becoming a globally competitive chemicals manufacturing and innovation hub.

Oilseeds: About 188.37 lakh ha area coverage under oilseeds has been reported as compared to 188.69 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.32 lakh ha. Jute & Mesta: About 6.34 lakh ha area coverage under Jute & Mesta has been reported as compared to 6.23 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing an increase of 0.10 lakh ha. Overall, the increase in Jute & Mesta area is mainly attributable to higher coverage in Bihar and West Bengal, which more than offset the decline reported in Assam.

Cotton: About 108.45 lakh ha area coverage under cotton has been reported as compared to 108.73 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.28 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Rajasthan (1.06 lakh ha), Haryana (0.90 lakh ha), Punjab (0.43 lakh ha) etc. Higher area coverage has been reported mainly in Telangana (1.32 lakh ha), Gujarat (0.67 lakh ha), Karnataka (0.14 lakh ha) etc. Overall, the marginal decline in cotton area is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Rajasthan and Haryana, which have largely offset the gains recorded in Telangana and Gujarat.

2302872.title: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal addresses Japanese Business Federation in Tokyo
2302872.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal addresses Japanese Business Federation in Tokyo
India-Japan partnership has expanded into strategic areas such as economic security, defence, supply-chain resilience, technology, innovation, clean energy and people-to-people exchanges: Shri Piyush Goyal
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

India-Japan partnership has expanded well beyond traditional trade to encompass strategic areas such as economic security, defence, supply-chain resilience, technology, innovation, clean energy and people-to-people exchanges stated Union Minister for Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, while addressing a round-table with Keidanren (Japan Business Federation), the apex economic organisation representing more than 1,500 leading Japanese companies.

Shri Goyal called for a deeper business-to-business partnership between the two countries and highlighted the improving ease of doing business in India and the opportunities emerging from the country’s rapidly expanding economy. The Minister invited Japanese investors to scale up their commitment to India and double the number of Japanese companies operating in the country, stating that the number of Japanese companies operating in India “should double this decade from current levels.” He also noted that India and Japan have designated 2026 as the “India-Japan Year of Shared Horizons,” marking 75 years of diplomatic relations between the two nations.

Shri Goyal held business meetings with the leadership of Sumitomo Corporation, Meiji Seika Pharma, Mitsubishi Corporation, Tokyo Electron and MinebeaMitsumi. Discussions focused on opportunities for further expansion of their operations and enhancement of investments in India.

During the meetings, Shri Goyal met Mr. Shingo Ueno, Representative Director, President & CEO, Sumitomo Corporation; Mr. Toshiaki Nagasato, President & Representative Director, Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd.; and Mr. Juro Baba, Representative Director, Executive Vice President, Corporate Functional Officer for Global Planning & Coordination, Mitsubishi Corporation.

The Minister also met with two companies at the forefront of semiconductor manufacturing. At Tokyo Electron, he met Mr. Takeshi Okubo, Chair of Tokyo Electron India; Mr. Vaidya Bharadwaj, India Project Leader; Mr. Takuo Kawauchi, General Manager; Ms. Saori Tsuchiya, Director; and Ms. Yukiko Otaka. At MinebeaMitsumi Inc., he met Mr. Katsuhiko Yoshida, Director, President, COO & CFO, who is overseeing the company’s semiconductor plant project in India. These meetings reflect the growing focus on semiconductor investment as a pillar of the bilateral relationship.

In the afternoon, Shri Goyal held a meeting with Mr. Ichikawa Keiichi, Secretary General of Japan’s National Security Secretariat, Cabinet Office, at the Kantei (Deputy Prime Minister’s Office), underlining the strategic dimension of the bilateral relationship alongside its economic dimension.

Shri Goyal thereafter participated in a Round-table on the Capital Goods, Machinery and Automotive Industry, which provided a platform to discuss ways to strengthen linkages between Japanese enterprises and India’s Tier-II and Tier-III supplier ecosystem and identify new avenues for industrial collaboration and technology partnerships, including for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The round-table saw participation of around 70 businesses from India and Japan.

The Minister highlighted the immense scope of collaboration between the two countries in capital goods, machinery, automotive and advanced manufacturing, and invited Japanese companies to deepen their presence in India in these sectors.

The discussions also explored opportunities for Japanese companies to deepen their engagement with India’s manufacturing ecosystem and contribute to stronger and more resilient supply chains.

In the evening, Shri Goyal participated in a fireside chat moderated by Nikkei Asia, attended by members of the business community and media from India and Japan. He highlighted the expanding contours of the India-Japan economic relationship and the opportunities emerging from India’s growth trajectory, technological transformation and increasing integration with global value chains.

The day’s engagements reaffirmed the strong momentum in the India-Japan economic partnership and India’s commitment to deepening trade, investment, technology and business-to-business linkages, while creating new opportunities for mutually beneficial growth.

Shri Piyush Goyal, arrived in Tokyo today to lead India’s largest-ever business delegation to Japan, comprising over 200 representatives from industry, drawn from sectors including manufacturing, semiconductors, clean energy, steel, automotive, financial services, healthcare, and start-ups. The four-day visit, running from 24 to 27 August, will take the delegation across Tokyo, Nagoya, and Osaka, and is aimed at deepening trade and investment ties under the India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership.

The delegation has been constituted jointly by India’s leading industry associations, in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, and includes representatives nominated by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India (ASSOCHAM).

2302858.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
IFS Officer Trainees of 2025 Batch call on PM
PM calls upon young diplomats to build strong grassroots-level engagement in their countries of posting and deepen India’s connection with local communities
PM asks Officer Trainees to serve as catalytic agents for India’s economic engagement with the world
PM emphasises importance of strengthening digital presence of Indian Missions
PM urges Officer Trainees to work towards making India more attractive global tourism destination by showcasing its civilisational, cultural and geographical strengths
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Officer Trainees of the 2025 Batch of Indian Foreign Service (IFS) called on Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at Seva Teerth earlier today. The group comprised 50 IFS Officer Trainees who come from different States and UTs across the country.

During the interaction, Prime Minister called upon the young diplomats to build strong grassroots-level engagement in their countries of posting and deepen India’s connection with local communities. He emphasised that Indian Missions should foster meaningful relationships not only with governments and institutions but also with people at the community level. He encouraged the Officer Trainees to expand their networks beyond traditional diplomatic circles and deepen engagement with people. Prime Minister encouraged them to combine India’s civilisational strengths with technology, innovation and effective communication to further strengthen India’s global engagement.

Prime Minister called upon the Officer Trainees to serve as catalytic agents for India’s economic engagement with the world. He also emphasised the importance of strengthening the digital presence of Indian Missions. He said that a website is often the first gateway through which people interact with an institution and called for greater use of technology to make the delivery of consular and other services more seamless, responsive and citizen-centric.

Prime Minister urged the Officer Trainees to work towards making India a more attractive global tourism destination by showcasing its civilisational, cultural and geographical strengths. He suggested leveraging the “Bharat ko Janiye” (Know India) Quiz to generate greater interest in India among young people across the world and encouraged the use of AI and gaming to make such initiatives more engaging.

The Officer Trainees shared their experiences from training and Bharat Darshan. They also spoke about the importance of understanding India’s civilisational and cultural links with the world.

2302842.title: From Unpaid Helper to Sanitation Entrepreneur: How NAMASTE-SUY Support Transformed Kapil’s Life
2302842.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Unpaid Helper to Sanitation Entrepreneur: How NAMASTE-SUY Support Transformed Kapil’s Life
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 6:54PM by PIB Delhi

For young people from financially disadvantaged families, limited education and unstable employment can restrict opportunities for progress. Timely financial assistance and mechanised equipment can help sanitation workers build safer, sustainable and dignified livelihoods.

Demonstrating the impact of support under the NAMASTE-Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) Initiative, Kapil, a 25-year-old resident of Village Husainpur in Muradnagar, Ghaziabad District, Uttar Pradesh, progressed from working as an unpaid helper with his father to becoming an independent sanitation entrepreneur.

Kapil belongs to the Scheduled Caste (Khatik) community and comes from a financially weak family dependent on sanitation work. Due to poor economic conditions, he could continue his education only up to the 12th standard.

After completing school, Kapil began assisting his father in sewer and septic tank cleaning. Through hands-on experience, he learned the practical aspects of sanitation services, but received no fixed salary for the physically demanding work.

As the eldest son, Kapil carried major responsibilities from a young age. He helps support his parents, four sisters and three brothers. With limited resources, the household depended mainly on traditional sanitation-related work.

Financial hardship, limited higher education, unstable employment and the social stigma associated with sanitation work restricted Kapil’s prospects. Despite these barriers, he remained determined to become self-reliant and improve his family’s living conditions. Kapil aspired to establish his own enterprise with a desludging vehicle, provide safer and more efficient sanitation services and earn a stable income with dignity.

Kapil received financial assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana, implemented through the NAMASTE Scheme, for purchasing a tractor fitted with a suction machine in 2023. Against a total project cost of ₹10,70,400, he received a loan of ₹6,77,800 and a capital subsidy of ₹3,92,600.

 

The assistance enabled Kapil to establish a mechanised sanitation service business. With the tractor and suction machine, he now undertakes sewer and septic tank cleaning independently and efficiently. The support has strengthened his livelihood, confidence, dignity and social recognition.

Before receiving assistance, Kapil worked as an unpaid helper and had no fixed monthly income. Today, he earns approximately ₹30,000–₹35,000 per month from mechanised sanitation work, even after meeting operational expenses and paying a monthly loan instalment of ₹14,517.

His improved income enables him to meet household expenses, maintain regular savings and provide greater financial security to his family while continuing to repay the loan and manage his enterprise.

The NAMASTE-SUY Initiative transformed Kapil’s practical experience into sustainable self-employment. Access to finance and mechanised equipment helped him move from uncertain, labour-intensive work towards safer operations and an independent livelihood. His journey from an unpaid helper to a sanitation entrepreneur reflects the potential of targeted support to promote mechanised sanitation, dignity of labour and economic empowerment. With determination and timely assistance, he is now building a more secure future for himself and his family.

2302841.title: From Financial Dependence to Self-Employment: Suji K.P.’s Journey of Empowerment
2302841.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Dependence to Self-Employment: Suji K.P.’s Journey of Empowerment
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

For women from economically constrained families, skills alone may not be sufficient to create sustainable livelihoods. Timely access to affordable credit can help them establish enterprises, earn independently and strengthen their families’ financial security.

Demonstrating the impact of support under the NBCFDC Self-Employment Scheme, Suji K.P., a resident of Wayanad district in Kerala, transformed her tailoring skills into a viable enterprise and moved from financial dependence towards self-reliance.

Suji belongs to the OBC Hindu Thiyya community. Before receiving assistance, she had no independent source of income and was financially dependent on her husband, whose earnings were the primary source of livelihood for the family.

Although Suji possessed tailoring skills and wished to start her own business, limited family income made it difficult to arrange the capital required for machinery, materials and other essential business needs.

The major barrier in her journey was economic. Her loan applications were rejected by conventional banks because she had no personal earnings and the family had limited financial resources. As a result, she was unable to establish a tailoring unit despite having the required skills and determination.

Suji aspired to become financially independent by setting up her own tailoring unit. She wanted to create a sustainable source of income, contribute to household expenses and provide greater financial security to her family.

It proved turning point when Suji attended an awareness programme organised by the Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC). Through the programme, she learned about the financial assistance available under the NBCFDC Self-Employment Scheme. And, in 2023, Suji received a loan of ₹3,00,000 under the NBCFDC Schemethat enabled her to establish a tailoring unit and convert her existing skills into a dependable livelihood.

Suji subsequently expanded the enterprise by adding photocopy and lamination services. The diversification helped her cater to a wider range of customers, improve the viability of the unit and build a steadier source of income.

Before receiving the loan, Suji had no independent source of income. Today, she earns approximately ₹15,000 per month through her enterprise, marking a significant improvement in her economic position.

The steady income has reduced her financial dependence on her husband and strengthened the family’s financial security. It has also given her greater confidence, dignity and an identity as a self-employed entrepreneur.

The NBCFDC Self-Employment Scheme enabled Suji to overcome the financial barrier that had prevented her from starting a business. Access to institutional credit helped her translate her skills and aspirations into sustainable self-employment.

Suji K.P.’s journey from having no independent income to running a multi-service enterprise reflects the transformative potential of timely financial assistance. Her success demonstrates how access to credit can empower women from economically constrained communities to build secure livelihoods and contribute meaningfully to their families.

2302840.title: From Financial Constraints to PhD Completion: How NFSC Support Strengthened Shubhankar Ghorai’s Academic Journey
2302840.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Constraints to PhD Completion: How NFSC Support Strengthened Shubhankar Ghorai’s Academic Journey
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

For scholars from financially constrained families, limited educational resources and restricted access to career opportunities can create significant barriers to pursuing higher education. Timely fellowship support can enable scholars to continue their academic journey with greater confidence and focus.

Demonstrating the impact of support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Shubhankar Ghorai, a 31-year-old scholar from Paschim Medinipur, West Bengal, overcame financial constraints and limited resources to successfully complete his Ph.D.

Before receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme, Shubhankar faced financial difficulties and limited access to educational resources. These constraints affected his academic progress and made it challenging for him to pursue better educational opportunities and professional development.

His family also faced financial difficulties and had limited resources for his education and career development. Economic constraints, along with a lack of career opportunities, affected his academic and professional growth.

Despite these challenges, Shubhankar aspired to complete higher education, improve his research skills and secure a good professional position. He also wanted to support his family and contribute to society through his work.

Shubhankar began receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme in February 2020 that proved turning point for him. The support included a fellowship, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency assistance.

The financial assistance helped him continue his research work, manage academic expenses and focus on achieving his academic and career goals without a major financial burden. It reduced the financial stress associated with pursuing advanced research.

With greater financial security, Shubhankar was able to continue his Ph.D. research smoothly that improved his academic progress and enabled him to devote greater attention to developing his research skills.

The fellowship also gave him confidence and strengthened his professional opportunities for future career growth. It enabled him to pursue his academic goals while working towards a more secure professional future.

Shubhankar has now completed his Ph.D. His achievement reflects how sustained fellowship assistance can help scholars overcome economic pressures and continue higher education without compromising their academic aspirations.

The NFSC Scheme not only reduced the financial burden during his Ph.D. journey but also supported his academic and personal development. The assistance helped transform a difficult journey marked by limited resources into one of confidence, progress and achievement.

Shubhankar Ghorai’s journey demonstrates how inclusive educational support can enable scholars from financially constrained backgrounds to overcome barriers. His experience highlights the importance of fellowship assistance in expanding access to higher education and strengthening research capabilities.

Through determination and timely support under the NFSC Scheme, Shubhankar progressed from facing financial difficulties and limited educational resources to successfully completing his Ph.D. His journey stands as an example of how educational empowerment can create meaningful academic, professional and personal change.

2302837.title: Chairman of the Railway Board Reviews IRCTC War Room; Directs Strengthening of Passenger Feedback and Kitchen Monitoring Systems to Improve the Quality of Catering Services
2302837.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Chairman of the Railway Board Reviews IRCTC War Room; Directs Strengthening of Passenger Feedback and Kitchen Monitoring Systems to Improve the Quality of Catering Services
Focus on Real-time Kitchen Surveillance, Effective Inspections, Prompt Action on Deficiencies and Closer Monitoring of Rail Madad Complaints
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi

Chairman  and Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Railway Board (Ministry of Railways), Sh. Satish Kumar reviewed the functioning of the IRCTC War Room at the IRCTC office yesterday, with a focus on strengthening the systems for passenger feedback, kitchen monitoring and quality assurance in catering services.

During the review, the Chairman of the Railway Board (CRB) interacted with the dedicated team for monitoring and feedback-related activities. He emphasized on strengthening the existing systems to make monitoring more responsive, technology-driven and outcome-oriented.

Sh. Satish Kumar directed that the Rail Madad interface should be further automated to enable passengers to communicate with the concerned system in a simple and convenient manner through a single click. Closer monitoring of Rail Madad complaints was also emphasized, including direct interaction with passengers wherever required, so that passenger concerns can be understood and resolved more effectively.

To strengthen accountability of inspecting agencies, the CRB directed that each inspecting agency should systematically post details of deficiencies observed as well as performance during inspections, enabling their work to be continuously monitored and evaluated.

Strengthening Real-time Kitchen Monitoring

The review also focused on expanding camera-based monitoring of railway catering kitchens. At present, four camera feeds are available for monitoring kitchen operations. The CRB directed that additional cameras be provided in raw material storage areas, along with a PTZ (Pan-Tilt-Zoom) camera, to enable wider and more effective surveillance of kitchen activities.

The camera-based monitoring system is also being used to assess the condition and functioning of kitchens. Where poor conditions are observed, appropriate notice and corrective action are to be initiated. During the review, a kitchen at Anantapur in South Central Railway was noted to require improvement based on inspection and video monitoring.

Particular emphasis was placed on the preparation of roti and paratha, identified as an area requiring focused review. The CRB directed that the entire process of roti and paratha preparation be comprehensively reviewed to identify gaps and ensure consistent quality.

Stronger Third-Party Inspections and Deterrent Action

Sh. Satish Kumar also reviewed the role of third-party inspection agencies in maintaining catering standards. While third-party inspection arrangements are available at several locations, emphasis was placed on ensuring that inspections are effective, meaningful and outcome-oriented. Agencies whose performance is found to be consistently ineffective should be reviewed for appropriate action, including delisting wherever warranted, to ensure that inspection mechanisms deliver the intended quality assurance.

The use of Artificial Intelligence-based monitoring and detection systems was also discussed. The CRB directed that AI-based alerts relating to issues such as rodents, cockroaches and other deficiencies should not remain limited to detection. Such instances should be followed by appropriate warning letters and deterrent action, ensuring that identified deficiencies result in timely corrective measures.

The review underscored the need for more effective inspections, stronger technology-enabled monitoring and prompt follow-up action to continuously improve the quality of railway catering services. The initiatives are aimed at strengthening passenger confidence, improving food quality and hygiene standards, and ensuring a more responsive and passenger-centric catering ecosystem across Indian Railways.

*****

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma

2302819.title: Students are the future of the largest democracy in the world: CEC Gyanesh Kumar
2302819.body_html:
Election Commission
Students are the future of the largest democracy in the world: CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi
  1. The Election Commission of India (ECI) organised the second regional conference on “Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC 2.0) and ECINET” in Lucknow today. The conference focuses on strengthening electoral literacy and democratic awareness among young citizens through educational institutions.
  2. Addressing the participants comprising students and teachers from schools and colleges across Uttar Pradesh, describing students as the future of the nation, CEC Gyanesh Kumar said the ELCs are imperative to carry forth the knowledge and the understanding of electoral processes and enrich democracy.
  3. CEC Gyanesh Kumar stated how elections in India are held strictly as per the constitution of India, law and instructions issued by ECI and is conducted transparently under the concurrent audit of political parties, candidates or their representatives at all stages. He underlined the need for students and young electors to familiarise students and young electors with India’s electoral system, democratic values, electoral registration, polling and counting processes, and the role and functioning of the Election Commission of India.
  4. Emphasising the importance of engaging young citizens, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar stated that their trust and informed participation in the electoral process is an investment in the future of democracy.
  5. ELC 2.0, with the tagline, “Learn Democracy. Lead Democracy.”, reinforces the objective of encouraging young and first-time voters not only to understand democracy but also to participate meaningfully and contribute to its progress.
  6. Earlier in the day Shri Gyanesh Kumar visited his alma mater, Colvin Taluqdar’s College and interacted with the teachers and students at the school. Tomorrow, the second day of the visit, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar will hold an interaction with Booth Level Officers (BLOs) of Uttar Pradesh.
  7. ELC 2.0 reimagines Electoral Literacy Clubs as structured, visible and digitally enabled platforms across schools, colleges and universities. The initiative envisages continuous, year-round activities to promote electoral literacy among young citizens and electoral awareness within their families, educational institutions and communities.
  8. ELC 2.0 will leverage the extensive ECINet digital platform which provides all election related services from roll to poll at the click of a button. A streamlined pan-India network of ELCs will be cultivated using a dedicated ELC portal on ECINet.
  9. The initiative assumes significance in view of India’s extensive educational ecosystem, comprising approximately 15 lakh schools with nearly 25 crore students and over one crore teachers. The higher education sector comprises nearly 1,500 universities and around 70,000 educational institutions, with an estimated enrolment of 4.33 crore students.
  10. Through this extensive institutional network, ELC 2.0 seeks to promote factual and experiential electoral education, enhance awareness about the transparency, integrity and credibility of India’s electoral system, and encourage young citizens to become ambassadors of informed democratic participation.
  11. The ELCs will also serve as platforms for disseminating information about different stages of the electoral process, including electoral registration, polling and counting, along with the ECINET App and other key initiatives of the Election Commission of India.

2302816.title: The Fifth Space – Where Education Meets Responsibility
2302816.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
The Fifth Space – Where Education Meets Responsibility
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Interacts with School Students on Education, Digital Responsibility and Human Dignity
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 6:17PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Social Justice & Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar today emphasized the importance of listening to the younger generation, understanding their concerns and creating an environment where they feel comfortable sharing their thoughts and challenges.

Addressing the school students at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC) during the programme “The Fifth Space – Where Education Meets Responsibility”, in the National Capital here today, Dr Kumar underlined that the rapidly changing digital environment requires parents, teachers and institutions to engage with young people with understanding rather than simply criticizing their use of technology.

The programme was organised by the National Commission for Women (NCW) in collaboration with DAIC, UNESCO New Delhi and Mount Abu Public School.

Dr. Virendra Kumar emphasised the importance of maintaining strong emotional connections between students, parents and teachers, enabling young people to seek guidance and support when facing difficulties.

The Minister also underscored the importance of recognizing the individual strengths, aspirations and needs of every child. He stressed the need to move from Vision To Insight (Drishti Se Antardrishti Ki Aur) — from merely seeing things to understanding them deeply and meaningfully

Dr Kumar spoke about the concept of the “Fifth Space”, which represents the convergence of home, school, culture, society, citizenship, knowledge and the digital world. He stressed that technology must be accompanied by ethics, responsibility and sound judgement, particularly among young people growing up in an increasingly digital environment.

The interaction provided students an opportunity to raise questions and share their perspectives directly with the Union Minister. The Minister encouraged the students to remain curious, responsible and conscious of their role in shaping the future of the country.

The programme also witnessed deliberations on child rights, safety, gender equality, human dignity, digital responsibility and responsible citizenship by distinguished speakers including Dr. Sanjeev Sharma, Member Secretary, National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR); Dr. Jyoti Arora, Principal, Mount Abu Public School and Vijaya Kishore Rahat, Chairperson, National Commission for Women.

The interaction between the Union Minister and the students highlighted the importance of bridging the generational gap through dialogue, empathy and mutual understanding, while ensuring that education prepares young people not only for academic success but also for responsible and dignified citizenship.

2302791.title: Mauritius Minister of Public Service and Administrative Reforms, Lutchmanah Raj Pentiah, calls on Minister Dr Jitendra Singh; discusses further strengthening of India-Mauritius cooperation in public service, training and capacity building
2302791.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2302791.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Mauritius Minister of Public Service and Administrative Reforms, Lutchmanah Raj Pentiah, calls on Minister Dr Jitendra Singh; discusses further strengthening of India-Mauritius cooperation in public service, training and capacity building
India and Mauritius share a special relationship rooted in deep historical, cultural and people-to-people ties, public administration and capacity building provide a natural area for further cooperation: Dr Jitendra Singh
Dr Jitendra Singh also discusses India’s experience under Mission Karmayogi in moving towards continuous, role-based and competency-driven learning for public servants
India, Mauritius Explore Expanded Cooperation in Public Administration; Dr. Jitendra Singh Discusses Strengthening of ABVIPSI-India Institutional Linkages
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

Minister of Public Service and Administrative Reforms, Republic of Mauritius, Mr. Lutchmanah Raj Pentiah, called on Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today at Kartavya Bhavan, accompanied by a high level official delegation, with the agenda to discuss further strengthening of India-Mauritius cooperation in public service, training and capacity building, with greater emphasis on sustained institutional engagement and exchange of expertise between the two countries.

Dr Jitendra Singh said the existing cooperation should be taken forward through wider training opportunities, stronger linkages between public service institutions and greater sharing of India’s experience in governance, administrative reforms and technology-enabled public service delivery.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India and Mauritius share a special relationship rooted in deep historical, cultural and people-to-people ties, and public administration and capacity building provide a natural area for further cooperation. He said India has consistently supported Mauritius in developing the capabilities of its public servants and that the ongoing engagement now provides an opportunity to build a more structured and enduring institutional partnership.

The Minister referred to the understanding reached during Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s visit to Mauritius last year to train 500 Mauritian civil servants over five years through the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG), with the first batch already undergoing training at Mussoorie. He said this initiative can serve as an important foundation for deeper and sustained engagement between the public services of India and Mauritius, beyond individual training programmes.

A major focus of the meeting was the development of stronger institutional linkages between ABVIPSI and leading Indian institutions engaged in public service training and capacity building, including the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA), Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA) and Institute of Secretariat Training & Management (ISTM). The proposed areas include joint programme design, faculty and training capacity building, exchange of expertise, exposure programmes, sharing of training methodologies, development of case studies and joint research.

He said the recently operationalised iGOT Karmayogi Mauritius platform can provide a strong foundation for sustained digital learning and capacity building of Mauritian public servants. Indian and Mauritian institutions can work together to develop learning pathways, curate content and incorporate Mauritian governance experiences and case studies into learning resources suited to the country’s requirements.

The meeting was attended by senior officials from the Government of India and the Republic of Mauritius, representatives of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Public Service and Innovation (ABVIPSI), and High Commissioner of Mauritius to India, H.E. Mrs. Sheila Bappoo. The discussions focused on expanding cooperation in public administration, capacity building, training, digital learning and public service innovation.

The meeting also explored the scope for expanding cooperation from conventional civil service training to wider areas of professional capacity building. IIPA has proposed collaboration with ABVIPSI for short- and long-term programmes in public administration, governance, leadership and public policy, besides capacity building of ABVIPSI faculty and staff and training programmes for scientific and technical officials from Mauritius.

IIPA has also proposed cooperation in joint research and consultancy, Monitoring and Evaluation of government schemes and projects, faculty and researcher capacity building, development of online training courses and modules, and faculty and staff exchanges. LBSNAA has proposed opportunities for Mauritian civil servants to participate in suitable mid-career and in-service training programmes and for joint design of programmes aligned with the capacity-building requirements of Mauritius.

Mr. Lutchmanah Raj Pentiah welcomed India’s continued support to Mauritius and sought further expansion of institutional cooperation. He proposed that NCGG teams visit Mauritius to train trainers and Mauritian public servants and to support more effective utilisation of the Karmayogi Bharat platform. He said 85 Mauritian officers have already undergone training through four missions and expressed readiness on the Mauritian side to facilitate further training programmes in Mauritius.

The Mauritian Minister also sought India’s continued support in developing ABVIPSI as a centre of excellence for public service learning and innovation for the Indian Ocean and Eastern African region. He invited Indian institutions to participate in an international conference on good governance and management proposed by Mauritius and sought deeper academic and institutional linkages with Indian institutions.

The two sides also discussed opportunities for cooperation in emerging areas relevant to both countries, including the Blue Economy, ocean technologies, fisheries, desalination and sustainable development. Specialised capacity-building programmes, practitioner exchanges and joint learning initiatives in these areas can create new avenues for India-Mauritius cooperation.

The discussions reaffirmed the shared commitment to take India-Mauritius cooperation in public administration and capacity building to a new level through stronger institutional partnerships and sustained training engagement. The partnership will build upon the 500-officer training programme, ABVIPSI, iGOT Karmayogi Mauritius and the emerging linkages between Mauritian and Indian training institutions, with the focus on building long-term public service capabilities and creating a framework for continuous exchange of knowledge, experience and best practices.

2302789.title: CHEMCONNECT 2026: Industry-Academia Event will be held Tomorrow at IIT, MADRAS
2302789.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
2302789.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
CHEMCONNECT 2026: Industry-Academia Event will be held Tomorrow at IIT, MADRAS
Technologies and Patents from the Centres of Excellence to be Showcased for Commercialization
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 5:42PM by PIB Delhi

CHEMCONNECT 2026, a one-day Industry-Academia Event, will be held Tomorrow, at the Student Activity Centre (SAC) Hall, IIT Madras.

The event is jointly organized by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers and the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras in order to facilitate 18 CoE established by the Department.

The event is being organised by the Centre of Excellence in Biodegradable Packaging Materials (CoE BioPack), and Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Madras in collaboration with CIPET.

The event serves as an inventors-and-industry meet designed to facilitate direct dialogue without intermediaries. The event brings DCPC’s Centres of Excellence together with companies ready to commercialize innovations, offering a structured platform for industry leaders, start-ups, MSMEs, researchers, policymakers, incubators, and investors seeking strategic partnerships.

During the event, technologies, prototypes, and patents from Centres of Excellence established under the DCPC scheme "Setting up of Centres of Excellence (CoE) in the field of Chemicals and Petrochemicals" will be showcased.

Principal Investigators from CoEs will exhibit their work at dedicated stalls and interact directly with industry representatives to explore opportunities for collaboration, licensing, and technology transfer.

2302766.title: Third Meeting of India-Cambodia Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment (JWGTI) Held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia
2302766.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Third Meeting of India-Cambodia Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment (JWGTI) Held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia
India-Cambodia Bilateral Trade Grows Over 36% to USD 406.78 Million in 2025-26
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 5:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Third Meeting of the India-Cambodia Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment (JWGTI) was held on 24 August 2026 in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Amit Verma, Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India, and Mr. Long Kemvichet, Director General of International Trade, Ministry of Commerce, Cambodia.

Both sides noted the encouraging momentum in bilateral trade, which grew by over 36% to reach USD 406.78 million in 2025-26, up from USD 299 million in the previous financial year, with the April-June 2026 quarter recording a further 63.25% year-on-year growth. Cambodia is currently India's 8th largest trading partner in ASEAN, accounting for 0.31% of India's total trade with the bloc, reflecting significant headroom for growth.

The meeting deliberated upon ways to diversify and deepen trade, including through cooperation and collaboration in traditional medicine, e-governance modules, recognition of Indian pharmacopeia, trade statistics reconciliation and the sharing of information on flagship trade fairs and business delegations.

The meeting also welcomed the successful launch of UPI acceptance at KHQR-enabled merchants in Phnom Penh on 2 June 2026, and discussed the next phase of enabling Cambodian payment applications to scan UPI QR codes in India, which would allow Cambodian travellers to use UPI-enabled terminals in India seamlessly.

The meeting further welcomed the agreement between both sides on the MoU on Custom Cooperation and discussed early signing, which would bring uniformity in custom procedure.

The two sides further discussed cooperation in agriculture and market access issues, expanding trade in dyes and pigments, banking and insurance sector cooperation. The two sides also welcomed the discussion for completion of the Bilateral Investment Treaty between India and Cambodia and agreed for early signature on it.

This was the third meeting of the JWGTI since its institutionalisation and the meeting reaffirmed the depth and growing potential of the India-Cambodia trade and economic partnership. The next meeting of the JWGTI will be held in India in 2027.

On the sidelines of the 3rd India–Cambodia JWGTI meeting, Shri Amit Verma had a productive call with H.E. Tith Rithipol, Under Secretary of State, Cambodia. Discussions covered strengthening bilateral trade and investment, cooperation in pharmaceuticals, and the successful UPI–KHQR digital payments linkage. Both sides reiterated their shared commitment for deepening the partnership between the countries.

Shri Amit Verma also met with members of the Indian Business Chamber in Cambodia (IBCC). Discussions focused on accelerating bilateral trade agreement discussions, facilitating Indian investment in Cambodia, and identifying 5–7 priority sectors including education, healthcare, IT, agriculture and tourism.

The meeting also discussed an “Invest in Cambodia” roadshow in India, positioning Cambodia as a production base for Indian companies seeking access to ASEAN markets, and establishing a mechanism for IBCC/FICCI/JBC to provide private-sector feedback to the JWGTI.

***

Abhishek Dayal/Garima Singh

2302702.title: “Khelo India Dialogue – Khel Ki Baat, PM Modi Ke Saath” to be Organised Nationwide on 27th August 2026 to celebrate National Sports Day
2302702.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2302702.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
 “Khelo India Dialogue – Khel Ki Baat, PM Modi Ke Saath” to be Organised Nationwide on 27th August 2026 to celebrate National Sports Day
Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Address Young Budding Athletes on Sports, Youth Leadership and Viksit Bharat
Dialogue to bring Youth, Athletes and Policymakers Together Across 1,500+ Educational Institutions
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi

To celebrate the National Sports Day 2026, the nation is set to witness a large-scale youth engagement initiative, “Khelo India Dialogue – Khel Ki Baat, Pradhan Mantri Modi Ke Saath”, on 27 August 2026, bringing together young people, athletes and educational institutions at more than 1,500 locations across the country.

The nationwide initiative will create a direct platform for young budding athletes to share their ideas, suggestions and innovative thoughts on the future of India’s sports and youth ecosystem. IITs, IIMs, NITs, AIIMS, leading medical colleges and universities will be among the educational institutions participating in the programme.

The programme will feature a virtual address by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Following the Prime Minister’s address, physical programmes will commence simultaneously across the participating locations.

The programme seeks to strengthen the connection between the aspirations and ground-level experiences of young people and policymaking. Youth participants will engage around four key themes: strengthening the sports ecosystem and expanding grassroots facilities, coaching and opportunities; nurturing talent for the 2036 Olympics through scientific talent identification and athlete development; enhancing youth leadership and participation in governance; and empowering young people with future-ready skills, volunteering and nation-building opportunities.

A major feature of the initiative will be direct interaction between youth having interest in sports and leading Indian athletes and medal winners. Prominent sportspersons including Deepa Karmakar, Saina Nehwal, Gagan Narang, Sreejesh, Mary Kom, Baichung Bhutia, Gopichand, Anju Bobby George, Karnam Malleswari, Mirabai Chanu and P.T. Usha, along with prominent cricketers, will engage with youth and share their sporting journeys, challenges, and experiences.

The participation will extend beyond athletes, with Members of Parliament, Members of Legislative Assemblies, Union Ministers, Ministers of State and State Sports Ministers engaging with young people and seeking their ideas and suggestions on the four identified themes.

The initiative will also feature the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue Quiz and encourage young participants to register on the MY Bharat Portal, creating an avenue for sustained youth engagement beyond the one-day programme.

“Khelo India Dialogue – Khel Ki Baat, Pradhan Mantri Modi Ke Saath” seeks to reinforce the idea that India’s sporting transformation is ultimately powered by its young people. By bringing youth aspirations, sporting experiences and policy perspectives onto a common platform, the initiative aims to give youth a meaningful voice in shaping the future of sports and youth development in the country.


*****

Pawan Singh Faujdar / Ayushman Kumar
